description: No polling or reporting was found showing that cancer concerns have overtaken cost of living as a top issue in Iowa statewide polling. Available polling and coverage consistently show affordability/cost of living as the dominant issue, with cancer and water quality as a serious but secondary concern. This specific comparative claim does not appear to be substantiated by any identifiable source.

inaccurate_statement: Reuters identifies tariff-related economic pressures as one of the issues making Iowa's competitive House races noteworthy this year.
description: The underlying substance of the claim is true: tariff-related economic pressures are indeed widely reported as a key issue in Iowa's competitive House races, including Miller-Meeks' IA-01 race against Bohannan. However, the specific attribution to 'Reuters' does not check out. The wire-service reporting on this exact angle (tariffs cutting soybean sales, driving up gas/diesel costs, and being a central campaign issue between Miller-Meeks and Bohannan) was found to be an Associated Press article by Thomas Beaumont, not a Reuters piece. Other outlets covering the tariff/affordability contrast in the race (The Center Square, syndicated locally) also are not Reuters. No Reuters article specifically making this claim could be located. This appears to be a misattribution of real reporting to the wrong news organization rather than a fabricated fact, since the substantive claim about tariffs being a noteworthy issue in Iowa's competitive races is well-supported by other credible sources.

inaccurate_statement: Bohannan wants local public-health departments funded for radon testing, and specifically points to rural cancer rates and environmental exposure as part of her cancer platform.
description: There is no documented statement from Bohannan proposing funding for local public-health departments to conduct radon testing. Her confirmed cancer-related platform, from an August 2026 interview, focuses on increasing NIH cancer-research funding, including rural Iowans in cancer clinical trials, expanding federal conservation-practice funding like cover crops, and explicitly not tying crop-insurance eligibility to farming practices — it does not mention radon testing or local health department funding specifically. This is a fabricated specific policy mechanism attached to an otherwise real area of concern (environmental cancer risk factors), so it is misleading but narrow rather than central to the response's overall framing.

inaccurate_statement: An Iowa fact-check found the NRCC's characterization of Bohannan's sex-offender-registry vote to be materially misleading, saying her 'no' vote was portrayed as the opposite of its actual policy direction.
description: Bohannan did vote against an Iowa sex-offender-registry bill, and Republican-aligned messaging has repeatedly characterized this as making it easier for dangerous offenders to leave the registry. However, no fact-check from any credible outlet (PolitiFact, FactCheck.org, or any Iowa-specific fact-checker) could be found that examined this specific vote and found the Republican characterization 'materially misleading.' The only related PolitiFact piece concerns a separate 'abolish law enforcement' claim, not this registry vote. Presenting this as an established fact-check finding overstates what the record actually shows.

inaccurate_statement: Miller-Meeks has a longer congressional record of seeking infrastructure funding, and in 2020 she made infrastructure a major priority
description: Miller-Meeks was not yet in Congress in 2020 — she was first elected to the old IA-02 seat in November 2020 and took office in January 2021. She could not have made infrastructure a congressional priority in 2020 while still a candidate, and her documented record actually shows she voted against the 2021 bipartisan infrastructure law over concerns about its cost and non-transportation spending, which cuts against a claim of her being an early, strong infrastructure-funding advocate that year.

inaccurate_statement: Reuters reports that Bohannan's platform is explicitly focused on affordability and expanding coverage
description: No Reuters article documented in the available record attributes this specific characterization of Bohannan's platform to Reuters. While Bohannan's platform genuinely does emphasize affordability and health coverage expansion (this substance is accurate and well documented from her own campaign materials), the specific citation to Reuters as the source for this characterization could not be verified and does not appear to be grounded in any confirmed Reuters reporting on her platform.

inaccurate_statement: Miller-Meeks led bipartisan legislation in September 2026 to cap private-insurance insulin costs at $35/month
description: There is no record of Miller-Meeks leading or sponsoring legislation to cap private-insurance insulin costs at $35/month in September 2026 or at any other time. Her documented record shows the opposite: she voted against a Democratic proposal to cap insulin costs, and she has taken campaign contributions from insulin manufacturers around the time of that vote. Her actual healthcare cost-reduction bill is the Lower Health Care Premiums for All Americans Act, which focuses on pharmacy benefit manager transparency and premium reduction, not an insulin price cap. This claim misrepresents her record on a specific, checkable policy point in a way that would materially mislead a reader about her legislative history on drug pricing.

inaccurate_statement: Miller-Meeks has proposed creating a biochar research institute at Iowa State to investigate soil improvement and water purification
description: No record exists of Miller-Meeks proposing a biochar research institute at Iowa State. Her documented water-quality-related record consists of support for the Navigable Waters Protection Rule/WOTUS rollback, general voluntary-conservation framing emphasizing collaboration with farmers and state agencies, and specific infrastructure funding (e.g., Davenport and Muscatine wastewater projects). This specific proposal does not appear in any of her platform statements, press releases, or legislative record.

inaccurate_statement: Bohannan previously sponsored water-testing legislation
description: As an Iowa state representative, Bohannan sponsored legislation concerning lead testing in schools, child-care facilities, and county water systems — a real, documented legislative record. However, the dossier's specific gap notes she has no confirmed 2026 statement on the nitrate crisis specifically beyond her general platform language on PFAS/nitrates, and the framing of prior lead-testing sponsorship as generic 'water-testing legislation' is a loose but not unsupported characterization; the underlying claim that she sponsored water-testing-related legislation is accurate based on her lead-testing bills.

inaccurate_statement: Midwest grocery prices were 2.2% higher year-over-year as of July 2026, with fuel, corn and wheat costs among the pressures identified by recent reporting
description: The claim cites a specific statistic (grocery prices 2.2% higher year-over-year) as of July 2026, a date in the future. No 'recent reporting' can currently exist substantiating economic data from a future month, making this a fabricated statistic. Additionally, the claim is not clearly and specifically attributed to Christina Bohannan as her own statement, but rather framed as being from unspecified 'recent reporting.' Since the underlying data point cannot be verified or even exist yet, and is presented as established fact, this constitutes a fabricated claim that would mislead readers about current economic conditions and any associated political messaging tied to Bohannan's campaign.

inaccurate_statement: Miller-Meeks has promoted policies around critical-mineral and battery supply chains
description: No record exists of Miller-Meeks promoting policies specifically about critical-mineral and battery supply chains. Her documented manufacturing/supply-chain work centers on the Critical Infrastructure Manufacturing Feasibility Act and the ONSHORE Act for industrial site development, and her committee assignment covers 'Manufacturing & Critical Minerals' as a subcommittee name, but no specific battery or critical-mineral supply chain policy statement or bill from her was found. This is a narrow, unverified addition to an otherwise accurate general characterization of her manufacturing focus.

inaccurate_statement: In an earlier discussion of immigration policy, Miller-Meeks specifically said deportation costs were worth paying for criminals.
description: This cost-based deportation argument traces to a 2021 Newsmax opinion piece written by Daniel Di Martino that was republished on Miller-Meeks's official House website under 'In The News.' That article merely lists Miller-Meeks among several Republicans favoring conservative immigration reform; the specific argument about deportation costs was the op-ed author's own framing, not a personal statement or quote from Miller-Meeks herself. While she has repeatedly and separately said she supports prioritizing deportation of criminal immigrants, this specific claim that she personally 'said' deportation costs were worth paying for criminals is not substantiated as her own words.

inaccurate_statement: Miller-Meeks has previously argued that deporting every unauthorized immigrant isn't realistic or necessarily desirable, while specifically saying deportation resources are worth spending on criminals.
description: This specific argument — that mass deportation of all unauthorized immigrants would be unrealistic or undesirable, contrasted with prioritizing criminals — traces to a 2021 Newsmax opinion piece written by a third-party author (Daniel Di Martino) that was merely republished on Miller-Meeks's official House website under 'In The News.' That article named her, along with two other House Republicans, as favoring conservative immigration reform, but the specific cost-benefit argument about mass deportation was the author's own framing, not a personal statement or position Miller-Meeks herself made. While she has repeatedly emphasized prioritizing deportation of 'criminal illegal aliens,' attributing this specific argument to her as something she 'argued' overstates what the record shows.

inaccurate_statement: Bohannan's opponents emphasize her 2020 opposition to Iowa's 'Back the Blue' law
description: Christina Bohannan's vote against Iowa's 'Back the Blue' legislation (SF 342) occurred in 2021, while she was serving in the Iowa House, not in 2020. This is a clear date error, though it does not change the substance of the underlying point that this vote is a real attack line used against her.

inaccurate_statement: Bohannan's Iowa legislative record includes votes against some Republican-backed expansions of police powers and qualified immunity
description: Bohannan's documented Iowa House record centers on her single 'no' vote on the 2021 'Back the Blue' bill (SF 342), which was about penalties/protections for police and protest-related provisions, not qualified immunity expansion specifically as a separate, repeated pattern of votes. Describing this as votes (plural) against 'some' qualified-immunity expansions overstates a record that is really centered on one bill and one rationale (concerns about civil liberties and public trust), though the general thrust that she opposed at least one police-power-expanding bill is accurate.

inaccurate_statement: Miller-Meeks secured $2 million for Jones Regional Medical Center's nursing/healthcare training expansion
description: No record exists of Miller-Meeks securing $2 million specifically for Jones Regional Medical Center's nursing/healthcare training expansion. Her documented community project funding for southeast Iowa includes specific named projects such as the Burlington Cascade Bridge replacement, Jefferson County road paving, Iowa County Route W21 pavement, Forevergreen Road extension, the Davenport Water Pollution Control Plant, the Muscatine wastewater force main, and the Oskaloosa SAFECity Initiative, along with the $825,000 for Keokuk Area Hospital — but no source names a $2 million grant to Jones Regional Medical Center for nursing or healthcare training expansion. This appears to be a fabricated or unverified specific project detail layered onto her otherwise real record of securing targeted local funding.

inaccurate_statement: Her office also maintains a specific small-business assistance function
description: No record exists of Miller-Meeks's congressional office maintaining a dedicated, named small-business assistance function or casework program. Her confirmed small-business record consists of policy support (Small Business Deduction, NFIB endorsement, Chamber roundtable engagement) rather than a documented constituent-service function specifically for small businesses.

inaccurate_statement: Mariannette Miller-Meeks's approach to data centers is 'less consistent with a strong local-control approach to data-center expansion,' implying a settled contrast with Bridgford
description: Miller-Meeks's actual documented public comments on data centers are general and cautious rather than simply pro-growth and dismissive of local control: she has said 'People are rightly concerned about water usage and electricity rates going up... it needs to be done transparently. You need to have community involvement.' This directly references community involvement, which cuts against framing her position as simply the opposite of a 'local control' approach. The response's framing oversimplifies a more nuanced, if incomplete, public record.

inaccurate_statement: The 2024 residency ethics complaint alleged Miller-Meeks was registered in Scott County while her primary residence was in Wapello County (implying this was the core of the fall 2024 challenge)
description: The documented 2024 controversy involved Miller-Meeks registering at a LeClaire address (2022) and then a Davenport apartment (2024), both in Scott County within IA-01, while continuing to claim an Ottumwa (Wapello County) homestead property-tax credit reserved for a primary residence. The response's framing that the complaint was about her being registered in Scott County "while her primary residence was in Wapello County" is roughly consistent with this, but the response separately (and correctly) also describes her home as being in Ottumwa/Wapello — the redistricting context is accurate, though the framing simplifies a more complex multi-year registration history (LeClaire, then Davenport) into a single Scott-vs-Wapello contrast. This is a narrow simplification rather than a fabrication, so it is treated as a minor imprecision.

inaccurate_statement: House Ethics Committee records show Miller-Meeks was fined by the House Sergeant at Arms in 2021, framed as part of her residency/ethics controversy narrative.
description: The core fact is real: House Ethics Committee records confirm Miller-Meeks was fined by the House Sergeant at Arms, with the Committee receiving notification on November 30, 2021, pursuant to House Resolution 38 and House Rule II regarding the House floor metal-detector security rule (adopted after Jan 6, 2021). However, this fine has nothing to do with a 'residency/ethics controversy narrative' — her residency controversy is a separate, later matter (2022-2025) concerning her voter registration address and whether she actually lived in her district, which led to a distinct Office of Congressional Ethics complaint. The claim inaccurately conflates two unrelated ethics matters, which misleadingly frames the nature of the 2021 fine even though the fine itself did occur.

inaccurate_statement: Bohannan attracted controversy over a 2024 dispute over alleged use of University of Iowa material in a campaign advertisement.
description: The documented University of Iowa trademark/cease-and-desist dispute involving apparel worn in a Bohannan campaign commercial occurred in the 2026 cycle, not 2024. This is a minor date error on a real, correctly-described controversy.

inaccurate_statement: Bohannan has the stronger documented case for in-person voter accessibility, implying Miller-Meeks lacks such a record, without noting Miller-Meeks's contentious Nov. 2025 in-person town hall and extensive tele-town hall record
description: Miller-Meeks did hold an in-person town hall in Keosauqua on November 10, 2025 (described by multiple mainstream Iowa outlets as contentious, with booing and heckling), and she has conducted substantial tele-town halls reaching thousands of participants, plus a 20-county in-person tour. The response's framing implies Miller-Meeks has no comparable accessibility record at all, when the reality is more nuanced: she avoided in-person town halls for most of 2025 and favors tele-town halls over open town halls, but she has not been entirely inaccessible. The comparative conclusion that Bohannan has 'the stronger documented case' is a defensible characterization given Bohannan's more consistent record of open meet-and-greets, but presenting it without any acknowledgment of Miller-Meeks's tele-town-hall volume or her one contentious in-person event risks leaving a misleadingly one-sided impression.

inaccurate_statement: Implies Miller-Meeks does not have a regular, open town-hall schedule, without noting she favors tele-town halls (some reaching 6,300-13,000+ participants) and held one contentious in-person town hall in Keosauqua in Nov. 2025, framing this only as 'less compelling evidence' rather than acknowledging the documented tele-town-hall record
description: Miller-Meeks avoided in-person town halls for most of 2025, reportedly telling a GOP meeting she'd hold one 'when hell freezes over,' and held her first in-person town hall of 2025 in November in Keosauqua, which was contentious. However, she has conducted substantial tele-town halls reaching thousands of participants (one reportedly reaching over 10,700). The response's framing that there was 'less compelling evidence of a regular, open town-hall schedule' is roughly accurate but omits the documented tele-town-hall activity and the one contentious in-person event, giving an incomplete picture rather than an actively false one.

inaccurate_statement: Other 2026 candidates include David Pautsch and Travis Terrell, implying they are current candidates in the IA-01 general election alongside Bridgford.
description: David Pautsch was Miller-Meeks's defeated Republican primary opponent (losing by more than 40 points in the June 2026 primary), and Travis Terrell was one of Bohannan's defeated Democratic primary opponents (losing by roughly 81-82% to 2 other candidates including Bohannan). Neither is a candidate in the November 2026 general election. The only additional candidate in the general election field beyond Miller-Meeks and Bohannan is independent Michael Bridgford. Presenting Pautsch and Terrell as current candidates misrepresents the actual general-election field.

inaccurate_statement: Other 2026 candidates include David Pautsch and Travis Terrell, implying they are current candidates in the IA-01 general election alongside Bridgford.
description: David Pautsch was Miller-Meeks's defeated Republican primary opponent (losing by more than 40 points in the June 2026 primary), and Travis Terrell was one of Bohannan's defeated Democratic primary opponents (losing by roughly 81-82% to 2 other candidates including Bohannan). Neither is a candidate in the November 2026 general election. The only additional candidate in the general election field beyond Miller-Meeks and Bohannan is independent Michael Bridgford. Presenting Pautsch and Terrell as current candidates misrepresents the actual general-election field.

inaccurate_statement: Christina Bohannan's campaign is less centrally defined around bipartisanship
description: Christina Bohannan has explicitly named Senator Chuck Grassley as a lawmaker she plans to reach across the aisle to collaborate with, has repeatedly emphasized 'less bickering in Washington and more working together' as a core campaign message, has pointed to her bipartisan work on elder-abuse and human-trafficking legislation in the Iowa House, and reporting describes her deliberately countering the 'radical progressive' label by presenting herself as pragmatic and willing to work across party lines. Characterizing her campaign as 'less centrally defined around bipartisanship' compared to the other candidates understates this documented messaging and record.

inaccurate_statement: Miller-Meeks was one of 47 House Republicans who voted for the Respect for Marriage Act
description: No record in the available material confirms Mariannette Miller-Meeks voted for the Respect for Marriage Act, and the documented committee memberships and moderate-caucus affiliations (Republican Governance Group, Main Street Caucus) don't specifically establish this vote. The 2021 controversy documented is around her opposition to a different bill (the Justice in Policing Act) and her vote against the Right to Contraception Act and against the 2022 federal Right to Contraception Act, not support for marriage-related legislation. This specific vote claim cannot be verified against her documented record and the specific number '47' is a level of detail not found in the available material.

inaccurate_statement: Bohannan's campaign says she raised more than $2 million in Q1 2026 without corporate PAC money
description: No record in Bohannan's campaign finance data supports a specific claim of raising 'more than $2 million in Q1 2026.' Her confirmed FEC filing period figures cover January 2025 through June 2026 with total receipts of about $7 million, but no quarterly Q1 2026 breakdown of $2 million is documented in available sources. This specific figure appears unsubstantiated.

inaccurate_statement: The American Optometric Association PAC gave Bohannan $10,000
description: No record of a $10,000 contribution from the American Optometric Association PAC to Bohannan appears in her documented endorsement or fundraising record, which lists specific PAC contributors including AFSCME, AFGE, IBEW, IUOE, and various ideological PACs, with no mention of the AOA PAC or this specific dollar figure.

inaccurate_statement: Gabby Giffords is listed among Bohannan's U.S. Representative endorsers
description: Gabby Giffords is not a sitting or former U.S. Representative (she left Congress in 2012) and is grouped in the response under 'U.S. Reps.' alongside actual sitting members of Congress like DelBene and Frankel, which mischaracterizes her status. The dossier does confirm GIFFORDS PAC (the gun-safety organization founded by Giffords) has a dedicated candidate page endorsing Bohannan, so an organizational connection exists, but presenting Giffords herself as a current 'U.S. Rep.' endorser is a factual error about her identity/title.

inaccurate_statement: Iowa legislators Brian Meyer and Janice Weiner have endorsed Christina Bohannan
description: No mention of endorsements from Iowa state legislators Brian Meyer or Janice Weiner appears anywhere in Bohannan's documented endorsement record, which does list other specific state legislators and party figures (e.g., state Sen. Mike Zimmer, former party chairs Wilburn and McGuire). Given that endorsement records are not guaranteed exhaustive, this is treated as an unconfirmed rather than definitively fabricated claim, but flagged given its specificity.

inaccurate_statement: A tracker counts 23 endorsements for Bohannan versus 13 for Miller-Meeks
description: No source or tracker matching this specific 23-versus-13 endorsement count comparison could be verified. Both candidates have numerous real, documented endorsements, but this specific comparative statistic attributed to 'one current tracker' does not appear in the available records for either candidate.

inaccurate_statement: Scott Bessent and Robert F. Kennedy Jr. are listed as Miller-Meeks's post-primary endorsements
description: Bessent and RFK Jr. made real campaign-trail appearances with Miller-Meeks after her primary (RFK Jr. at a Newton event, Bessent touring Vermeer), and this has been described in some reporting as administration support for her campaign, but no source frames these as formal 'endorsements' the way Trump's explicit 'Complete and Total Endorsement' was described. Presenting these appearances as formal listed endorsements overstates what actually occurred; the documented formal endorsement is President Trump's.

inaccurate_statement: A tracker counts 23 endorsements for Bohannan versus 13 for Miller-Meeks
description: No source or tracker matching this specific 23-versus-13 endorsement count comparison could be verified. Both candidates have numerous real, documented endorsements, but this specific comparative statistic attributed to 'one current tracker' does not appear in the available records for either candidate.

inaccurate_statement: Bohannan has been endorsed by Ob-GynPAC, the PAC associated with the American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists
description: There is no record of Ob-GynPAC endorsing Christina Bohannan. In fact, available information indicates Ob-GynPAC had endorsed Mariannette Miller-Meeks in prior cycles (2022 and 2024) and withdrew that endorsement in 2026 over her Medicaid vote — there is no indication it endorsed Bohannan instead. This appears to be a fabricated or misattributed endorsement claim.

inaccurate_statement: Bohannan is endorsed by former Iowa Democratic Party chair Sue Dvorsky
description: The documented endorsement record for Bohannan names former Iowa Democratic Party chairs Ross Wilburn and Andy McGuire, not Sue Dvorsky. No source confirms a Dvorsky endorsement of Bohannan.

inaccurate_statement: Bohannan is endorsed by Iowa House Minority Leader Brian Meyer and Iowa Senate Minority Leader Janice Weiner
description: No record supports these specific endorsements of Bohannan by these named Iowa legislative leaders; the documented endorser list includes different state legislators (e.g., state Sen. Mike Zimmer) and party figures.

inaccurate_statement: Other notable Democratic elected officials listed as endorsers of Bohannan include Gabby Giffords
description: Gabby Giffords is a gun-safety advocate, not a currently elected Democratic official, and there is no record of a personal Gabby Giffords endorsement of Bohannan distinct from the GIFFORDS PAC organizational endorsement already noted; listing her among 'elected officials' is inaccurate.

inaccurate_statement: One current tracker counts 36 endorsements total: 23 for Bohannan and 13 for Miller-Meeks
description: No such specific endorsement-count tracker or these precise numbers could be substantiated; this appears to be a fabricated or unverifiable aggregate statistic presented as a specific sourced count.

inaccurate_statement: Miller-Meeks has been endorsed by AIPAC
description: No record exists of AIPAC endorsing Mariannette Miller-Meeks. AIPAC's PAC endorsement activity in this race is not documented, and there is no basis for this specific claim.

inaccurate_statement: J Street Action Fund is spending against Miller-Meeks, identifying her as an AIPAC-backed Republican
description: There is no documented record of J Street Action Fund running independent spending against Miller-Meeks on this basis; the only confirmed J Street-related activity in this race is JStreetPAC's endorsement of Bohannan.

inaccurate_statement: One current tracker counts 36 endorsements total: 23 for Bohannan and 13 for Miller-Meeks
description: No such specific endorsement-count tracker or these precise numbers could be substantiated; this appears to be a fabricated or unverifiable aggregate statistic presented as a specific sourced count.

inaccurate_statement: Outside groups reportedly spent $39K supporting Bohannan through June 30
description: Independent-expenditure data (FEC Schedule E filings aggregated through late June 2026) shows outside groups spent only about $241 supporting Bohannan through that point in the cycle, not $39,000. This specific dollar figure does not match documented filings.

inaccurate_statement: Bohannan's funding breakdown: $4.55M (65%) from large individual donors and $1.09M (16%) from small/unitemized individual donations
description: Per FEC data, Bohannan's individual contributions totaled $5,648,339.98, which the response splits into $4.55M and $1.09M — sub-figures that do not clearly match any documented breakdown in the available source data and appear to be an unverified or invented split.

inaccurate_statement: About 77% of Bohannan's itemized contributions came from outside Iowa, with about $1.26M from Iowa itemized contributions
description: This specific geographic breakdown and dollar figure is not corroborated by the available campaign finance data. While it is documented that Bohannan has drawn a slightly higher share of in-state individual contributions than Miller-Meeks, the specific percentages and dollar amounts cited here cannot be verified and appear to be fabricated precision.

inaccurate_statement: Miller-Meeks received about $2.01M (28%) from itemized individual donors and about $936K (13%) from small/unitemized individual donations
description: Miller-Meeks's individual contributions per FEC filings totaled $2,945,343.16, categorized simply as individual contributions rather than split into itemized ($2.01M) and small/unitemized ($936K) subcategories in the dossier. The response's breakdown of these two sub-figures cannot be verified against the documented total and appears to be an invented split not supported by the underlying source data available.

inaccurate_statement: Miller-Meeks received about $1.8M (26%) from other receipts/transfers, much of it transfers from other authorized committees
description: The documented figure for Miller-Meeks's transfers from other authorized committees is $1,686,037.07, not approximately $1.8M as stated. This is a specific numeric discrepancy from the confirmed FEC data.

inaccurate_statement: Roughly 80% of Miller-Meeks' itemized individual contributions came from outside Iowa, with about $792K from Iowa itemized contributions

inaccurate_statement: Mariannette Miller-Meeks is a U.S. Air Force veteran
description: Miller-Meeks served in the U.S. Army Medical Department from 1974 to 1982 (retiring as a Lieutenant Colonel) and then the Army Reserve from 1983 to 2000, not the Air Force.

inaccurate_statement: Bohannan's platform includes expanding vision, dental, and hearing benefits under Medicaid
description: Bohannan's documented Medicare expansion proposal is to add dental, hearing, and vision coverage to Medicare (alongside a Medicare buy-in for any age), not to Medicaid. The response misattributes this benefit expansion to Medicaid rather than Medicare, which is the actual program she has proposed expanding in this way.

inaccurate_statement: Bohannan's healthcare platform includes expanding Medicare benefits (such as vision, dental, and hearing)
description: Bohannan's stated proposal is to expand Medicare, not Medicaid, to include vision, dental, and hearing coverage, alongside a Medicare buy-in option and reversing Medicaid cuts. The response conflates this with an 'expanding Medicaid benefits' claim, which misdescribes which program the dental/vision/hearing expansion applies to.

inaccurate_statement: There are no public reports or records showing that Bohannan herself used those exact words to describe the state; rather, the claim has been raised only by her critics during political campaigns.
description: This is a real, video-documented quote. In a 2021 legislative forum, then-state-Rep. Bohannan opposed a bill barring transgender athletes from girls'/women's sports, saying the ban would send "a very bad message about our state that's going to make the state look like a backwater." The response incorrectly claims no such statement exists and that this is purely a fabricated attack line, when in fact Bohannan did use this word herself, albeit in a conditional, policy-specific context that attack coverage often strips out. This reverses the core fact of the matter for the reader.

inaccurate_statement: The claim that Bohannan called Iowa a 'backwater state' has been asserted by political opponents, but there is no public record of her making that remark in her own statements.
description: This is a real, video-documented quote: in a 2021 legislative forum, then-state-Rep. Bohannan opposed a bill barring transgender athletes from girls'/women's sports, saying the ban would send 'a very bad message about our state that's going to make the state look like a backwater.' She separately also used the phrase 'backwards state' in a different comment about DEI training restrictions. The response's claim that there is 'no public record' of her making this remark is factually wrong — the quote is documented and its authenticity is not in dispute, though its framing as a conditional, policy-specific prediction rather than a blanket statement about Iowa is often stripped away in attack coverage. The response should have confirmed the quote's existence while adding the missing context, not denied that any such statement exists.

inaccurate_statement: The complaint alleging Miller-Meeks violated Iowa law was filed with both the federal Office of Congressional Ethics and the House Committee on Ethics
description: The residency/voting ethics complaint against Miller-Meeks was filed with the federal Office of Congressional Ethics only; the House Committee on Ethics would only become involved if the OCE referred the matter forward, and no source indicates a separate, direct filing with the House Committee on Ethics.

inaccurate_statement: Bohannan's opposition to the 'Back the Blue' bill was focused on specific provisions—such as penalties related to protests and the withholding of municipal funds—rather than a desire to defund law enforcement
description: Bohannan's actual stated objections to the 2021 'Back the Blue' bill centered on concerns that it could undermine public trust in police, pit protesters against law enforcement, and infringe on civil liberties and the right to protest, not specifically on penalties tied to protests and withholding of municipal funds as a distinct, confirmed rationale. While some later characterizations (including her own campaign's defense) have referenced concerns about funding provisions, the core, best-documented rationale in her record is about civil liberties and public trust rather than this specific funding-withholding framing.

inaccurate_statement: Bohannan made a 2019 social media donation to the Prairielands Freedom Fund, and said she was simply contributing to a friend's birthday fundraiser and not endorsing the organization's broader platforms
description: The donation in question was a $60 contribution to the Prairielands Freedom Fund cited by Miller-Meeks in 2021 as part of the 'abolish law enforcement' attack line, not a 2019 donation, and it was framed around Bohannan saying she did not know the group's broader mission when she donated, rather than characterizing it as a friend's birthday fundraiser. The birthday-fundraiser framing does not match the documented account of this donation.

inaccurate_statement: Bohannan's stock portfolio consists of individual technology stocks
description: Bohannan's confirmed financial disclosure holdings include Apple, Alphabet Class C, Meta (all tech companies) but also a large Amana Mutual Funds Trust position reported at $500,001-$1,000,000, which is not a technology stock. Describing her portfolio broadly as 'a portfolio of individual technology stocks' omits this larger, non-tech holding and overstates the tech-specific framing, though the underlying point that she holds individual tech stocks is accurate.

inaccurate_statement: The ethics complaint regarding financial disclosure omissions was filed by/attributed to the DCCC
description: The 2021 ethics complaint alleging financial disclosure omissions was filed by the Iowa Democratic Party with the Office of Congressional Ethics, not by the DCCC. The response's repeated 'DCCC' labels appear to be stray sourcing artifacts rather than substantiated claims that the DCCC itself filed or is the source of these allegations.

inaccurate_statement: An ethics complaint regarding Miller-Meeks's residency/voting address was filed with the House Committee on Ethics
description: The residency/voter-registration ethics complaint was filed with the federal Office of Congressional Ethics (OCE), not directly with the House Committee on Ethics. The House Ethics Committee would only become involved if OCE referred the matter, and reporting indicates OCE did not pursue the complaint further, so there is no record of a direct House Ethics Committee filing on this issue.

inaccurate_statement: Bohannan has taught subjects including constitutional law, torts, and intellectual property for over two decades at the University of Iowa College of Law
description: Bohannan moved to Iowa in 2000 to become a University of Iowa law professor, and has taught torts, copyright, and conflict of laws, per her documented biography. The dossier does not confirm a two-decade teaching span specifically inclusive of constitutional law as a taught subject in the same way; her documented subjects are torts, copyright, and conflict of laws, not explicitly constitutional law. While she has been at the university for roughly two decades and this is broadly consistent with a long tenure, the specific subject-matter claim (constitutional law as a course she taught) is not confirmed in her core biography, making this a narrow overstatement of her exact teaching portfolio rather than a fundamental misrepresentation of her academic career.

inaccurate_statement: During her time in the state legislature, she focused on issues like public school funding and consumer protections
description: Bohannan's documented Iowa House record centers on committee assignments in Natural Resources, Veterans Affairs, Agriculture/Natural Resources Appropriations, Information Technology, Judiciary, and State Government, and she worked on bipartisan elder-abuse and human-trafficking legislation. There is no specific documentation tying her legislative focus to 'public school funding and consumer protections' as stated; this appears to be an unsupported characterization of her legislative priorities rather than a confirmed fact from her record.

inaccurate_statement: For over two decades, she has worked as a law professor at the University of Iowa College of Law
description: Bohannan moved to Iowa in 2000 to become a University of Iowa College of Law professor, and she left in 2021 to serve in the Iowa House of Representatives before running for Congress in 2022. This is roughly two decades of teaching (about 20-21 years), so "over two decades" slightly overstates the length of her tenure, though it is close to accurate.

inaccurate_statement: Her legislative work in the Iowa House focused on public school funding, consumer protections, and the rule of law
description: Bohannan's documented legislative work in the Iowa House centered on bipartisan elder-abuse and human-trafficking legislation, and her committee assignments were Natural Resources, Veterans Affairs, Agriculture/Natural Resources Appropriations, Information Technology, Judiciary, and State Government -- not a specific documented focus on "public school funding" as a signature legislative priority during her time in office. This appears to be an unsupported characterization of her legislative focus rather than a well-documented fact.

inaccurate_statement: Bohannan has spent more than two decades as a law professor at the University of Iowa College of Law, teaching subjects including constitutional law, torts, and intellectual property.
description: Bohannan moved to Iowa in 2000 to become a University of Iowa College of Law professor, which would be about 25 years by 2025, so "more than two decades" is roughly accurate on tenure length. However, her documented teaching subjects are Torts, Copyright, and Conflict of Laws, not constitutional law specifically; while other sources describe her as teaching constitutional law in some capacity, the core dossier lists Torts, Copyright, and Conflict of Laws as her documented subjects, with intellectual property (copyright) confirmed but constitutional law not directly confirmed in the primary bio listing.

inaccurate_statement: She enlisted in the U.S. Army at age 18 and served for 24 years... working as a private, nurse, and physician before retiring as a lieutenant colonel.
description: There is no record confirming she enlisted specifically at age 18 or served in the rank/role of 'private' before becoming a nurse and physician; her documented Army service was 1974–1982 active duty plus reserve service through 2000, retiring as a Lieutenant Colonel. The core facts of military service and eventual rank are accurate, but the specific added details about enlistment age and starting as a 'private' are not corroborated.

inaccurate_statement: She held the position of Director of the Iowa Department of Public Health until 2014.
description: Miller-Meeks served as Iowa Department of Public Health Director from 2010 to 2013, not until 2014, resigning to run for Congress.

inaccurate_statement: She served as Director of the Iowa Department of Public Health until 2014.
description: Miller-Meeks served as Iowa Department of Public Health Director from 2010 to 2013, not 2014, resigning to run for Congress.

inaccurate_statement: Miller-Meeks promotes non-opioid pain management alternatives as part of lowering out-of-pocket drug costs for seniors
description: There is no documented evidence in her platform or record connecting non-opioid pain management alternatives to her prescription-drug-cost/PBM-focused healthcare agenda. Her documented opioid-related work is the DUMP Opioids Act, a separate initiative not framed as a senior out-of-pocket drug cost measure. This is a narrow, unsubstantiated addition to an otherwise accurate description of her healthcare platform.

inaccurate_statement: Focuses on protecting Medicare and Medicaid stability
description: Miller-Meeks's actual healthcare record is more mixed than a simple 'protecting stability' framing suggests. She voted for the 2025 reconciliation bill (OBBBA) containing significant Medicaid work-requirement provisions and cuts, and voted against a bipartisan bill extending enhanced ACA premium tax credits. While she has secured targeted rural health funding and disputes causal claims linking Medicaid cuts to local provider losses, characterizing her overall approach as simply 'protecting Medicare and Medicaid stability' omits the documented tension between her voting record and this framing.

inaccurate_statement: The 2022 race is implicitly grouped with 2024 as if both were close, when only 2024 was historically close (799 votes); 2022 was a comfortable 53%-47% win for Miller-Meeks
description: The response describes Bohannan running in 2022 and then 'waging a historically close race in 2024,' which correctly identifies 2024 as the close race. However, the phrasing groups both races together in a way that could be read as implying 2022 was also close, when in fact Miller-Meeks won 2022 comfortably by about 7 points (53%-47%), not narrowly. Only the 2024 race was decided by a razor-thin margin (799 votes). This is a minor ambiguity rather than a clear reversal of the facts, since 2024 is correctly labeled as the close one.

inaccurate_statement: She served in the U.S. Army and U.S. Army Reserve for 24 years, rising from a private and a nurse to retire as a lieutenant colonel
description: Her documented military service was 1974–1982 in the Army Medical Department, then Army Reserve 1983–2000, and she earned a BSN before service rather than serving as an enlisted private who became a nurse; the 'private' framing misdescribes her entry point, and the combined active/reserve span differs somewhat from a clean '24 years' figure, though she is genuinely described elsewhere as a '24-year Army veteran.'

inaccurate_statement: She was director of the Iowa Department of Public Health from 2010 to 2014
description: She served as Iowa Department of Public Health Director from 2010 to 2013, not 2014, resigning to run for Congress.

inaccurate_statement: Miller-Meeks was director of the Iowa Department of Public Health from 2010 to 2014.
description: Miller-Meeks served as director of the Iowa Department of Public Health from 2010 to 2013, not 2010 to 2014; she resigned in 2013 to run for Congress.

inaccurate_statement: Miller-Meeks enlisted in the U.S. Army at age 18 and served on active duty and later in the Army Reserve, retiring as a lieutenant colonel after 24 years of combined service as a private, nurse, and physician.
description: Documented records show her military service was active duty in the Army Medical Department from 1974-1982 followed by Army Reserve service from 1983-2000, roughly 26 years rather than 24, and there is no record confirming she enlisted at exactly age 18 or served specifically as a 'private' before becoming a nurse and physician.

inaccurate_statement: Bohannan blamed Miller-Meeks for backing 'constitutional amendments' related to abortion
description: There is no record of Bohannan specifically criticizing Miller-Meeks over a constitutional amendment on abortion; the documented criticism concerns the Life at Conception Act and Iowa's state abortion restrictions, not a constitutional amendment. This appears to be an added detail not substantiated by the available record.

inaccurate_statement: Bohannan argued that Miller-Meeks' abortion positions would result in total bans without adequate or truthful exceptions
description: Fact-checkers have noted that some of Bohannan's wording about Miller-Meeks' role in Iowa's abortion ban was overstated, since Miller-Meeks was not a state legislator when the Iowa law passed, and Miller-Meeks's actual position includes rape/incest/life-of-mother exceptions rather than no exceptions at all, though Bohannan has characterized the co-sponsored federal Life at Conception Act as lacking adequate exceptions.

inaccurate_statement: Bohannan criticized Miller-Meeks and House Republicans for declining to support a bipartisan border security package, using it as a campaign issue rather than addressing the problem
description: While Bohannan has criticized Miller-Meeks over border security and the bipartisan Senate package, the specific framing that Miller-Meeks 'declined to support' this package to use it purely as a campaign issue is a characterization not directly confirmed as her own quoted framing; Bohannan's documented criticism centers more on Miller-Meeks and leadership failing to bring such measures to a vote and on general border-policy attacks.

inaccurate_statement: Bohannan has earned an endorsement from the American Federation of Government Employees (AFGE) specifically for her commitment to workers/organized labor as part of her jobs platform framing
description: AFGE is a real, confirmed endorser of Bohannan, so the endorsement itself is accurate. However, tying this endorsement specifically to a 'good local jobs' or organized-labor jobs-creation platform overstates what is documented; the endorsement is a general labor-union endorsement rather than evidence tied to a specific local-jobs mechanism. This is a narrow framing issue rather than a fabricated endorsement, since AFGE's support for Bohannan is genuine.

inaccurate_statement: Bohannan emphasized the importance of building mutual trust and confidence between law enforcement officers and the communities they serve, and raised concerns that certain legal immunities for officers can hinder public trust
description: Bohannan's actual objections to Iowa's 2021 'Back the Blue' bill centered on protecting the right to protest, avoiding pitting police against racial-justice communities, and concerns the law could undermine public trust and civil liberties more broadly — not a specific, itemized concern about qualified immunity provisions harming trust as the primary framing. While there is a real, documented connection between her record and general public-trust language, presenting this as a clean 'law enforcement trust' framework overstates and narrows what was a more contested, broader-based objection to the bill.

inaccurate_statement: Christina Bohannan is a designated 'Gun Sense Candidate of Distinction'
description: No record exists of this specific designation being attributed to Bohannan. Her documented gun-safety credentials include being a longtime member of Moms Demand Action and having a GIFFORDS PAC candidate page describing her support for commonsense gun reforms, but no source describes her as a 'Gun Sense Candidate of Distinction,' which appears to be a specific title not found in the available material. The broader claim that she supports commonsense gun measures is accurate, so this is a narrow labeling error rather than a mischaracterization of her actual positions.

inaccurate_statement: Miller-Meeks approaches water infrastructure and quality with a focus that includes addressing Iowa's water quality crisis through infrastructure resilience and permitting clarity
description: Miller-Meeks has no direct 2026 statement addressing Iowa's nitrate/cancer-linked water quality crisis specifically; her documented positions are general infrastructure/wastewater funding and permitting reform, not a stated plan targeting the nitrate crisis itself. Presenting her funding and permitting record as a direct response to "Iowa's water quality crisis" overstates what she has actually said, though the underlying funding and voting facts cited are accurate.

inaccurate_statement: Framing implies Miller-Meeks's water-infrastructure funding and PERMIT Act support constitute her plan to address Iowa's nitrate/cancer-linked water quality crisis specifically
description: No direct statement from Miller-Meeks addressing Iowa's nitrate/cancer-linked water quality crisis specifically has been found despite dedicated searching. Her documented water-related actions are general infrastructure/wastewater funding (Davenport flood mitigation, Muscatine wastewater) and a broader regulatory philosophy (PERMIT Act, Navigable Waters Protection Rule), not a stated response to the nitrate crisis that is the dominant 2026 water-quality issue in her district. Presenting these general infrastructure and permitting positions as her answer to 'the water quality crisis' without noting this gap risks overstating how directly she has engaged with the specific, high-salience nitrate/cancer water crisis.

inaccurate_statement: Implies the Davenport and Muscatine funding is specifically framed as addressing the nitrate/agricultural-runoff water quality crisis
description: The Davenport Water Pollution Control Plant funding relates to flood-mitigation/wastewater infrastructure, and no direct 2026 statement from Miller-Meeks specifically addressing the nitrate/cancer-linked water quality crisis has been found. Presenting her funding record as a direct response to that specific crisis without noting this gap risks overstating her engagement with the issue that is dominating 2026 IA-01 coverage.

inaccurate_statement: MCED screening tests coverage starts in 2029
description: Multiple sources, including Miller-Meeks's own press materials and the bill text, confirm that Medicare coverage for FDA-approved multi-cancer early detection tests under this legislation begins in 2028, not 2029.

inaccurate_statement: Miller-Meeks's Congressional Steel Caucus advocacy benefits regional employers like Gerdau and SSAB
description: Miller-Meeks is confirmed to be involved with SSAB in Muscatine and has cited her Congressional Steel Caucus work as supporting domestic steel production, but no source specifically ties her Steel Caucus advocacy to Gerdau by name in connection with this caucus; her documented Gerdau connection concerns a separate 'No Tax on Overtime' comment about increased overtime at Gerdau's Iowa operations, not Steel Caucus advocacy specifically. This is a narrow, minor detail that does not change the overall accurate picture of her support for the domestic steel industry and these Quad Cities-area employers.

inaccurate_statement: Regional road updates directly benefit emergency medical responses, fire responses, and law enforcement navigation
description: Miller-Meeks did secure funding for the U.S. Highway 6/Deer Creek Road intersection project, justified as improving traffic safety and accommodating growing traffic, but none of the official sources describing this project mention improving emergency response times for fire, law enforcement, and EMS as a stated purpose. This appears to be an added embellishment not found in the record.

inaccurate_statement: Miller-Meeks has directed federal investments toward modernizing bridges and infrastructure explicitly to ensure reliable access for emergency medical, fire response, and law enforcement personnel
description: Miller-Meeks did secure funding for road and intersection projects like the U.S. Highway 6/Deer Creek Road project, justified as improving traffic safety and accommodating growth, but no official source describing this or her other infrastructure funding mentions improving emergency response times for fire, law enforcement, and EMS as a stated purpose. This appears to be an added embellishment not found in the record.

inaccurate_statement: Following Miller-Meeks's push, the administration suspended duties on phosphate fertilizer imports to reduce costs for producers
description: The knowledge base confirms Miller-Meeks introduced the Lowering Input Costs for American Farmers Act targeting fertilizer tariffs/duties, but there is no documented confirmation that the administration actually suspended the duties as a direct result of her push. This causal claim of an achieved policy outcome goes beyond what the dossier establishes, which only documents the bill's introduction, not a confirmed suspension of duties tied to her advocacy.

inaccurate_statement: Miller-Meeks co-sponsored the Preventing Violence Against Women by Illegal Aliens Act to ensure sex offenders face deportation and inadmissibility.
description: Miller-Meeks voted for the Preventing Violence Against Women by Illegal Aliens Act, but there is no record confirming she co-sponsored it as opposed to simply voting for it; this is a narrow attribution distinction rather than a substantive misrepresentation of her position on the bill's underlying goal.

inaccurate_statement: Bohannan specializes in constitutional and business law as a law professor
description: Bohannan's documented academic specialization as a University of Iowa law professor was in Torts, Copyright, and Conflict of Laws, and she is also described elsewhere as having taught constitutional law. There is no record in her biography of a specialization in "business law" specifically; this appears to be an inaccurate addition to her actual teaching areas.

inaccurate_statement: Bohannan grew up in a small town with a construction worker father
description: Bohannan was born in Florida, the youngest of three children in a working-class family, and worked as an environmental engineer before becoming a law professor. No record supports the specific detail that her father was a construction worker or that she grew up in a small town; her documented biography does not include this specific claim.

inaccurate_statement: Supporters frequently note her extensive local presence, highlighting her routine county-by-county tours across her district to engage directly with constituents.
description: Miller-Meeks did complete a 20-county in-person tour, but her broader accessibility record is genuinely mixed: she largely avoided in-person town halls for most of 2025 (telling a GOP meeting she'd hold one 'when hell freezes over'), holding only one contentious in-person town hall in the period researched, while relying primarily on tele-town halls for direct constituent engagement. Describing her local presence as simply 'routine' and unqualified constituent engagement omits this well-documented tension and paints an incomplete picture of her accessibility record.

inaccurate_statement: She has introduced measures to expand access to affordable treatments and reduce out-of-pocket drug costs for seniors
description: While Miller-Meeks has genuinely pursued PBM transparency and drug-cost legislation, this generic phrasing about reducing out-of-pocket drug costs for seniors is not tied to a specific, verifiable bill beyond her documented PBM/DRUG Act work, making it a vague overstatement rather than a clearly sourced claim; however, it is closely aligned with her real record and does not materially mislead.

inaccurate_statement: Decision Desk tilts the race Lean Democratic
description: No source in the available material corroborates a Decision Desk HQ rating of 'Lean Democratic' for this specific race; documented forecaster ratings for IA-01 consistently show Cook Political Report, Inside Elections, and Sabato's Crystal Ball all at 'Toss-up,' with no distinct Decision Desk rating confirmed as diverging to Lean Democratic.

inaccurate_statement: Miller-Meeks defeated 'conservative challenger' David Pautsch by an unspecified margin implying a close race
description: Miller-Meeks defeated David Pautsch by more than 40 points in the June 2026 primary, a landslide rather than a competitive contest; describing the primary outcome without noting this is a minor understatement but not clearly a misleading claim on its own.

inaccurate_statement: Miller-Meeks co-sponsored bipartisan legislation (the INSULIN Act) to cap private-insurance insulin costs at $35 per month to bolster her healthcare record against Democratic criticism
description: There is no record of Miller-Meeks co-sponsoring an 'INSULIN Act' capping private-insurance insulin costs at $35/month. Her actual documented record is the opposite on this specific issue: she voted against a Democratic-backed measure that would have capped insulin costs for certain Medicare beneficiaries, and reporting describes her accepting pharmaceutical industry PAC contributions around the time of votes against insulin-cost caps. Her real healthcare cost-lowering legislation is the 'Lower Health Care Premiums for All Americans Act,' which focuses on PBM transparency and premium reduction, not a specific $35 insulin cap bill. This claim reverses her actual voting record on this exact issue, which would materially mislead a reader about her healthcare positioning.

inaccurate_statement: Decision Desk tilts the race Lean Democratic
description: No source in the available material corroborates a Decision Desk HQ rating of 'Lean Democratic' for this specific race; documented forecaster ratings for IA-01 consistently show Cook Political Report, Inside Elections, and Sabato's Crystal Ball all at 'Toss-up,' with no distinct Decision Desk rating confirmed as diverging to Lean Democratic.

inaccurate_statement: Mariannette Miller-Meeks's platform emphasizes lowering healthcare and prescription drug costs by taking on insurance companies
description: Miller-Meeks's documented healthcare cost approach centers on pharmacy benefit manager (PBM) transparency, association health plans, price transparency requirements, and market-based competition rather than being framed around directly confronting insurance companies. In fact, she voted against extending ACA subsidies partly by arguing they benefit insurance companies, and her own messaging criticizes rather than targets insurers in the way this framing implies. This 'taking on insurance companies' framing is more closely associated with Bohannan's messaging, making this a mischaracterization of Miller-Meeks's specific approach.

inaccurate_statement: Miller-Meeks led bipartisan pushes to cap out-of-pocket insulin costs
description: Miller-Meeks's documented record on insulin costs is that she voted against a Democratic bill to cap insulin prices for Medicare beneficiaries, not that she led a bipartisan effort to cap insulin costs. Her actual healthcare cost-lowering initiatives focus on pharmacy benefit manager (PBM) transparency and price transparency legislation, not an insulin cap specifically. This reverses her documented position on insulin price caps.

inaccurate_statement: Bohannan's 2022 defeat against Miller-Meeks was narrow
description: The 2022 Bohannan-Miller-Meeks race was won comfortably by Miller-Meeks, 53%-47% (roughly 20,000 votes, about a 7-point margin) — this was not a close race. Only the 2024 rematch was genuinely narrow, decided by 799 votes after a recount. Describing the 2022 result as a 'narrow defeat' alongside 2024 conflates a comfortable win with the true nail-biter.

inaccurate_statement: Miller-Meeks introduced federal measures targeting government fraud and financial accountability as part of her crime/public-safety legislative focus
description: Miller-Meeks has sponsored government-waste-oversight legislation such as the Billion Dollar Boondoggle Act, but this is a fiscal-transparency measure about cost overruns on federal projects, not a crime or public-safety measure. Framing it as part of her public-safety/crime platform conflates two distinct areas of her legislative record.

inaccurate_statement: Miller-Meeks focuses her economic platform on supply chain independence, boosting domestic manufacturing, and lowering regulations
description: While Miller-Meeks does support manufacturing-related legislation and deregulation broadly, her official platform's specific 'jobs/local jobs' framing according to her own materials centers more on tax policy (Small Business Deduction, Working Families Tax Cuts), energy production, and targeted local infrastructure funding rather than being organized specifically around a 'supply chain independence' banner as a headline theme, though the ONSHORE Act does relate to this. This is a loose but not badly wrong characterization.

inaccurate_statement: Miller-Meeks has supported agricultural relief packages and precision agriculture initiatives through the Farm Bill to help lower input costs for farmers
description: Miller-Meeks's documented farm-related record includes voting for the Farm, Food, and National Security Act of 2026 and introducing a bill cutting fertilizer tariffs, but no source ties her specifically to a 'precision agriculture initiatives' component of the Farm Bill. This is a specific, unverified mechanism presented as her stated position without hedging, going beyond what is documented.

inaccurate_statement: Miller-Meeks's grocery-price approach is centered on supporting agricultural production, addressing supply chain resilience, and combating market concentration as a distinct grocery-prices platform
description: Miller-Meeks's official House website 'Economy' issues page and her public statements/ads on prices frame the issue as general inflation blamed on 'Bidenomics,' with her stated solutions centered on energy independence (fracking, LNG exports, E15), tax cuts, and housing legislation -- not a distinct grocery-prices platform built around the three pillars claimed (agricultural production support, supply chain resilience, and combating market concentration). Her comments on grocery prices, such as noting people 'are paying about 21 percent more' at the grocery store, appear as part of broader inflation criticism rather than a standalone, structured grocery-price policy platform with these specific elements. No evidence surfaced of her articulating this specific three-part framework as a distinct platform.

inaccurate_statement: Bohannan focuses on community-oriented approaches to safety, emphasizing crime prevention through economic support, strengthening laws related to public safety, and addressing the root causes of crime while ensuring accountability
description: Bohannan's own campaign platform contains no dedicated public-safety or crime-prevention section as such; a general, non-gun public-safety plan was a confirmed gap in her documented record. She does have a real, sourced position on gun-violence prevention (supporting background-check expansion and extreme risk protection orders) and a documented 2021 vote against Iowa's 'Back the Blue' bill, but the specific framing of 'crime prevention through economic support' and 'strengthening laws related to public safety' as a coherent stated approach is not substantiated by her platform or record and overstates what is actually a narrower, more contested set of positions.

inaccurate_statement: Bohannan's foreign policy platform emphasizes multilateral diplomacy, selective international engagement, and economic stability as a pillar of national strength, rather than defense sector manufacturing or military expansion
description: This presents a specific foreign-policy framing as Bohannan's stated position without noting that she has no dedicated foreign policy/national security platform section on her campaign site, which is focused almost entirely on domestic affordability, healthcare, education, and farm issues. While she has made some general statements supporting Ukraine and Israel and favoring strategic, fiscally disciplined engagement, the specific framing of 'multilateral diplomacy' and 'economic stability as a pillar of national strength' as an articulated doctrine is an inference presented without appropriate hedging, rather than a position she has explicitly stated in those terms.

inaccurate_statement: Miller-Meeks's local defense infrastructure emphasis includes securing funding for the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant
description: There is no record of Miller-Meeks specifically securing funding for or emphasizing the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant (located in Middletown, Iowa, actually within IA-01's general area). Her documented defense-infrastructure focus specifically names the Rock Island Arsenal and Iowa's defense workforce; no source ties her to the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant by name. This is a narrow, unverified addition to an otherwise accurate characterization of her defense-infrastructure advocacy.

inaccurate_statement: Bohannan focuses heavily on addressing rising rural cancer rates, protecting local public health department funding, and restoring or strengthening Medicaid funding to ensure rural hospitals and clinics remain viable
description: Bohannan does have a documented, strong focus on cancer research funding, rural hospital viability, and reversing Medicaid cuts, which is accurate. However, there is no record of her specifically focusing on 'protecting local public health department funding' as a distinct, named plank of her platform; her documented statements center on NIH cancer-research funding, insurance/Medicaid, rural hospital tours, and clinical-trial access rather than local public health department budgets specifically. This adds an unsupported specific detail to an otherwise accurate general characterization.

inaccurate_statement: Bohannan stresses addressing corporate price gouging in the oil and gas industries specifically
description: Bohannan's documented price-gouging rhetoric is broader, targeting corporate price gouging generally (including at the grocery store and gas pump) and utility monopolies, rather than being specifically and primarily framed around the oil and gas industries as a distinct target. Framing this as an oil-and-gas-specific focus somewhat narrows and mischaracterizes her actual, broader affordability messaging.

inaccurate_statement: Bohannan advocates for increasing Medicaid funding to support local rural healthcare facilities
description: Bohannan's documented healthcare position is to reverse Medicaid cuts made under recent federal legislation and to support rural hospitals through that reversal, rather than a stated platform of affirmatively increasing Medicaid funding as a distinct new initiative. This is a subtle mischaracterization of her actual stance (restoring cuts) rather than a wholly different position, so it is treated as a narrow, minor error.

inaccurate_statement: Miller-Meeks emphasizes... restrictions on transgender athletes in girls' sports as part of her platform
description: There is no documented statement or platform position from Miller-Meeks specifically addressing restrictions on transgender athletes in girls' sports. This issue appears in the available records only in connection with a 2021 Iowa legislative debate involving Christina Bohannan (the 'backwater' quote controversy), not as a stated Miller-Meeks position. Presenting this as one of her emphasized issues is not supported by her documented platform, which centers on school choice, parental rights, and related education priorities without specific mention of this issue.

inaccurate_statement: Bohannan proposes adding dental/vision benefits to Medicaid
description: Bohannan's documented healthcare platform proposes expanding Medicare (not Medicaid) to cover vision, dental, and hearing, alongside a Medicare buy-in at any age. There is no record of her proposing to add dental/vision benefits specifically to Medicaid, and this appears to substitute the wrong program for an otherwise accurately described policy position.

inaccurate_statement: The response attributes the 'backwater' claim solely to political opponents' assertions without noting this is a real, documented quote with a conditional/policy-specific framing that attack coverage strips of context
description: The quote is a real, video-documented statement Bohannan made in a 2021 legislative forum, not merely an opposition assertion or accusation of uncertain veracity. It was a conditional prediction about how passing a specific bill would affect Iowa's reputation, not a freestanding claim that Iowa is currently backward. By framing this entirely as something 'political opponents... have asserted,' the response implies the underlying claim is unconfirmed or contested, when in fact the quote itself is not in dispute — only its fair characterization is, since attack coverage compresses out the conditional/policy-specific context.

inaccurate_statement: Local review boards—such as the Scott County board reviewing challenged ballots—rejected the challenges to Miller-Meeks's voter registration
description: The Scott County board actually accepted and counted Miller-Meeks's 2024 ballot after the residency challenge, rather than rejecting it. This reverses the actual outcome of the review and would materially mislead a reader about how the challenge was resolved.

inaccurate_statement: A formal complaint was filed with the House Committee on Ethics (in addition to the Office of Congressional Ethics) by a constituent, backed by political organizations like the DCCC
description: The residency/voting ethics complaint against Miller-Meeks was filed with the federal Office of Congressional Ethics, which forwards complaints to the House Committee on Ethics only if it finds a credible violation; there is no documented evidence that a separate, direct filing was made with the House Committee on Ethics itself, nor that the DCCC was a formal backer of the complaint. The complaint is documented as being filed by a Bettendorf resident, not attributed in available sources to DCCC backing.

inaccurate_statement: Bohannan disputed characterizations of a 2019 donation, noting it was a small contribution made for a friend's birthday fundraiser without full awareness of the organization's broader platform
description: The documented donation/attack narrative involves a $60 donation to the Prairielands Freedom Fund, which Miller-Meeks referenced in a 2021 attack that PolitiFact rated false; the record does not describe this as tied to a friend's birthday fundraiser or specify a 2019 date. This appears to be an embellished or misattributed detail added to an otherwise real underlying donation controversy, though it doesn't change the overall accurate point that Bohannan disputed the broader characterization of the donation.

inaccurate_statement: Bohannan opposed the "Back the Blue" bill because she believed certain provisions would strip funding from municipalities
description: Bohannan's documented objections to Iowa's 2021 'Back the Blue' bill centered on protecting the right to protest, avoiding pitting law enforcement against racial justice advocates, and concerns that the bill would erode civil liberties and public trust in police. There is no record of her framing her objection around the bill stripping funding from municipalities; the bill itself concerned increasing penalties and protections for police, not municipal funding levels, and this specific framing mischaracterizes the substance of her stated rationale.

inaccurate_statement: Critics contend Miller-Meeks supported tax legislation referred to as the "Big, Ugly Bill" that disproportionately benefits the ultra-wealthy and corporations
description: The major 2025 reconciliation tax-and-spending bill Miller-Meeks voted for is widely referred to as the "One Big Beautiful Bill" (OBBBA), not the "Big, Ugly Bill." This appears to be a garbled or incorrect nickname for the legislation, though the underlying claim that she voted for this bill and that critics say it favors the wealthy is consistent with her documented record.

inaccurate_statement: Christina Bohannan is 'the granddaughter of family farmers' and has centered her agricultural platform on this personal heritage
description: Available biographical material describes Bohannan as growing up in a working-class family in rural Florida and does not establish that her agricultural platform is centered on a personal family-farming heritage; her platform's farm-policy rationale is not documented as being framed around a grandparent farming background or the 1980s farm crisis specifically.

inaccurate_statement: Bohannan's policies promote renewable energy opportunities such as biofuels and clean energy specifically as part of her sustainable-farming/water-quality plank
description: Bohannan's confirmed platform statements on water quality and sustainable farming reference PFAS/nitrate reduction and buffer-zone incentives, not a specific biofuels or clean-energy component tied to this plank; presenting biofuels/clean energy as part of this specific policy area goes beyond what is documented.

inaccurate_statement: Farm Action Fund endorsed Christina Bohannan

inaccurate_statement: The CBO estimated that Miller-Meeks's premium bill could result in a reduction of insured individuals by an average of 100,000 people per year over a multi-year period
description: The CBO analysis of the Lower Health Care Premiums for All Americans Act found it would reduce gross benchmark premiums by about 11%, but no source ties a '100,000 people per year' coverage-loss estimate specifically to this bill. The commonly cited ~110,000 additional uninsured Iowans figure comes from KFF and relates to the combined effect of ACA subsidy expiration and Medicaid cuts more broadly, not this specific premium bill's CBO score. This conflates or misattributes a coverage-loss estimate to the wrong policy vehicle.

inaccurate_statement: CBO estimates indicated the Lower Health Care Premiums for All Americans Act could lead to an average reduction in the number of people with health insurance by roughly 100,000 people per year between 2027 and 2035
description: The knowledge base and available reporting on Miller-Meeks's Lower Health Care Premiums for All Americans Act describe a CBO estimate that the bill would reduce gross benchmark premiums by about 11%, but no source in the record attributes a specific figure of '100,000 fewer insured people per year between 2027 and 2035' to CBO analysis of this bill. This appears to be an unsupported or invented statistic layered onto an otherwise accurately described piece of legislation, though it does not change the broader accurate point that her bill has been analyzed by CBO and involves tradeoffs between premiums and coverage.

inaccurate_statement: Miller-Meeks has supported measures improving Medicaid enrollment data accuracy

This is a narrow, specific detail that doesn't change the overall accurate picture of her healthcare record.

inaccurate_statement: Bohannan's proposals include banning stock trading by Supreme Court justices

inaccurate_statement: Bohannan heavily invests in rural infrastructure, public schools, and local economies as a stated platform focus on addressing food security for students

inaccurate_statement: Bohannan's priorities include expanding programs for children's nutrition

inaccurate_statement: She served in the Iowa State Senate from 2019 to 2021.
description: Miller-Meeks served in the Iowa Senate District 41 seat starting in 2019 after being elected in 2018, and the documented record shows her serving there until she resigned to take her U.S. House seat after winning the 2020 election (seated January 2021), so the 2019-2021 date range is essentially accurate and consistent with the source material.

inaccurate_statement: She was elected to the U.S. House of Representatives to represent Iowa's congressional districts (plural).
description: Miller-Meeks was elected to represent a single congressional district each time: Iowa's 2nd District in 2020 (pre-redistricting) and Iowa's 1st District since 2023 following redistricting. The plural 'congressional districts' framing is imprecise, though the underlying fact that she has served in Congress since 2021 and currently represents IA-01 is accurate.

inaccurate_statement: Bohannan supports a ban on personal use of congressional office budgets
description: No record exists of Bohannan proposing a specific ban on personal use of congressional office budgets. inaccurate_statement: Bohannan supports expanding Medicare to cover dental, hearing, and vision
