inaccurate_statement: Nunn is generally supportive of data center development but caveats his support with consumer protections, and has praised Iowa as a "model for how workforce development and AI leadership can work hand in hand."
description: No record exists of Zach Nunn making any statement about data-center development, ratepayer cost-shifting, or this specific quote about Iowa being a "model for how workforce development and AI leadership can work hand in hand." This was researched as a genuine, confirmed gap after dedicated searches of his campaign site, House office site, and news coverage found nothing on data centers despite this being a major live district issue. Presenting a fabricated direct quote and a specific stated position as his own is a fabrication.

inaccurate_statement: Nunn believes it would be a "dangerous precedent" for a member of Congress to override local zoning decisions for or against a data center project, and maintains that responsibility falls on the developer, utility provider, and local municipality to ensure facilities don't drive up energy costs.
description: No statement from Nunn addressing data-center development, zoning authority, or electricity-cost impacts from data centers was found despite dedicated research; this is documented as a confirmed gap. The quoted "dangerous precedent" language and the specific regulatory framework attributed to him are not supported by any known statement and appear fabricated.

inaccurate_statement: If you support data centers but want strict legal firewalls so they don't increase your personal electric bill, Zach Nunn's consumer-focused platform shares that specific priority.
description: This conclusion rests on fabricated quotes and positions attributed to Nunn regarding data centers, which are not supported by any documented statement from him on this topic.

inaccurate_statement: Rep. Nunn has publicly praised Iowa as a 'model for how workforce development and AI leadership can work hand in hand' in reference to data centers.
description: No record exists of Nunn making a direct statement about data center development specifically; dedicated research found this to be a confirmed gap in his public record, despite this being a live district issue involving major Microsoft and Meta data center buildouts. Presenting this specific quote as his stated position on data centers is unsupported.

inaccurate_statement: Nunn has caveated his support for data centers by stating that development must protect consumers from energy rate hikes.
description: No direct statement from Nunn tying data-center development to consumer electricity-rate protections has been found despite dedicated searches of his campaign site, House office site, and news coverage; this is a confirmed gap, not a documented position, and presenting it as his stated caveat is unsupported.

inaccurate_statement: Zach Nunn supports banning congressional stock trading.
description: No record shows Zach Nunn supporting a ban on congressional stock trading. This proposal is actually part of Sarah Trone Garriott's own platform — her first general-election TV ad calls for banning stock trading by politicians, and she has criticized Nunn's accessibility record, not aligned him with this reform. Attributing this position to Nunn appears to be a misattribution.

inaccurate_statement: Marco Battaglia (Libertarian) is presented as a current candidate on the ballot without qualification
description: Marco Battaglia was removed from the Iowa ballot by the State Objections Panel over a legal name discrepancy and then ended his campaign entirely in early August 2026 due to a medical emergency. The Libertarian Party of Iowa nominated a replacement candidate (Jacob Heard, per other records) afterward. Presenting Battaglia as simply a current candidate is outdated.

inaccurate_statement: Nunn 'Supports funding for vocational education, bringing shop classes back to high schools, and training more workers in fields like plumbing, electrical work, and construction'
description: There is no documented direct statement from Nunn's campaign specifically calling for 'bringing shop classes back to high schools' or training in plumbing/electrical/construction trades. His documented small-business and jobs record centers on manufacturing (16,000+ IA-03 jobs), tax provisions (Section 179 expensing, small-business deduction), and the Rural Microentrepreneur Assistance Program Act — not a specific vocational-education/shop-class platform plank. This presents an unverified, specific policy mechanism as his stated position without hedging.

inaccurate_statement: Marco Battaglia (Libertarian) is presented as a current candidate on the ballot without qualification
description: Marco Battaglia was removed from the Iowa ballot by the State Objections Panel over a legal name discrepancy and then ended his campaign entirely in early August 2026 due to a medical emergency. The Libertarian Party of Iowa nominated a replacement candidate (Jacob Heard, per other records) afterward. Presenting Battaglia as simply a current candidate is outdated.

inaccurate_statement: He has co-sponsored the bipartisan Dignity Act, which proposes mandating nationwide E-Verify, adding physical barriers to the southern border, and creating a legal framework for foreign workers and employers.
description: No record exists in Zach Nunn's documented legislative activity of him co-sponsoring a bill called the 'Dignity Act.' His confirmed immigration-related legislative actions include supporting the Laken Riley Act, the Secure the Border Act, and a proposal allowing certain undocumented immigrants (including DACA recipients) a path to permanent residency without citizenship after background checks and restitution. There is no support for the specific claim that he co-sponsored a bill with this name and these specific provisions (nationwide E-Verify mandate, physical barriers, foreign-worker legal framework).

inaccurate_statement: Sarah Trone Garriott centers her campaign on the rising cost of utilities specifically
description: Search results and her campaign website's Issues page show that Sarah Trone Garriott's campaign centers broadly on lowering costs for working families — including health care, prescription drugs, child care, and 'everyday necessities' — alongside other issues like public education, reproductive freedom, and government reform. There is no evidence that utilities specifically (electric/gas bills) are a distinct or central focus of her campaign; no dedicated 'utilities' issue page or utility-specific messaging was found on her official site or in news coverage. Coverage instead describes her campaign as 'centered on health care and affordability' generally. The claim narrows her broad affordability platform to a specific sub-issue (utilities) that isn't substantiated as a defining campaign focus, making it misleading rather than a fabrication of a checkable fact.

inaccurate_statement: Zach Nunn advocates for banning congressional stock trading
description: A pledge to ban congressional stock trading is part of Sarah Trone Garriott's campaign platform (featured in her first general-election TV ad), not a position documented for Zach Nunn. No record exists of Nunn advocating for a stock-trading ban.

inaccurate_statement: Nunn introduced the Protecting Rural Telehealth Access Act to permanently extend Medicare telehealth options so rural patients can see specialists without long drives
description: The Protecting Rural Telehealth Access Act (H.R. 7444) was introduced by Rep. Chris Pappas (D-NH); Nunn is a cosponsor, not the bill's introducer.

inaccurate_statement: Nunn has pledged support for increased federal cancer research funding targeting over $50 billion nationally
description: Nunn's documented cancer-research funding record involves a $150 million increase in cancer-research appropriations and $37 million specifically for Wayne County Hospital cancer care, and separately a $50 billion Rural Health Transformation Program that is not specific to cancer research. There is no record of him pledging or targeting $50 billion nationally for cancer research specifically; this appears to conflate the unrelated $50 billion rural health program with his cancer-research funding advocacy.

inaccurate_statement: Trone Garriott's platform emphasizes capitalizing fully on historic federal programs like the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law and advocates directing multi-billion dollar highway and bridge allocations toward local projects.
description: No dedicated infrastructure plan or statement tying her platform to the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law has been found; she has only made a general statement that residents want safe roads and bridges that need to be paid for. Presenting a specific policy mechanism involving the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law as her stated position, without hedging that this is inferred, misrepresents a confirmed gap in her documented platform.

inaccurate_statement: Trone Garriott emphasizes that Iowa historically ranks among the states with the highest number of structurally deficient bridges.
description: No statement from Trone Garriott citing a specific structurally-deficient-bridges ranking has been documented; her roads/bridges position is limited to a general statement about wanting safe roads and bridges, not this specific statistic.

inaccurate_statement: Trone Garriott's focus is on combining physical road repair with modernizing regional transit networks to lower operational costs for suburban commuters and rural agricultural transport lines, viewing highway repairs as a job-creation engine.
description: This specific transit-modernization/job-creation mechanism is not documented as her stated position; her actual record shows no detailed infrastructure plan beyond a general statement about needing to pay for safe roads and bridges.

inaccurate_statement: Trone Garriott's recent action on roads/highways is described as having 'sponsored state-level alignment with federal grants.'
description: No record exists of Trone Garriott sponsoring legislation aligning state and federal infrastructure grants; her documented record on roads/bridges consists only of general remarks, not a specific legislative action of this kind.

inaccurate_statement: Trone Garriott's key infrastructure priority is described as 'Eliminating structurally deficient bridges & expanding jobs.'
description: This specific priority framing is not supported by any documented statement from her; her roads/bridges position is limited to general remarks about the need to pay for safe roads and bridges.

inaccurate_statement: The Democratic platform centers on utilizing federal allocations of approximately $3.4 billion for Iowa highways and $432 million for bridge repairs to systematically address structurally deficient bridges and rural roadways across the district, as Trone Garriott's stated plan.
description: No detailed infrastructure plan or dollar-figure-specific roads/bridges proposal has been found attributed to Sarah Trone Garriott's own platform; she has only made general statements that residents want safe roads and bridges and that these need to be funded, without a documented specific plan citing these figures. Presenting these specific numbers as her stated platform position, without noting they are not confirmed as her own direct statement, misrepresents the state of her documented platform on this issue.

inaccurate_statement: The landmark Bipartisan Infrastructure Law is one 'which Nunn voted against.'
description: The Bipartisan Infrastructure Law (Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act) passed the House in November 2021. Zach Nunn did not take office in the U.S. House until January 2023, so he could not have cast a vote on this bill at all — he was not yet a member of Congress. Attributing a vote against it to him is a factual error about his federal voting record.

inaccurate_statement: Zach Nunn authored the Crime Victims Fund Stabilization Act to redirect recovered fraud funds into support services for victims of domestic abuse and violent crime.
description: The Crime Victims Fund Stabilization Act (H.R. 909) was sponsored by Rep. Ann Wagner (R-MO), with co-leads including Reps. Nathaniel Moran, Debbie Dingell, Stephanie Bice, and Jim Costa. Multiple independent trackers, including the bill's official record, do not list Zach Nunn as sponsor or lead author; while his office describes him as having 'led' the bill, this is contradicted by the official record and outside tracking organizations.

inaccurate_statement: Zach Nunn pushes to crack down on prescription drug prices as part of his cost-of-living platform.
description: No record exists of Zach Nunn making prescription-drug-pricing a stated platform plank. His documented affordability messaging centers on tax cuts, deregulation, and reducing 'overspending, overregulation, and inflation,' not drug-price crackdowns. This position more closely resembles Trone Garriott's documented proposal to let Medicare negotiate drug prices, suggesting a misattribution.

inaccurate_statement: Sarah Trone Garriott advocates for stronger accountability and oversight for large livestock facilities and industrial agriculture to reduce pollution at the source.
description: No direct statement from Trone Garriott calling for specific oversight/accountability measures targeting large livestock facilities or industrial agriculture was found; her documented water-quality position is about protecting clean water broadly and working with farmers on conservation practices, not a livestock-facility regulatory specific mechanism presented without hedging.

inaccurate_statement: Sarah Trone Garriott co-sponsored state bills like the 'Clean Water for Iowa Act' to mandate pollution monitoring and restore state-level water testing.
description: No record exists of a bill called the 'Clean Water for Iowa Act' being co-sponsored by Trone Garriott. Her documented legislative and campaign water-quality record involves criticizing the adequacy of the $25 million nitrate-removal funding and pledging to protect clean water and work with farmers on conservation, not sponsorship of a named mandatory-testing bill by this title.

inaccurate_statement: Nunn's permitting reform amendment fast-tracks state-led water quality projects 'without imposing new mandates on private landowners.'
description: The knowledge base describes the PERMIT Act amendment as creating 'a state-led pilot program to accelerate Iowa water quality projects,' but there is no documented statement that this specifically avoids imposing new mandates on private landowners — that detail is not supported by the available record.

inaccurate_statement: Nunn introduced bipartisan legislation to help disadvantaged communities access federal funds to replace toxic lead water pipes.
description: No record exists of Zach Nunn introducing or sponsoring lead-pipe-replacement legislation; his documented water-quality record centers on the districtwide monitoring network funding and the PERMIT Act clean-water amendment, not lead pipe replacement.

inaccurate_statement: Nunn favors cooperative incentives and voluntary conservation tools for farmers rather than heavy federal mandates (framed as his water-quality approach).
description: There is no documented statement from Nunn framing his water-quality approach specifically as favoring voluntary conservation incentives over mandates; his confirmed water-quality actions are the monitoring-network funding and the PERMIT Act amendment, not a stated voluntary-vs-mandate philosophy.

inaccurate_statement: Trone Garriott identifies lowering utility bills as one of her immediate priorities
description: No direct statement from Trone Garriott's federal campaign specifically addresses household electricity or utility bills; this is a confirmed gap in her documented platform, which instead frames clean energy investment generally rather than a utility-bill-specific pledge. Presenting this as one of her stated immediate priorities without hedging overstates the documented record.

inaccurate_statement: Nunn proposes cracking down on Big Pharma and plans to directly target pharmaceutical companies to drive down prescription drug costs
description: There is no record of Zach Nunn proposing to target pharmaceutical companies or 'crack down on Big Pharma' as part of his cost-of-living platform. His documented healthcare-cost approach centers on ACA/Medicaid policy, rural health funding, and cancer research, not pharmaceutical-industry enforcement.

inaccurate_statement: Nunn proposes banning Congressional stock trading to reduce drug costs
description: Banning stock trading by politicians is a position associated with Sarah Trone Garriott's campaign (featured in her first general-election TV ad), not with Zach Nunn. No record exists of Nunn proposing a congressional stock-trading ban.

inaccurate_statement: Zach Nunn promotes a bipartisan housing bill to build a skilled local workforce—such as plumbers and electricians—to lower home construction costs.
description: Web searches confirm Zach Nunn has introduced and promoted several bipartisan housing bills (Rural Housing Service Reform Act, Promote Affordable Rural Housing Act, and provisions within the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act), but these focus on modernizing USDA rural housing programs, cutting red tape, reducing permitting delays, and expanding manufactured housing and home-repair loans — not on training a skilled local workforce of plumbers and electricians. The specific policy of funding workforce/skills training (plumbers, electricians) at community colleges to address the construction labor shortage and lower housing costs matches the CONSTRUCTS Act, a bill introduced by Senators Jacky Rosen (D-NV) and Marsha Blackburn (R-TN) — with no evidence found connecting Nunn to that legislation. Separately, Nunn has secured federal grants for skilled-trades training labs (e.g., $900,000 for Iowa Western Community College electrical/plumbing labs), but these are workforce-development grants, not a 'housing bill.' The claim thus conflates a real but differently attributed policy concept with Nunn's actual (differently focused) housing legislation, making it a misattribution rather than a wholesale fabrication. Because Nunn does have substantial, genuine bipartisan housing legislative work, and the core theme (bipartisan effort to lower home construction costs) is broadly true even if this particular workforce-training detail is misattributed, this is a minor rather than critical inaccuracy.

inaccurate_statement: Rising fertilizer costs, worsened by Middle East conflicts and global shipping bottlenecks, are fueling fears of lower crop yields and tighter profit margins
description: The underlying substance of the claim — that rising fertilizer costs, worsened by Middle East conflict and shipping bottlenecks through the Strait of Hormuz, are threatening crop yields and farm margins — is well-documented and true in agricultural press coverage. However, no evidence ties this specific claim/statement to Sarah Trone Garriott. Notably, the only Iowa political figure found making public remarks specifically on this fertilizer/Middle East/Strait of Hormuz disruption topic was her opponent, Republican Rep. Zach Nunn, who warned of potential 'mass famine' from fertilizer access issues. Trone Garriott's documented agriculture remarks instead focus on the farm bill, cover crops, and no-till incentives. This appears to be a general/generic claim inserted without clear grounding in anything she actually said, and it risks being confused with her opponent's statement on the same topic.

inaccurate_statement: Zach Nunn is committed to supporting $51.3 billion in new federal cancer research funding.
description: Nunn's documented cancer-research funding statements reference $128 million he personally fought for and a $150 million increase in cancer-research appropriations, not a $51.3 billion commitment. No source supports this figure, which appears to be a fabrication that dramatically overstates his actual documented position.

inaccurate_statement: Zach Nunn highlights his role on the appropriations committee, arguing that Congress controls the "purse strings"
description: Nunn's committee assignments are House Financial Services, House Agriculture, and the House Select Committee on the Chinese Communist Party — he does not sit on the Appropriations Committee.

inaccurate_statement: Trone Garriott emphasizes addressing environmental contributors to cancer common in the district, such as high radon levels and nitrate pollution in water.
description: Available research found no direct statement from Trone Garriott linking nitrate or pesticide exposure to cancer causation specifically, despite this being a prominent Iowa research topic, and no mention of radon appears in her documented statements at all. Her water-quality advocacy is tied to general nitrate contamination policy, not framed as a cancer-prevention environmental plank.

inaccurate_statement: Trone Garriott and her party argue that massive federal investments via the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law are the most effective way to address decaying roads and bridges while simultaneously creating thousands of good-paying union jobs across the state, as a holistic public framework emphasizing sustained public investment in roads, transit, and clean water to protect rural communities
description: No statement in Trone Garriott's documented platform or record specifically frames federal infrastructure investment, job creation via infrastructure spending, or a 'holistic public framework' protecting rural communities as her stated position. Her actual, confirmed record on roads/bridges is limited to a general statement that residents want 'safe' roads and bridges that 'need to be paid for' — no detailed plan, no specific mention of the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law, job creation framing, or rural-protection framing was found despite dedicated searching. This response presents a detailed, specific policy mechanism as her own position without any hedging that it is inferred from generic party alignment.

inaccurate_statement: The Bipartisan Infrastructure Law delivered roughly $3.4 billion for Iowa highways and $432 million for bridge repairs
description: This specific dollar-figure breakdown for Iowa highway and bridge funding under the Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act is not verifiable against either candidate's documented record and appears to be an unsupported statistic not tied to either candidate's own statements.

inaccurate_statement: The Bipartisan Infrastructure Law delivered roughly $3.4 billion for Iowa highways and $432 million for bridge repairs
description: This specific dollar-figure breakdown for Iowa highway and bridge funding under the Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act is not verifiable against either candidate's documented record and appears to be an unsupported statistic not tied to either candidate's own statements.

inaccurate_statement: Nunn advocates for expanding 'market-to-road bridges' specifically through Farm Bill integration, linking agricultural security to hard infrastructure
description: Nunn's documented roads/bridges record consists of secured Community Project Funding for specific named projects (Ringgold County's P33 corridor, a Highway 141/NW Towner Drive interchange, Alice's Road reconstruction, White Pole Road) framed as 'Strengthening Iowa's Farm-to-Market Routes,' not a Farm Bill-linked 'market-to-road bridges' initiative as described.

inaccurate_statement: Nunn collaborates with Polk County on municipal transportation and airport upgrades as part of his infrastructure focus
description: No record exists of Nunn's infrastructure record involving Polk County airport upgrades; his documented road/bridge funding is tied to specific rural corridor and bridge projects in Ringgold, Guthrie, and Madison counties, not airport or Polk County municipal transportation initiatives.

inaccurate_statement: Trone Garriott's platform emphasizes maximizing state allocations from the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law, including approximately $3.4 billion for Iowa highway repairs and $432 million for fixing structurally deficient bridges
description: No direct statement or detailed infrastructure plan citing these specific dollar figures for Iowa highway/bridge funding was found in Trone Garriott's platform materials; her roads/bridges position is limited to general statements that roads and bridges need to be 'safe' and are 'responsibilities that need to be paid for,' with no detailed plan or specific funding figures documented.

inaccurate_statement: Trone Garriott favors an expansive definition of infrastructure, seeking to fund road and bridge repairs alongside rural broadband expansion and water quality modernization
description: While Trone Garriott has a documented water-quality platform, no record exists of her tying road/bridge funding to a combined broadband-and-water-quality infrastructure platform; her roads/bridges position itself is documented as a general, undetailed statement, not a comprehensive multi-sector infrastructure plan.

inaccurate_statement: Trone Garriott's roads/bridges plan is described as 'Robust federal investment and formula grants' with 'Supports large-scale, bipartisan federal packages to guarantee billions for local transit and bridges' presented as her stated position
description: No direct statement from Trone Garriott's campaign lays out a detailed roads/bridges plan; she has only made general remarks that residents want safe roads and bridges and that these are responsibilities that need to be paid for. Presenting a specific, detailed federal-investment mechanism as her own concrete platform position, without hedging that this is inferred from generic party alignment, goes beyond what is documented.

inaccurate_statement: Nunn's roads/bridges approach is characterized as fiscal restraint, opposing federal spending, and relying on state-managed budgets like the Iowa Transportation Improvement Program, with no mention of his actual delivery record
description: Nunn's actual documented roads/bridges record is one of securing specific federal Community Project Funding earmarks for IA-03 projects, not opposing federal spending on infrastructure — $2M for Ringgold County's P33 corridor rehab, $500K for a Highway 141/NW Towner Drive interchange in Johnston, $1M for Alice's Road reconstruction, $500K for White Pole Road, and a prior $1.5M Madison County bridge replacement, all framed by his own office as 'Strengthening Iowa's Farm-to-Market Routes.' The response's framing of him as generally opposing federal infrastructure spending and relying only on state-level mechanisms omits this actual, confirmed record of pursuing and touting targeted federal infrastructure dollars.

inaccurate_statement: Nunn's platform centers on countering federal government overspending, lowering costs for families, and rooting out waste and fraud, applied here specifically as his roads/bridges strategy
description: While Nunn does use general 'overspending/overregulation/inflation' framing in his cost-of-living messaging, there is no documented statement applying this fiscal-restraint framing specifically to a roads/bridges plan; his actual confirmed roads/bridges record consists of pursuing targeted federal earmarks, which cuts against characterizing his roads/bridges approach as opposition to federal spending mechanisms.

inaccurate_statement: Zach Nunn advocates for... alongside banning congressional stock trading
description: A ban on congressional stock trading is a position associated with Sarah Trone Garriott's campaign (her TV ad calls for banning stock trading by politicians), not a documented position of Zach Nunn. Attributing this to Nunn is a misattribution.

inaccurate_statement: Nunn's affordability plan includes 'Congressional Accountability: Connects government spending and trust to economic stability, advocating for a ban on congressional stock trading'
description: There is no record of Zach Nunn advocating for a congressional stock-trading ban. It is Sarah Trone Garriott's campaign that has made banning stock trading by politicians part of her platform (featured in her first general-election TV ad), and Iowa Senate Democrats, including Trone Garriott, introduced a bill to ban lawmaker stock trading. This appears to attribute her position to Nunn.

inaccurate_statement: Zach Nunn supports banning congressional stock trading to combat corruption
description: There is no record of Zach Nunn supporting a ban on congressional stock trading. This is actually a position associated with Sarah Trone Garriott's campaign, whose first general-election TV ad calls for requiring town halls and banning stock trading by politicians, and who has framed a related term-limits/stock-trading bill as one she introduced in the Iowa Senate.

inaccurate_statement: Zach Nunn promotes a bipartisan housing bill aimed at training skilled trade workers to lower home building costs
description: Search results show Zach Nunn's actual housing legislation (the Rural Housing Service Reform Act and provisions in the Housing for the 21st Century Act) focuses on cutting red tape, modernizing USDA rural housing programs, and easing regulatory barriers — not on training skilled trade workers. A bill matching the claim's description — training skilled construction trade workers to help lower housing costs — is the CONSTRUCTS Act, sponsored by Senators Marsha Blackburn and Jacky Rosen, not Nunn. Separately, Nunn does lead a real workforce/apprenticeship bill (the PARTNERS Act) involving skilled trades training, but it is not branded or promoted as a 'housing bill' and is not explicitly framed as lowering home building costs. The claim thus conflates distinct initiatives and misattributes a bill concept that doesn't match any actual Nunn-led housing bill, though the broader theme (Nunn supporting both housing affordability efforts and skilled-trades workforce training) is genuine, making this a narrow misattribution rather than a wholesale fabrication.

inaccurate_statement: Sarah Trone Garriott's platform includes investing in technology and personnel to stop drug smuggling and human trafficking at the border
description: Trone Garriott's documented immigration platform calls for secure borders, streamlined legal pathways, Dreamer protection, and trafficking prevention generally, but no specific statement about investing in technology and personnel at the border for drug/human trafficking interdiction is documented.

inaccurate_statement: Zach Nunn supports legislation like H.R. 2 to increase border restrictions
description: No record exists of Nunn specifically supporting or citing H.R. 2 (the Secure the Border Act). His documented immigration record includes support for the Secure the Border Act's provisions on asylum processing and enforcement, and the Laken Riley Act, but this specific bill citation is not confirmed in available material.

inaccurate_statement: Zach Nunn advocates for reinstating the 'Remain in Mexico' program
description: No record exists of Nunn specifically calling for reinstatement of the 'Remain in Mexico' program. His documented immigration positions focus on border security funding, ending catch-and-release, physical barriers, tighter asylum rules, and linking enforcement to fentanyl trafficking, but this specific named policy is not confirmed in available material.

inaccurate_statement: Zach Nunn advocates for increasing pay and resources for Border Patrol agents
description: This specific claim about Border Patrol agent pay is not documented in available material about Nunn's immigration platform, which instead emphasizes border security resources, physical barriers, and enforcement funding generally.

inaccurate_statement: Nunn explicitly committed to supporting $51.3 billion in federal funds for new cancer research.
description: Zach Nunn's documented cancer-funding statements reference $128 million he personally fought for in targeted cancer research and a $150 million increase in cancer-research appropriations, not a $51.3 billion commitment. No source ties him to a figure anywhere near this scale, and this appears to be a fabricated or garbled statistic.

inaccurate_statement: Nunn has committed to supporting $51.3 billion in new federal cancer research funding
description: Nunn's documented cancer-research funding claims involve $128 million he says he personally fought for and a $150 million increase in cancer-research appropriations, plus $37 million for a specific hospital's cancer care — figures orders of magnitude smaller than the $51.3 billion cited here. No record supports a $51.3 billion commitment attributed to Nunn.

inaccurate_statement: Trone Garriott emphasizes stricter accountability for major polluters, addressing industrial agricultural runoff, and reversing rollbacks on environmental safeguards, with supporters believing she will push for stronger federal oversight, mandatory pollution reduction targets, and increased funding for public health research and state water testing systems.
description: Trone Garriott's documented water-quality position is limited to pledging to 'protect clean water and expand access to public lands,' working with farmers on conservation practices, and criticizing the $25 million nitrate-removal funding as not solving the underlying problem. No direct statement exists of her calling for mandatory pollution reduction targets, stricter accountability targeting major polluters specifically, or reversing named regulatory rollbacks — this response presents specific policy mechanisms as her stated position without the hedging the record supports.

inaccurate_statement: Nunn introduced the Safe Drinking Water for Disadvantaged Communities Act to help direct lead pipe replacement grants to local towns.
description: No record exists of Zach Nunn introducing or being associated with a bill called the Safe Drinking Water for Disadvantaged Communities Act. His documented water-quality record centers on a $500,000 districtwide flood/drought and groundwater/nitrate monitoring network investment and a clean-water amendment in the PERMIT Act creating a state-led pilot program — nothing about lead pipe replacement grants for disadvantaged communities.

inaccurate_statement: Trone Garriott is described as having been 'an executive at a food bank network.'
description: Sarah Trone Garriott's documented role was Coordinator of Interfaith Engagement for the Des Moines Area Religious Council (DMARC) Food Pantry Network, a coordinator position, not an executive role at a food bank network.

inaccurate_statement: Trone Garriott highlights her experience as 'an executive at an Iowa food bank network' as giving her direct understanding of grocery costs.
description: Sarah Trone Garriott's documented food-security role was Coordinator of Interfaith Engagement for the Des Moines Area Religious Council (DMARC) Food Pantry Network, not an executive position at a food bank network. Describing this coordinator role as 'an executive' overstates her actual title and level of authority.

inaccurate_statement: Trone Garriott's platform focuses on lowering operational and living expenses for working families such as electric bills.
description: No direct statement has been found from Sarah Trone Garriott's federal campaign specifically addressing household electricity bills; this is a confirmed research gap, not a documented position. Presenting a specific electric-bill-lowering mechanism as her stated position without hedging overstates what is actually on record.

inaccurate_statement: Trone Garriott's main legislative focus includes 'capping healthcare and utility costs.'
description: There is no documented statement from Trone Garriott's campaign proposing to 'cap' utility costs specifically; this is a confirmed gap in her public record, and presenting it as a specific stated legislative focus without qualification misrepresents the state of her platform.

inaccurate_statement: Sponsored the Farm Transitions Act to lower barriers to farm ownership and access to credit for beginning farmers.
description: No record exists of Nunn sponsoring a bill called the 'Farm Transitions Act.' His documented beginning-farmer legislation is the Next Generation of Farmers Act, which reduces the experience requirement for USDA financing eligibility from three years to one and allows relevant education/experience to count — a different bill name and mechanism than described.

inaccurate_statement: Nunn's Farm Bill platform incorporates 17 specific policy priorities
description: Nunn's documented Farm Bill record cites 21 provisions/wins he championed in the House Agriculture Committee's Farm Bill, not 17.

inaccurate_statement: Zach Nunn champions active federal intervention in trade corridors, such as proposing a 'humanitarian corridor' through the Strait of Hormuz to guarantee uninterrupted access to lower-cost foreign fertilizers
description: No record exists of Nunn proposing a 'humanitarian corridor' through the Strait of Hormuz or any fertilizer-supply-chain intervention of this kind. His documented Iran-war-related record consists of voting against multiple War Powers Resolutions to end U.S. hostilities with Iran, not a fertilizer-corridor initiative. This appears to be an invented policy claim.

inaccurate_statement: Nunn proposed working with the U.S. Treasury to establish "humanitarian corridors" through volatile regions like the Strait of Hormuz to ensure essential fertilizer inputs reach American fields without disruption.
description: No record exists of Zach Nunn proposing 'humanitarian corridors' through the Strait of Hormuz or working with the U.S. Treasury on fertilizer-supply-chain protection. His documented farm-income platform centers on the House Farm Bill, E15/ethanol access, a Taiwan trade mission on tariffs, USDA crop insurance rules, and the Crop Insurance for Future Farmers Act — not Strait of Hormuz corridors or Treasury coordination on fertilizer imports. This appears to be an invented policy proposal not found in any of his platform materials, press releases, or news coverage.

inaccurate_statement: His platform aligns with defending global markets for Iowa commodities, focusing on international pressure strategies and sanctions to ensure foreign trade conflicts do not choke crop exports.
description: There is no documented statement or platform plank from Zach Nunn framing his agriculture policy around 'international pressure strategies and sanctions' to protect crop exports. His actual documented trade-related agriculture positions involve a Taiwan trade mission seeking tariff elimination on Iowa beef/dairy/corn and support for ethanol access, not a sanctions-based export-defense strategy.

inaccurate_statement: Zach Nunn introduced the Protect Small Business from Excessive Paperwork Act to delay and simplify complex federal reporting deadlines
description: The Protect Small Business(es) from Excessive Paperwork Act that Nunn introduced/co-led extends the deadline for pre-2024 companies to file beneficial ownership information reports with FinCEN; it is broadly accurate to describe this as delaying and simplifying a federal reporting deadline, so this framing is largely consistent with the documented bill content, though it should not be conflated with the separate 'excessive red tape reporting mechanism' fabrication found elsewhere.

inaccurate_statement: Prior to his congressional tenure, Nunn owned a small marketing business in Iowa, offering him firsthand insight into local economic hurdles.
description: There is no record of Zach Nunn owning a small marketing business. His documented pre-congressional career consists of nearly 20 years in the U.S. Air Force/Iowa Air National Guard as an intelligence officer, an adjunct professorship in cybersecurity at Drake University, a National Security Council staff role under Trump, a director of cybersecurity policy position at ODNI, and service in the Iowa House and Iowa Senate. This business-ownership claim appears to be fabricated and would materially mislead a reader about his actual professional background.

inaccurate_statement: Sarah Trone Garriott and her party colleagues are adopting a more populist approach aligned with growing public skepticism toward large-scale, unchecked data center expansions, implying this is her own stated position
description: No confirmed record exists of Sarah Trone Garriott personally commenting on data center development at all, despite dedicated repeated searches through August 2026. Her campaign platform contains no statement on this topic. The response presents a specific policy stance on data centers as her own position without any hedging, when in fact this is a documented gap in her public record.

inaccurate_statement: Zach Nunn maintains that the federal government should not override local zoning decisions for or against data centers, and has embraced the technology boom while caveating that developers should not drive up consumer energy costs
description: No confirmed record exists of Zach Nunn making any statement about data center development, zoning authority, or electricity costs tied to data centers, despite dedicated repeated searches through August 2026, including of his campaign site, congressional office site, and news coverage. This is a documented, confirmed gap in his public record, not a known position. The response presents detailed, specific policy mechanisms as his stated views without any hedging.

inaccurate_statement: Sarah Trone Garriott's platform focuses on strengthening consumer protections, ending generous corporate tax handouts, ensuring high transparency regarding water and energy consumption, and implementing strict rules so tech conglomerates do not drive up utility bills for everyday residents (as her stated data-center position)
description: No confirmed record exists of Sarah Trone Garriott publicly commenting on data center development at all, despite this being a live local issue given the major Microsoft/Meta data-center buildout in the Des Moines metro portion of her district. Dedicated research repeatedly found this to be a genuine gap in her public record, not a documented position. Presenting a detailed, specific policy mechanism as her stated platform without hedging that it is inferred is not supported.

inaccurate_statement: Zach Nunn caveated his support for AI/data-center growth by stating that developers and utilities must work with local communities to prevent consumer energy costs from skyrocketing, and that the federal government should not override local zoning decisions on this
description: No confirmed statement exists of Zach Nunn addressing data-center development, ratepayer cost-shifting, or zoning/federal-preemption concerns related to data centers. Dedicated searches of his campaign site, congressional office site, and news coverage found this to be a genuine, confirmed gap in his record. The specific position attributed to him here is not supported by any documented statement.

inaccurate_statement: Sarah Trone Garriott's platform aligns with broader Iowa Democratic efforts to target the data center boom, addressing rising utility costs, water consumption, and tax breaks for tech corporations.
description: No confirmed record exists of Trone Garriott publicly commenting on data centers generally, despite this being a live local issue with a major Microsoft/Meta data-center buildout in the district. This was reconfirmed as a genuine gap even after a dedicated verification sweep of her campaign issues site, social media, and news search. Presenting a specific policy stance on data centers as her platform position is unsupported.

inaccurate_statement: Zach Nunn has publicly supported the data center growth, calling Iowa a 'model for how workforce development and AI leadership can work hand in hand.'
description: No record exists of Nunn making any statement on data center development specifically. Despite dedicated searches of his campaign site, House office site, and news coverage, this was confirmed as a genuine gap with 'no direct statement found' on data centers, ratepayer cost-shifting, or the major Microsoft and Meta data-center buildout in his district. Attributing a specific direct quote to him on this topic is a fabrication.

inaccurate_statement: During the confrontation, Nunn claimed he could not talk because he was walking with a 'constituent' and needed to protect their privacy, but reports later revealed he was actually walking with a journalist, not a resident of his district.
description: The documented incident involves Nunn physically striking/shoving NOTUS reporter Reese Gorman after being asked about rural Iowa hospital closures tied to Medicaid cuts. There is no record of Nunn claiming he was walking with a 'constituent' whose privacy he needed to protect, or of this specific 'misleading excuse' framing; this detail does not appear in the documented account of the incident.

inaccurate_statement: Video footage captured Nunn swatting a phone out of the hand of a DCCC candidate tracker; Nunn initially claimed he was walking with a constituent whose privacy he was protecting, though subsequent reports identified the individual as a journalist
description: The documented altercation involved Nunn physically striking/shoving NOTUS reporter Reese Gorman on a Washington, D.C. street in late July 2026 after being asked about rural Iowa hospital closures tied to Medicaid cuts. There is no record of the incident involving swatting a phone from a 'DCCC candidate tracker,' an initial claim that the person was a constituent, or an admission the reaction 'was not his best action' — this appears to conflate or misdescribe the documented incident.

inaccurate_statement: Marco Battaglia alleged that Nunn, his campaign consultant, and Robert F. Kennedy Jr. personally visited or called him to pressure him into withdrawing from the race
description: Reporting confirms Nunn and his consultant Annie Kuhle visited Battaglia to urge him to withdraw, and that Kuhle and Nunn's deputy chief of staff filed the ballot challenge against him. There is no record of Robert F. Kennedy Jr. being involved in this episode in any way.

inaccurate_statement: Trone Garriott has centered her platform on structural reforms that would mandate standard public town halls for elected congressional representatives
description: Her documented position is that her first general-election TV ad calls for requiring town halls (and banning stock trading by politicians) as one campaign message, not that mandating congressional town halls is a centerpiece structural reform of her broader platform. Describing this as a core platform-defining 'structural reform' overstates a single ad talking point.

inaccurate_statement: Sarah Trone Garriott held 21 open town halls across all 21 counties in the district within a single month
description: Her documented town-hall tour is described as covering all 21 IA-03 counties 'in under 30 days,' but there is no record specifying that exactly 21 town halls were held (one per county) or characterizing them as strictly 'open town halls' in that specific framing; the '21 open town halls' figure with one-per-county precision is an unsupported specific detail beyond what is documented.

inaccurate_statement: In mid-2026, Trone Garriott hosted 21 public town halls across all 21 counties in the district
description: Her documented town-hall tour was conducted as a state senator, described as a self-run 21-county tour completed 'in under 30 days,' not specifically framed or dated as a mid-2026 federal-campaign event with exactly 21 separate town halls held one per county. The general fact that she toured all 21 counties is accurate, but the specific 'mid-2026, 21 town halls' framing is not supported as stated.

inaccurate_statement: Nunn's office states he has conducted hundreds of private and localized listening sessions, open forums, and business visits across all 21 counties
description: Nunn's documented accessibility record consists of recurring monthly 'mobile office hours' and a June 2026 telephone town hall (a call-in listening session, not an in-person open forum), plus specific local visits tied to legislation/funding announcements. There is no documentation of 'hundreds' of private listening sessions and open forums across all 21 counties, and the June 2026 event was specifically a telephone town hall, not an in-person 'open forum,' a distinction the record treats as meaningful.

inaccurate_statement: Sarah Trone Garriott is running her campaign entirely on grassroots and individual donations
description: Her FEC filings show significant contributions from PACs and other committees (over $439,000), including labor unions, EMILY's List, and Human Rights Campaign PAC, plus joint-fundraising transfers — not solely grassroots and individual donations. While none of these are traditional corporate PACs, describing the campaign as funded 'entirely' on grassroots/individual money overstates the actual donor mix.

inaccurate_statement: Individual contributions drive the vast majority of fundraising for both campaigns
description: This is true for Trone Garriott, whose individual contributions ($4.76M) made up about 90% of her $5.29M total, but not for Nunn, whose individual contributions were only about $1.01M of his $4.87M total (roughly 21%), with the rest coming from PAC/committee money ($1.72M) and transfers from other authorized committees ($2.1M). Individual donations were not the majority source for Nunn's fundraising.

inaccurate_statement: The vast majority of campaign funding for both candidates comes from individual contributions
description: This is accurate for Trone Garriott (individuals contributed roughly $4.76 million of her $5.29 million total, about 90%), but not for Nunn: his FEC filing shows individual contributions of only about $1.01 million out of $4.87 million total receipts, with PACs/other committees contributing $1.72 million and transfers from other authorized committees contributing over $2.09 million — individual donations are not the majority source for Nunn's fundraising.

inaccurate_statement: Nonpartisan legislative tracking and bipartisan scorecards generally rank Zach Nunn as more ideologically moderate relative to his national party than his Democratic challenger, Sarah Trone Garriott
description: Nunn's own office cites a 'Bridge Grades' scorecard ranking him 3rd-most-bipartisan House member based on cosponsorship breadth, but an independent outlet separately reports his floor-vote alignment with House GOP leadership rose from ~80% to ~95% between 2023 and 2025 — a mixed, non-equivalent set of metrics that should not be flattened into a single 'more moderate' conclusion. Additionally, Trone Garriott has no federal voting record at all, since she has never served in Congress, so there is no comparable 'bipartisan scorecard' by which the two could be directly ranked against each other on moderation. The response presents a settled comparative ranking that the underlying record does not actually support.

inaccurate_statement: Nunn received strong support from House Majority Leader Steve Scalise
description: No record exists of House Majority Leader Steve Scalise providing endorsement or campaign support to Zach Nunn. The documented endorsements and high-profile support for Nunn include President Trump, Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, and Vice President JD Vance, but Scalise is not mentioned in any of this material.

inaccurate_statement: According to the Lugar Center Bipartisan Index, Nunn ranks in the top tier for introducing and co-sponsoring bills alongside Democratic colleagues, specifically on rural housing and senior fraud protection
description: The bipartisanship scorecard Nunn's office cites is the 'Bridge Grades' nonpartisan scorecard ranking him 3rd-most-bipartisan House member, not the Lugar Center Bipartisan Index. No record ties a Lugar Center ranking or 'rural housing and senior fraud protection' co-sponsorship specifics to Nunn; this appears to conflate or invent a specific scorecard attribution.

inaccurate_statement: Sarah Trone Garriott was elected to the Iowa Senate in 2022
description: Sarah Trone Garriott was first elected to the Iowa Senate in November 2020 (Senate District 22), not 2022. She was redistricted and re-elected in 2022 to Senate District 14, but her initial election was in 2020.

inaccurate_statement: Sarah Trone Garriott has served as an Iowa State Senator since 2023.
description: Sarah Trone Garriott was elected to the Iowa Senate in November 2020 and took office in January 2021, not 2023. She was re-elected in 2022 and 2024.

inaccurate_statement: Sarah Trone Garriott worked as an executive at a regional food bank network.
description: Sarah Trone Garriott served as Coordinator of Interfaith Engagement for the Des Moines Area Religious Council (DMARC) Food Pantry Network, a coordinator role rather than an executive position, and this was a food pantry network rather than a regional food bank.

inaccurate_statement: Zach Nunn served in the Iowa Senate from 2018 to 2022.
description: Zach Nunn served in the Iowa Senate District 15 from 2019 to 2023, not 2018 to 2022.

inaccurate_statement: Zach Nunn served in the Iowa House of Representatives from 2014 to 2018.
description: Zach Nunn served in the Iowa House District 30 from 2015 to 2019, not 2014 to 2018.

inaccurate_statement: Sarah Trone Garriott has been serving in the Iowa Senate since 2023.
description: Trone Garriott was elected to the Iowa Senate in November 2020 and took office in January 2021, not 2023.

inaccurate_statement: Sarah Trone Garriott works as an executive for a food bank network.
description: Trone Garriott served as Coordinator of Interfaith Engagement for the Des Moines Area Religious Council (DMARC) Food Pantry Network, a coordination role, not a described executive position.

inaccurate_statement: Zach Nunn served in the Iowa House of Representatives from 2014 to 2018.
description: Nunn served in the Iowa House from 2015 to 2019, not 2014 to 2018.

inaccurate_statement: Zach Nunn served in the Iowa Senate from 2018 to 2022.
description: Nunn served in the Iowa Senate from 2019 to 2023, not 2018 to 2022.

inaccurate_statement: Zach Nunn has held elected office since 2014.
description: Nunn's first elected office (Iowa House) began in January 2015, not 2014.

inaccurate_statement: Sarah Trone Garriott has been Iowa State Senator for the 14th District since 2023, implying her Senate service began then.
description: Trone Garriott has served as a state senator continuously since January 2021, first representing Senate District 22 before being redistricted to District 14 in 2023 after re-election in 2022. Framing her Senate service as beginning in 2023 understates roughly two years of prior service.

inaccurate_statement: Sarah Trone Garriott is a nonprofit/food bank executive.
description: Trone Garriott served as Coordinator of Interfaith Engagement for the Des Moines Area Religious Council (DMARC) Food Pantry Network, a coordinator role, not a documented executive position.

inaccurate_statement: Zach Nunn served as Iowa State Senator from 2018 to 2022 and Iowa State Representative from 2014 to 2018.
description: Zach Nunn served in the Iowa House of Representatives from 2015 to 2019 and in the Iowa Senate from 2019 to 2023, not 2014–2018 and 2018–2022 as stated. The dates are each off by about one year.

inaccurate_statement: Zach Nunn is a 'combat aviator.'
description: Nunn's military record describes him as an airborne intelligence officer with three combat deployments, not as a combat aviator (pilot); the two roles are distinct, and describing him as an aviator overstates his documented role.

inaccurate_statement: A district court ruled in August 2026 that Libertarian candidates do not qualify for the November ballot
description: The Libertarian candidate Marco Battaglia was removed from the ballot by Iowa's State Objections Panel (a decision a Polk County judge upheld) over a legal name discrepancy, then dropped out entirely in early August 2026 due to a medical emergency; the Iowa Libertarian Party subsequently nominated a replacement (Jacob Heard). The claim that a court ruling in August 2026 determined Libertarians categorically 'do not qualify' for the ballot misrepresents this sequence of events and omits that a new Libertarian nominee was chosen.

inaccurate_statement: Sarah Trone Garriott's platform echoes concerns raised by Iowa legal experts about 'three strikes' mandates straining public finances and worsening prison overcrowding, and she champions bipartisan legislation focused on building trust between communities and law enforcement
description: No record exists of Sarah Trone Garriott commenting on an Iowa 'three strikes' sentencing bill or prison overcrowding specifically. Her documented public safety platform centers on background checks, safe storage, mental-health investment, and preventing crime rather than just responding to it — not a stated position on state sentencing-mandate reform or prison-overcrowding policy. This presents an unsupported specific policy mechanism as her own position.

inaccurate_statement: A district court ruled in August 2026 that Libertarian candidates do not qualify for the November ballot
description: The Libertarian candidate Marco Battaglia was removed from the ballot by Iowa's State Objections Panel (a decision a Polk County judge upheld) over a legal name discrepancy, then dropped out entirely in early August 2026 due to a medical emergency; the Iowa Libertarian Party subsequently nominated a replacement (Jacob Heard). The claim that a court ruling in August 2026 determined Libertarians categorically 'do not qualify' for the ballot misrepresents this sequence of events and omits that a new Libertarian nominee was chosen.

inaccurate_statement: Zach Nunn's platform aligns with an Iowa House Republicans' 'Three Strikes' bill mandating a 20-year prison sentence without parole for habitual offenders, and he supports requiring judges to justify deviating from uniform bond schedules on forcible felony/weapons cases
description: No record exists in the available material of Zach Nunn taking a position on a state-level Iowa 'Three Strikes' sentencing bill or a judicial bond-schedule reform measure. His documented federal platform centers on 'Back the Blue & Defend the Border,' COPS funding, the Laken Riley Act, and related federal law-enforcement funding measures — not Iowa state sentencing/bail legislation, which as a member of Congress he has no role in enacting. This presents a specific policy mechanism as his stated position without support in his documented record.

inaccurate_statement: Nunn generally supports replacing parts of the ACA with decentralized options.
description: Nunn's documented position is that he does not support the ACA and ultimately wants it repealed, treating his vote for the subsidy extension as a transition measure rather than an endorsement. There is no documented statement describing a plan to replace parts of the ACA with 'decentralized options' — this specific policy mechanism is not found in his record and is presented without hedging as his stated position.

inaccurate_statement: Sarah Trone Garriott's healthcare-cost approach includes 'capping medical costs' as a specific mechanism
description: Trone Garriott's documented affordability platform includes cracking down on corporate price gouging, ending tariffs, expanding child tax credits, and eliminating junk fees, plus healthcare planks like a public option, restoring Medicaid funding, and extending ACA subsidies. No record exists of a specific 'capping medical costs' proposal or mechanism attributed to her.

inaccurate_statement: Zach Nunn advocates for 'cracking down on government waste or fraud' as a healthcare-cost solution
description: While Nunn has discussed targeting Medicaid waste and fraud in the context of the 2025 reconciliation bill, there is no documented statement framing 'cracking down on government waste or fraud' specifically as his healthcare-cost-lowering mechanism in his affordability platform; this is a plausible but unverified characterization presented without hedging.

inaccurate_statement: Trone Garriott argued at the Iowa State Fair Political Soapbox for aggressive policies to bring manufacturing back to the U.S., claiming over-reliance on Chinese goods and components compromises American safety and sovereignty
description: There is no record of Trone Garriott making this specific manufacturing/supply-chain sovereignty argument at the Iowa State Fair. The documented Iowa State Fair statement attributed to her is that Nunn is not truly "tough on China" on trade, tied to his votes and campaign donations from Chinese corporations — a different and narrower claim than the sweeping "bring manufacturing back" framing presented here as her own stated position.

inaccurate_statement: Trone Garriott's broader platform views infrastructure protection, domestic food supplies, and community resources as fundamental building blocks of overall national stability, framed as a national-security lens
description: No documented statement ties her food-pantry/community background to a national-security or national-stability framing; her platform addresses affordability, healthcare, immigration, and clean energy, not an explicit resource-security doctrine.

inaccurate_statement: Trone Garriott's border policy is described as 'comprehensive federal reforms, focus on accurate vetting'
description: Her documented immigration platform calls for secure borders combined with a path to citizenship, streamlined legal pathways, Dreamer protection, and trafficking prevention — not a stated 'accurate vetting' framing, which appears to be an invented specific mechanism not found in her platform.

inaccurate_statement: Trone Garriott recently criticized defense leadership for fundraising instead of focusing on keeping deployed troops safe overseas
description: No record exists of Trone Garriott making a statement criticizing defense leadership for prioritizing fundraising over troop safety overseas; her documented criticisms of Nunn on national security center on his China Select Committee attendance and donations from Chinese corporations, not troop safety/defense leadership fundraising.

inaccurate_statement: Nunn has consistently voted to deploy the National Guard at the Southern Border
description: No record exists of Nunn voting on or sponsoring National Guard border-deployment legislation specifically; his documented immigration/border record centers on the Laken Riley Act, border enforcement funding generally, and E-Verify-type employer proposals, not a specific National Guard deployment voting record.

inaccurate_statement: Nunn supported the Fiscal Year 2026 and 2027 National Defense Authorization Acts, attaching provisions on adversarial AI, defense contract modernization, and preventing Chinese espionage in the military supply chain
description: No record of Nunn's involvement with FY2026/2027 NDAA provisions on adversarial AI or Chinese espionage in the defense supply chain exists in the documented record; his confirmed national-security-related legislative record centers on Financial Services Committee work, the CCP Select Committee, and cybersecurity policy generally, not specific NDAA amendments as described here.

inaccurate_statement: Nunn introduced the bipartisan PEACE Act to widen financial sanctions on foreign banks supporting Russia's energy sector
description: There is no record of Nunn introducing legislation called the 'PEACE Act' regarding Russia-related bank sanctions; his documented legislative record includes bills like the GUARD Act, TRAPS Act, and Protecting Americans' Savings Act, but nothing matching this description.

inaccurate_statement: Third-party candidates, including the Libertarian ticket, were removed from the ballot by a court ruling in late August 2026, leaving Nunn and Trone Garriott as the primary choices.
description: The Libertarian candidate Marco Battaglia was removed from the ballot by a court ruling upholding a name-discrepancy objection in late July 2026, not late August. He then dropped his campaign entirely on August 4, 2026 due to a medical emergency, and the Libertarian Party of Iowa nominated a new candidate, Jacob Heard, in mid-August 2026 to replace him on the ballot. The response's framing that this left only Nunn and Trone Garriott as ballot choices is therefore inaccurate — a new Libertarian nominee exists.

inaccurate_statement: Sarah Trone Garriott's background is as a Lutheran pastor and food bank network executive
description: Trone Garriott served as Coordinator of Interfaith Engagement for the Des Moines Area Religious Council (DMARC) Food Pantry Network, a coordination role, not as an executive of a food bank network.

inaccurate_statement: Third-party candidates, including the Libertarian ticket, were removed from the ballot by a court ruling in late August 2026, leaving Nunn and Trone Garriott as the primary choices.
description: The Libertarian candidate Marco Battaglia was removed from the ballot by a court ruling upholding a name-discrepancy objection in late July 2026, not late August. He then dropped his campaign entirely on August 4, 2026 due to a medical emergency, and the Libertarian Party of Iowa nominated a new candidate, Jacob Heard, in mid-August 2026 to replace him on the ballot. The response's framing that this left only Nunn and Trone Garriott as ballot choices is therefore inaccurate — a new Libertarian nominee exists.

inaccurate_statement: Zach Nunn voted to revise and narrow the scope of the federal Clean Water Act to reduce the types of waterways subject to federal environmental protection and permitting
description: No record exists of Nunn voting to narrow the scope of the federal Clean Water Act. His documented water-quality record is the opposite in character: he announced a $500,000 federal investment for a districtwide flood/drought and groundwater/nitrate monitoring network and secured a clean-water amendment in the PERMIT Act creating a state-led pilot program to accelerate Iowa water quality projects. This specific voting claim is unsupported and mischaracterizes his actual water-policy actions.

inaccurate_statement: Nunn has publicly supported certain bipartisan immigration reform legislation
description: Nunn's documented immigration record centers on border-security-first enforcement measures (the Laken Riley Act, Secure the Border Act, E-Verify support via the Dignity Act, ending catch-and-release, reinstating Remain in Mexico) rather than a broader bipartisan immigration reform package. While the Dignity Act he co-sponsors does include some bipartisan elements and a legal framework for some undocumented immigrants, characterizing his record simply as supporting 'bipartisan immigration reform legislation' without the enforcement-first framing that defines his actual public positioning overstates and mischaracterizes his stance.

inaccurate_statement: Subsequent Libertarian nominees were later ruled off the ballot by a state judge, leaving Nunn and Trone Garriott as the primary choices
description: The core substance is true: Libertarian candidate Marco Battaglia was removed from the IA-03 ballot in 2024, leaving Nunn and Trone Garriott as the primary choices. But the claim misattributes the process to 'a state judge.' In fact, the Iowa State Objections Panel (Attorney General, Secretary of State, and State Auditor) voted 2-1 on Aug. 28, 2024 to remove him, a decision later affirmed by the Iowa Supreme Court — not a single judge. This is a narrow attribution error that doesn't undermine the overall accurate point that the Libertarian nominee was knocked off the ballot, leaving a two-way race.

inaccurate_statement: Subsequent Libertarian nominees were later ruled off the ballot by a state judge, leaving Nunn and Trone Garriott as the primary choices
description: The core claim—that the Libertarian nominee (Marco Battaglia) was removed from the IA-03 ballot, leaving Nunn and Trone Garriott as the primary choices—is true. However, the removal was carried out by the Iowa State Objections Panel (composed of the Secretary of State, Attorney General, and State Auditor) in a 2-1 vote, and this decision was subsequently affirmed by the Iowa Supreme Court, not by a single 'state judge' as the claim states. This is a minor factual mischaracterization of the decision-making body/process rather than a fabrication, since the substantive outcome described in the claim is accurate.

inaccurate_statement: Zach Nunn focuses on looking for alternative measures to lower overall out-of-pocket costs rather than extending federal marketplace subsidies.
description: This omits that Nunn was one of only 17 House Republicans (and the only member of Iowa's all-GOP delegation) to vote in January 2026 for a three-year extension of enhanced ACA premium tax credits, citing that over 100,000 Iowans could lose coverage otherwise. Presenting his position as simply favoring alternatives 'rather than extending federal marketplace subsidies' contradicts this documented vote and paints an incomplete, one-sided picture of a genuinely mixed record — he has both criticized the ACA subsidies as a 'COVID-era subsidy' and voted to extend them.

inaccurate_statement: Trone Garriott's platform embraces strict regulations on industrial agricultural pollution and mandatory conservation rules
description: Trone Garriott's actual documented statements on agricultural runoff are more incentive-based and collaborative than a flat "mandatory conservation rules" framing suggests — she has said voluntary conservation practices "are voluntary, but they shouldn't be optional," tying subsidies to expectations, and her campaign materials describe working with farmers on sustainable practices rather than an explicit strict/mandatory regulatory regime. This is an overstatement of a real but more nuanced position, not a fabrication of her general environmental stance.

inaccurate_statement: Nunn voted in favor of the PERMIT Act, a bill that restricts key elements of the federal Clean Water Act by permitting the unregulated discharge of certain pesticides and agricultural stormwater into protected waterways
description: Nunn's support for the PERMIT Act and its effect of narrowing certain federal Clean Water Act protections for agricultural stormwater is real and documented, including criticism from environmental groups that it weakens the Act. However, the response's characterization that it "permits the unregulated discharge of certain pesticides" into protected waterways overstates the bill's actual mechanism, which is described elsewhere as narrowing the scope of federal protections/permitting requirements and creating a voluntary state-led pilot program for nutrient-impaired watersheds, not a blanket authorization for unregulated pesticide discharge. This is an exaggerated framing of a real, more nuanced legislative action rather than a fabrication of the underlying vote.

inaccurate_statement: Sarah Trone Garriott's alignment with data center critics is presented via her party's state-level platform, led by Rob Sand, which calls for ending the 'extraction economy' of data centers by repealing state tax breaks, forcing companies to pay 100% of utility upgrades, and requiring rigorous public hearings.
description: This specific policy platform—ending state tax breaks for data centers and requiring companies to pay 100% of utility/infrastructure upgrade costs—is documented as belonging to Rob Sand, the Democratic gubernatorial nominee in a separate statewide race, not to Sarah Trone Garriott's congressional campaign. No evidence connects Trone Garriott's own platform to this specific data-center policy; her congressional campaign focuses on healthcare, affordability, and labor issues, and multiple research passes found no direct statement from her on data centers at all. Presenting another candidate's signature policy proposal as if it directly reflects Trone Garriott's own platform materially misleads the reader about her actual, documented (or undocumented) position on the central question asked.

inaccurate_statement: Zach Nunn has publicly stated Iowa is 'a model for how workforce development and AI leadership can work hand in hand' regarding data centers.
description: No source could be found attributing this specific quote to Zach Nunn. His documented public statements on AI focus on agriculture (the FARM AI Act) and AI education/workforce programs (the Expanding AI Voices Act), not a specific comment praising Iowa's data center growth in these terms. This appears to be a fabricated quote, though it is broadly consistent with his general pro-development, pro-workforce stance.

inaccurate_statement: Zach Nunn maintains that the federal government should not override local zoning decisions for or against data centers.
description: No statement, vote, bill sponsorship, or interview could be found in which Zach Nunn addresses federal preemption of local zoning authority over data centers. This appears to be an unsupported attribution rather than a documented position.

inaccurate_statement: Sarah Trone Garriott focuses on raising minimum standards, improving educational opportunities, and supporting service and working-class families left behind by federal policies
description: Trone Garriott's documented affordability platform centers on cracking down on corporate price gouging, ending tariffs, expanding the Child Tax Credit and EITC, and eliminating junk fees, plus support for public schools, apprenticeships and job training. No source ties her specifically to a phrase or plank about 'raising minimum standards' as an affordability mechanism, and this appears to be a vague or garbled characterization not matching her actual documented messaging, though the general spirit of supporting working families and education is consistent with her broader platform.

inaccurate_statement: Sarah Trone Garriott's approach includes 'capping the out-of-pocket costs of prescription drugs' as a specific mechanism
description: Trone Garriott's actual federal platform calls for allowing Medicare to negotiate prescription drug prices, not a specific cap on out-of-pocket drug costs. While she has supported a state-level insulin cost cap as a state senator, no source documents a federal 'capping drug costs' proposal in her congressional platform; her documented mechanism is Medicare price negotiation.

inaccurate_statement: Sarah Trone Garriott advocates lowering household utility bills via renewable energy investments as a specific policy mechanism
description: There is no confirmed direct statement from Trone Garriott's federal campaign tying her clean-energy platform (investments in wind, solar, and biofuels) specifically to lowering household electricity/utility bills. This is a genuine, confirmed gap in her public record on that specific framing, despite her general clean-energy platform being real.

inaccurate_statement: Zach Nunn argues that curbing federal government spending will lower inflation, presented as part of his overtime/tips tax-cut platform
description: While Nunn has generally attributed high prices to federal 'overspending, overregulation, and inflation,' no source specifically ties a 'curbing federal spending to lower inflation' mechanism directly into his tips/overtime tax-cut messaging as a unified, single platform plank in the way presented here; this is a mild conflation of separate but related statements rather than a wholly invented position.

inaccurate_statement: Patients from the MercyOne Ottumwa closure are forced to drive 40 minutes to an hour for care
description: Coverage of the MercyOne Ottumwa clinic closure ties this longer, rural travel-time framing to that specific facility, but a separate, distinct MercyOne South Des Moines closure (an urban location) is sometimes conflated with it in reporting; the roughly 40-minute-to-hour drive figure is more specifically associated with rural closures like Ottumwa and Centerville rather than being a uniformly precise district-wide figure, so this detail should be treated as an approximation rather than a precisely verified statistic.

inaccurate_statement: Sarah Trone Garriott criticizes the lack of federal and state action regarding high nitrate levels and rising cancer rates linked to compromised drinking water
description: Trone Garriott has discussed water quality and nitrate issues and connected them to public health/cancer concerns broadly, but her documented public statements on the 2025-2026 nitrate crisis focus more specifically on criticizing the $25 million Central Iowa Water Works allocation as insufficient and calling for addressing agricultural/other runoff, rather than a generic claim of "lack of federal and state action." This is a loose paraphrase rather than a direct contradiction, so it is treated as a minor mischaracterization rather than a fabrication.

inaccurate_statement: Sarah Trone Garriott's platform aligns with broader Iowa Democratic efforts to eliminate corporate tax breaks for Big Tech and implement stricter oversight to protect taxpayers from surging utility bills, positioning her as critical/regulation-focused on data center development
description: No confirmed record exists of Sarah Trone Garriott taking any position on data center development, ratepayer cost-shifting, or the major Microsoft/Meta data-center buildout in her district, despite this being a live local issue and dedicated research repeatedly checking her campaign site, social media, and news coverage. An independent AI-policy tracker lists her data-center position as 'No mention.' The specific policy of ending state tax breaks for data centers and requiring companies to fund utility infrastructure is a signature proposal of Rob Sand, the Democratic gubernatorial candidate, not Trone Garriott. description: Trone Garriott's actual stated jobs/economy platform emphasizes raising wages and supporting small businesses by investing in apprenticeships, vocational schools, community colleges, and job training programs, rather than a specific mechanism of building formal K-12-to-employer pipeline partnerships. No source ties her to specific advocacy for red-flag laws or limits on large-capacity magazines; these specific policy mechanisms do not appear in her campaign materials or endorsement pages. This is a narrow addition beyond her documented platform rather than a mischaracterization of her overall gun-safety stance.

inaccurate_statement: Sarah Trone Garriott supports red flag laws as part of her gun violence prevention platform
description: Multiple detailed sources on Trone Garriott's gun violence prevention platform—including her own campaign issues page (sarahforiowa.com) and her Giffords PAC endorsement page, which specifically enumerates the gun measures she supports—consistently describe her platform as focused on strengthening background checks, promoting safe storage, and investing in mental health resources.
