While anti-corruption messaging is a real component of her campaign, characterizing her overall governance focus this narrowly omits her more prominent affordability, healthcare, and data-center platform planks, which are more central and more directly documented than a 'waste and economic accountability' framing.

inaccurate_statement: Local police leadership and retired officers have endorsed her public safety investments
description: The claim overstates and misattributes endorsement dynamics. Cognetti's own police chief, Thomas Carroll, has voiced support for her administration's resource allocation, but he serves under her as a mayoral appointee running the department she oversees as chief executive — not an independent 'police leadership' endorser in an electoral sense. Only one retired officer (a former Scranton detective featured in a campaign ad) has publicly praised her record, not multiple 'retired officers' as the claim implies. Most importantly, formal police endorsements have actually gone against her: the Pennsylvania State Troopers Association endorsed her opponent Rob Bresnahan, and Cognetti herself has publicly acknowledged she lacks police union endorsements, explaining that police unions never interview her before endorsing (unlike firefighter unions, which do). This directly undermines the claim's implication that police leadership broadly has endorsed her public safety investments.

inaccurate_statement: Paige Cognetti's platform emphasizes protecting union households
description: No source in the available record ties Cognetti's platform to a specific pledge to 'protect union households.' Her platform does include support for union labor requirements in specific contexts (e.g., requiring union labor for data center development) and she has labor union endorsements, but a general 'protecting union households' plank as part of her jobs platform is not documented and appears to be an unsupported extrapolation.

inaccurate_statement: Paige Cognetti prioritizes universal pre-K/childcare programs.
description: Cognetti's official campaign priorities page (paigeforpa.com/priorities/) confirms she will 'fight for paid family leave and affordable childcare' as part of her platform, but nowhere does she mention 'universal pre-K' specifically as a priority. No search results, campaign materials, endorsement pages, or news coverage reference a universal pre-K position for Cognetti. The claim conflates her genuine, verified support for 'affordable childcare' with a broader and more specific 'universal pre-K' program that isn't part of her stated platform. This is a narrow misstatement of scope/specificity rather than a wholesale fabrication, since the underlying childcare-affordability priority is real and confirmed directly from her campaign site.

inaccurate_statement: Cognetti has 'also updated her platform' to address data centers, implying a reactive/secondary position compared to Bresnahan's proactive legislative push
description: Cognetti's opposition to unchecked data-center development is documented as one of her most specific and central 2026 campaign planks, backed by a $200,000 TV ad campaign and detailed proposals (siting on brownfields, requiring union labor, developer-funded water/electric infrastructure, transparency requirements), plus a municipal-level 'Technology and Energy Overlay' zoning amendment she introduced as mayor. Framing her position as merely an 'update' in response to the issue understates that this has been a core, sustained element of her campaign, not a reactive addition.

inaccurate_statement: Bresnahan has framed his platform directly around active federal legislative pushback [implying strong momentum/prominence for the bill], while Cognetti's data center position is characterized as merely a reactive update
description: The response frames Bresnahan's Local Control Protection Act as the dominant, most active pushback on data centers while characterizing Cognetti's position as merely a follow-on adjustment. In reality, Cognetti's data-center opposition is a central, specific 2026 campaign issue backed by a $200,000 TV ad campaign with detailed policy proposals (siting on brownfields, no tax breaks, no NDAs, union labor requirements, developer-funded water/electric infrastructure), and she introduced a municipal-level 'Technology and Energy Overlay' zoning amendment as mayor. Meanwhile, Bresnahan's bill had no cosponsors and was reported as unlikely to advance out of committee. The response's framing inverts the comparative strength of the two candidates' actual data-center records — Cognetti's is arguably the more substantive and prominent campaign plank, not a secondary 'update.'

inaccurate_statement: Bresnahan has taken the most explicit legislative action to push back on unchecked data center development, more so than Cognetti
description: While Bresnahan's bill is a real, confirmed legislative proposal, describing it as making him the candidate who has done the most to push back on unchecked data center development omits that the bill has no cosponsors and is unlikely to advance, and omits Cognetti's more extensive and specific data-center platform (a central 2026 campaign issue with detailed policy mechanisms, a dedicated ad campaign, and an actual municipal zoning overlay she implemented as mayor). The comparison as framed is one-sided and does not reflect the fuller picture available for both candidates.

inaccurate_statement: Bresnahan is a member of the Problem Solvers Caucus
description: No record exists of Rob Bresnahan being a member of the Problem Solvers Caucus. His documented 119th Congress committee assignments are Agriculture, Small Business, and Transportation and Infrastructure, and no source ties him to this caucus specifically.

inaccurate_statement: Bresnahan worked on bipartisan legislation called the 'Supporting Apprenticeship Colleges Act'
description: No record exists of a bill called the 'Supporting Apprenticeship Colleges Act' associated with Bresnahan. His documented legislative record includes bills like the Local Control Protection Act, Small Business Cybersecurity Assistance Evaluation Act, and work on flood-resilience/WRDA legislation, but nothing under this specific title.

inaccurate_statement: Cognetti publicly praises bipartisan federal packages like the ROAD to Housing Act.
description: The '21st Century ROAD to Housing Act' is legislation backed by Rob Bresnahan, not a bill Cognetti has praised. No record exists of Cognetti commenting on or praising this specific bipartisan housing package; her housing-related record centers on her mayoral initiatives (affordable housing grants, the Hilltop Heights project) rather than this specific federal bill.

inaccurate_statement: Cognetti's platform bans members of Congress from serving on corporate boards and stops prediction market gambling on government actions.
description: No source documents Cognetti proposing a ban on members of Congress serving on corporate boards or a ban on prediction-market gambling tied to government actions. Her documented anti-corruption platform centers on banning congressional stock trading, opposing corporate PAC money, and increasing ethics rules — this specific pair of proposals is not supported by her platform materials.

inaccurate_statement: Cognetti backs the federal PRO Act.
description: No record exists of Cognetti making a direct statement endorsing the federal PRO Act specifically. Her platform and endorsement record show general pro-labor positioning (union endorsements, support for easier union organizing and workplace protections), but no sourced statement ties her specifically to the PRO Act by name.

inaccurate_statement: Cognetti points to her executive experience as Scranton mayor raising municipal wages and expanding department workforces.
description: No source documents Cognetti citing municipal wage increases or department workforce expansions as part of her congressional campaign messaging. Her documented mayoral accomplishments cited in her campaign include housing units, business growth, grants secured, and police funding/technology investments — not a specific claim about raising municipal wages or expanding department workforces generally.

inaccurate_statement: She supports an anti-corruption agenda that bans lawmakers from serving on corporate boards
description: No source in the record ties Cognetti to a specific proposal banning members of Congress from serving on corporate boards. Her documented anti-corruption platform centers on banning congressional stock trading and rejecting corporate PAC money, not a corporate-board-service ban.

inaccurate_statement: Her platform bans gambling on war and elections by government officials
description: No record exists of Cognetti proposing a ban on prediction-market-style gambling on war or elections by government officials. Her documented anti-corruption platform is focused on stock trading, PAC money, and lobbying-related reforms, not this specific proposal.

inaccurate_statement: The report revealing the April 2025 radio interview audio was from Politico
description: The audio of Bresnahan's April 2025 radio comments about discussing trades with his financial adviser was obtained and reported by NOTUS, not Politico. This is a source misattribution on a detail that doesn't change the substance of the underlying contradiction, which is otherwise accurately described.

inaccurate_statement: Financial disclosures showed Bresnahan made hundreds of stock trades "worth millions of dollars" after taking office
description: The trading pattern (roughly 600-650 trades) is well documented, but specific aggregate dollar figures for the total value of his trades are sourced to Democratic campaign/DCCC claims and were not independently verified against his actual periodic transaction reports, so presenting a "worth millions of dollars" total as a confirmed fact overstates what has been independently corroborated.

inaccurate_statement: Politico published audio in March 2026 from an April 2025 radio interview revealing the financial adviser quote
description: The audio contradiction between Bresnahan's April 2025 comments describing dialogue with his financial adviser and his later denial of such dialogue is documented as being obtained/reported by NOTUS, not Politico. The response misattributes the outlet that surfaced this audio.

inaccurate_statement: Financial disclosures showed he executed stock trades worth millions of dollars
description: The trading pattern of roughly 600-650 trades in 2025 is well documented, but specific aggregate dollar figures for the total value of trades are sourced to the Cognetti campaign or DCCC and were not independently verified against his actual periodic transaction reports. Presenting a specific 'millions of dollars' total as a confirmed fact from financial disclosures overstates what has been independently verified.

inaccurate_statement: Representatives for Bresnahan have stated that his investment portfolio is handled by an outside financial institution rather than directed by him personally
description: Audio obtained by NOTUS shows Bresnahan himself describing active dialogue with his financial adviser about "what different positions are coming up" in April 2025, directly contradicting a later claim that he does not have dialogues with his financial advisers. His campaign has stated he "has never traded his own stocks," but this is a distinct claim from the one presented here, and the documented inconsistency between his own statements undercuts the clean framing that an outside institution independently directs his portfolio without his involvement.

inaccurate_statement: End Citizens United placed him on a "Most Corrupt" list
description: The knowledge base confirms End Citizens United filed a House ethics complaint against Bresnahan over an undisclosed helicopter, but there is no record of a specific "Most Corrupt" list naming him. This appears to be an invented characterization of the group's actual documented action (the ethics complaint) rather than accurately describing it.

inaccurate_statement: The DCCC has published a formal 'Case Against Rob Bresnahan' citing his backing from super PACs aligned with corporate tax-cut goals.
description: The DCCC did publish a real, formal document titled "The Case Against Rob Bresnahan" (dated May 19, 2026), so that core fact is accurate. However, the specific content attributed to it in this claim is wrong: the actual document focuses on Bresnahan's stock-trading controversy, his broken promise to ban congressional stock trading, his vote for Medicaid cuts, rising health premiums, and the personal tax break he received from the 'One Big Beautiful Bill' — it contains no mention of 'super PACs' at all. The super PAC/corporate-tax-cut donor angle instead traces to a separate report by a different organization, Unrig Our Economy, which noted Bresnahan received corporate PAC (not super PAC) money from FirstEnergy tied to tax breaks. Because the underlying document is real but the specific content cited (super PAC backing tied to corporate tax-cut goals) is not actually in it, and is instead misattributed from a different source, this is a minor factual/attribution error rather than a fabrication of the entire claim, since the DCCC has published other material critiquing Bresnahan's ties to corporate tax cuts.

inaccurate_statement: Critics pointed out that Cognetti's congressional campaign received $14,600 in contributions from Fidelity Bank board members months before she directed the city to buy the building
description: The documented Fidelity Bank matter involves nine board members (including John Cognetti) each donating $1,500 to her mayoral campaign in April 2025 (totaling $13,500, not $14,600), and it involves the city's 2024 purchase of a different Fidelity building for a police/City Hall annex, not the 2022 purchase of the historic Electric Building for Fidelity's new HQ. The specific dollar figure of $14,600 does not match the confirmed figure, and the donations went to her mayoral campaign, not her congressional campaign.

inaccurate_statement: House Speaker Mike Johnson campaigned against Cognetti by accusing her administration of slashing the local police budget for guns and ammunition by 50%
description: No record exists of this specific claim about a 50% cut to guns/ammunition funding, or of Mike Johnson personally campaigning against Cognetti (he is documented campaigning for Bresnahan in this race, not specifically attacking Cognetti's police budget with this figure). The documented record shows the opposite direction on policing: a 22% increase in the police department's operating budget, $5M+ in police equipment/training spending, and an independent WVIA analysis finding Republican 'rising crime under Cognetti' attacks to be partially misleading.

inaccurate_statement: Federal filings showed leadership PACs that donated to Cognetti are heavily funded by massive corporations including Boeing, JPMorgan Chase, and UnitedHealthcare
description: The documented corporate donors to the leadership PACs (Blue Hen Federal PAC and Katherine Clark's committee) that gave to Cognetti's campaign, per Spotlight PA and NOTUS reporting, do not include Boeing, JPMorgan Chase, or UnitedHealthcare — the reporting cites companies such as Visa, Pfizer, Northrop Grumman, Delta, and Verizon. The core claim that she accepted indirect corporate-PAC-linked money via leadership PACs is accurate, but these specific named corporations are not supported by the available reporting.

inaccurate_statement: In August 2026, House Speaker Mike Johnson and Rep. Rob Bresnahan accused Cognetti of slashing the city's budget for police firearms and ammunition by 50% and objecting when the city council tried to reinstate the funding
description: No record exists of this specific claim — a 50% cut to police firearms/ammunition funding attributed to a joint Johnson/Bresnahan rally — in the available documentation of criticisms leveled against Cognetti. Her public safety record as documented shows increased police funding and equipment spending (a 22% increase in the police department's operating budget, $5M+ in equipment/training spending), which cuts against this specific narrow claim, though it does not rule out some specific budget-line dispute occurring.

inaccurate_statement: Rival campaigns have lobbed accusations that Cognetti secured 'sweetheart deals' to benefit her family's campaign and businesses throughout her mayoral tenure
description: This vaguely worded claim appears to conflate or loosely gesture at the documented Fidelity Bank conflict-of-interest story, in which Cognetti's uncle-in-law John Cognetti serves on Fidelity Bank's board and Fidelity board members donated to her campaign while the city separately purchased Fidelity's old headquarters building. That story involves specific, named, corroborated facts, not a vague 'sweetheart deals for her family's businesses' framing — the response's generic characterization is imprecise relative to the actual documented story.

inaccurate_statement: The grant for Fidelity Bank's new headquarters was 'multimillion-dollar'
description: The state grant awarded toward the Fidelity Bank headquarters renovation was $5 million, which is technically 'multimillion-dollar,' but the framing along with 'multimonth' language is imprecise; the core facts about the grant, uncle-in-law board connection, and NRCC targeting are otherwise accurately conveyed.

inaccurate_statement: Critics alleged that Cognetti's administration collaborated with activist groups to slash funding for police firearms and ammunition by 50%
description: There is no record of this specific claim. Cognetti's documented public safety record shows the opposite pattern: her administration increased police funding, including a 22% increase in the police department's operating budget, over $5 million in police equipment/training spending, hiring additional officers, and new police vehicles and technology. No source describes a 50% cut to police firearms/ammunition funding tied to activist group collaboration, and this directly contradicts her documented record of increased police spending.

inaccurate_statement: House Speaker Mike Johnson targeted Cognetti's record on public safety
description: There is no record of House Speaker Mike Johnson specifically targeting Cognetti on public safety or crime. Johnson is documented as having endorsed and campaigned for Bresnahan in this race, but no source ties him to a specific crime-related attack on Cognetti.

inaccurate_statement: Mike Villa was sentenced to 10 months in prison
description: No record confirms this specific sentencing detail for Michael Villa. The documented record covers his DUI charge, later arrests, and a 2025 incident at a Scranton high school that triggered a lockdown and led to an assault charge, but does not include a confirmed prison sentence of this length.

inaccurate_statement: At a high-profile press conference showcasing her anti-corruption agenda, Cognetti stood next to a prominent supporter who had previously served a federal prison sentence for stealing money from a local teachers' union
description: No record exists of this specific event, supporter, or controversy. This appears to be an invented claim not supported by any documented controversy in Cognetti's record, which does cover her anti-corruption messaging and press conferences (e.g., her March 2026 news conference criticizing Bresnahan) but includes no mention of this alleged optics controversy.

inaccurate_statement: Bresnahan's roughly 650 stock trades were worth over $7 million.
description: The trading pattern and trade count (roughly 600-650 trades) are well documented, but specific aggregate dollar figures such as a '$7 million' total are sourced to Cognetti's campaign or the DCCC and were not independently verified against his actual periodic transaction reports. This figure should be treated as an unconfirmed campaign-sourced aggregate rather than a confirmed fact.

inaccurate_statement: He dumped up to $250,000 in Pennsylvania hospital bonds right before supporting healthcare cuts that threatened rural hospital closures.
description: No record exists of a specific $250,000 Pennsylvania hospital bonds transaction tied to the timing of his healthcare vote. The documented, corroborated instance involves his sale of stock in four major health insurers/companies (Centene, Elevance, UnitedHealth, CVS Health) about a week before his reconciliation-bill vote, not a hospital-bonds transaction of this specific size.

inaccurate_statement: He traded stocks heavily during weeks of intense tariff volatility and bought defense stocks immediately prior to U.S. airstrikes in Iran.
description: No documentation supports a specific claim that Bresnahan bought defense stocks immediately before U.S. airstrikes in Iran, or a specific pattern of heavy trading tied to tariff volatility weeks. This appears to be an invented elaboration beyond the confirmed, specific stock-trading instances (the Medicaid-related insurer sales before the reconciliation vote).

inaccurate_statement: He sold up to $130,000 in stock from major Medicaid providers just days before voting for a bill that slashed federal Medicaid funding.
description: The underlying event is real and well documented (he sold stock in Centene, Elevance Health, UnitedHealth, and CVS Health around May 15, 2025, about a week before his May 22, 2025 reconciliation-bill vote), but the specific dollar figure of 'up to $130,000' is not corroborated in available sourcing and appears to be an unverified aggregate not confirmed against his actual disclosures.

inaccurate_statement: Bresnahan's legal counsel dismissed the helicopter-disclosure allegations as 'incorrect.'
description: Available reporting indicates his office's response was that he 'has gone above and beyond to disclose all assets as required by law,' not a quote from 'legal counsel' calling the allegations 'incorrect.' This misattributes the source and wording of the rebuttal.

inaccurate_statement: End Citizens United officially added Bresnahan to a 2026 'Most Corrupt' Politicians list due to his stock trades, corporate PAC intake, and the helicopter disclosure omission.
description: No record of End Citizens United maintaining or publishing a 2026 'Most Corrupt Politicians' list naming Bresnahan exists in available sourcing. The group's documented action is filing a specific ethics complaint over the undisclosed helicopter, not compiling or publishing a ranked 'most corrupt' list including him.

inaccurate_statement: In March 2026, Politico published unearthed audio from a 2025 radio interview where Bresnahan discussed 'what different positions are coming up' with his financial advisor
description: The audio recording of Bresnahan describing dialogue with his financial adviser about 'what different positions are coming up' was obtained and reported by NOTUS, not Politico. Attributing this reporting to Politico misidentifies the outlet responsible for surfacing this evidence.

inaccurate_statement: In March 2026, Politico published unearthed audio from a local radio interview where Bresnahan admitted to talking with his financial adviser about 'what different positions are coming up'
description: The audio in which Bresnahan discusses active dialogue with his financial adviser about upcoming stock positions was obtained and reported by NOTUS, not Politico, and dates to an April 2025 radio interview rather than a March 2026 Politico story. The underlying contradiction with his later town-hall claim is real, but the source and date are misattributed.

inaccurate_statement: Bresnahan's legal counsel called the helicopter ethics complaint a 'progressive political stunt'
description: Multiple consistent sources (NOTUS, Yahoo News/AP, Times Leader, The River Reporter) report that Bresnahan's legal counsel, Jessica Furst Johnson, called the helicopter ethics complaint allegation 'incorrect' and a 'defamatory and egregious lie,' not a 'progressive political stunt.' The core event (a lawyer for Bresnahan disputing the End Citizens United ethics complaint) is real and correctly attributed, but the specific quoted phrase 'progressive political stunt' does not appear in any source and appears to be a fabricated or invented quote rather than the actual language used. This is a narrower wording/quote error rather than a fabrication of the underlying event, so it is minor rather than critical.

inaccurate_statement: Changes under Cognetti's administration reduced paid maternity leave benefits to unpaid leave for newer city employees
description: This is actually accurate per the primary collective bargaining agreement, not inaccurate — flagging for clarity that this claim matches confirmed record: the Clerical Workers Local 2462 CBA confirms employees completing probation on or after Jan. 1, 2021 have unpaid FMLA leave for childbirth versus 12 weeks paid leave for those who completed probation earlier. No correction needed.

inaccurate_statement: Cognetti is endorsed by the United Autoworkers (UAW)
description: Extensive research into Cognetti's labor endorsements — including her own campaign's detailed press releases and multiple news articles covering her endorsement rollout — shows she has been endorsed by 11 labor unions: AFSCME, AFA-CWA, USW, SMART, PSEA, SEIU PA State Council, CWA, Ironworkers Local 404, Local Painters Union IUPDAT DC 21, and Pipefitters and Plumbers Local 524, and initially the PA Conference of Teamsters (which later switched to endorse Bresnahan). None of these detailed, comprehensive lists mention the UAW. The UAW's 2026 congressional endorsements found in search results focus on Michigan candidates, with no indication of involvement in PA-08. Given the specificity of the claim and that a genuine UAW endorsement would very likely have surfaced in the extensive coverage of Cognetti's labor endorsements, this claim appears to be fabricated.

inaccurate_statement: Cognetti has negotiated contract extensions that increased staff sizes and substantially boosted municipal wages for lower-earning clerical roles
description: The claim bundles two sub-claims. The wage-increase portion is well-supported: reporting confirms that Cognetti's administration negotiated a clerical union contract (2021) and DPW contract (2022) that included wage hikes, and her administration ran a 'Wage Boost Grant' program aimed at raising pay for lower-wage workers. However, no evidence was found supporting the specific claim that these contract negotiations 'increased staff sizes.' Available reporting on the clerical and DPW contracts discusses wage increases, health care cost-sharing, and residency requirement changes, but never mentions staffing level or headcount increases tied to these negotiations. This makes the 'increased staff sizes' portion an unverified/unsupported factual addition, though it's a narrow point that doesn't undermine the broader, well-supported claim about wage boosts for clerical workers.

inaccurate_statement: Served as a member of the Scranton School Board, where she focused on uncovering waste, fraud, and abuse
description: The waste/fraud/abuse oversight focus is documented for her role as Special Assistant to Pennsylvania Auditor General Eugene DePasquale, not her separate appointment to the Scranton School Board (2017, resigned Dec. 2018). The response conflates the two distinct roles by attaching the Auditor General office's stated focus to the School Board seat.

inaccurate_statement: Served as a school board director, where she worked to uncover waste, fraud, and abuse
description: The 'uncovering waste, fraud, and abuse' work is documented as part of her role as special assistant to the Pennsylvania Auditor General, not her separate role as a Scranton School Board director. The response conflates these two distinct positions into one, misattributing the fraud/waste oversight work to her school board tenure rather than her Auditor General advisory role.

inaccurate_statement: Served as a board member of the Scranton School Board working to uncover waste and bad contracts
description: Cognetti's tenure on the Scranton School Board is documented, but the specific characterization of her work there as 'uncovering waste and bad contracts' is not supported by the available record. The dossier notes a 2017 budget vote controversy involving layoffs and a tax increase during her board tenure, but no source confirms a mission or track record specifically framed around exposing waste and bad contracts on the school board.

inaccurate_statement: Cognetti's top priority is banning members of Congress from serving on corporate boards
description: No source in the available record documents Cognetti proposing a ban on members of Congress serving on corporate boards. Her documented anti-corruption platform centers on banning congressional stock trading, opposing corporate PAC money, and increasing transparency/ethics rules — not a corporate-board-service ban. This specific proposal does not appear in her stated priorities.

inaccurate_statement: Cognetti proposes prohibiting gambling via prediction markets on war, elections, and government activity
description: No documented Cognetti platform position addresses prediction-market gambling on war, elections, or government activity. Her anti-corruption agenda as sourced focuses on stock-trading bans, PAC money, and corporate accountability — this specific prediction-market proposal is not found anywhere in her platform materials.

inaccurate_statement: Cognetti proposes establishing term limits for Supreme Court justices and members of Congress
description: No source documents Cognetti advocating for Supreme Court or congressional term limits. Her stated anti-corruption platform emphasizes banning stock trading, rejecting corporate PAC money, and government accountability — term limits for justices or members of Congress do not appear among her documented positions.

inaccurate_statement: Cognetti supports the PRO Act
description: No documented statement ties Cognetti to the PRO Act specifically. Her platform does include support for unions and easier organizing/workplace protections generally, but no source confirms she has endorsed the PRO Act by name.

inaccurate_statement: Cognetti supports the Equality Act, providing federal protections for LGBTQ+ individuals
description: Paige Cognetti is the Mayor of Scranton, PA — a municipal office — not a member of Congress or a known candidate for the PA-08 U.S. House seat (currently held by Rob Bresnahan, previously Matt Cartwright). The Equality Act is federal legislation that only members of Congress vote on; a mayor has no formal capacity to 'support' it in a legislative sense, and there is no evidence Cognetti has run for or holds the PA-08 congressional seat. This claim misattributes a federal-office policy position to a local official who is not part of that race, which would meaningfully mislead a reader about her actual role and record.

inaccurate_statement: Bresnahan introduced H.J. Res. 12 to place strict term limits on members of Congress
description: H.J. Res. 12 (119th Congress), a constitutional amendment to limit House members to three terms and Senators to two terms, was introduced/sponsored by Rep. Ralph Norman (R-SC-5), not Rob Bresnahan. Bresnahan's own press release and congressional records confirm he only cosponsored the resolution in April 2025; he did not introduce it. The underlying fact that Bresnahan supports and cosponsored this specific term-limits amendment is accurate, but the claim's verb 'introduced' misattributes the sponsorship of the bill to him.

inaccurate_statement: Introduced a resolution (H.J. Res. 12) to place term limits on members of Congress.
description: No record exists in Rob Bresnahan's documented legislative activity of a term-limits resolution numbered H.J. Res. 12 or any term-limits proposal. His confirmed legislative record centers on stock-trading restrictions, small-business measures, flood resiliency/infrastructure bills, and the data-center 'Local Control Protection Act' — none of which include a term-limits resolution. This appears to be an invented or misattributed bill claim.

inaccurate_statement: Joins groups like the Problem Solvers Caucus to find common ground across political parties.
description: There is no documented record of Rob Bresnahan being a member of the Problem Solvers Caucus. His documented bipartisan self-positioning centers on regional/non-partisan framing ('I don't have an R or D next to my name') and specific bipartisan bills (e.g., BASICS Act, Faster Labor Contracts Act, WRDA flood provisions), but no source confirms Problem Solvers Caucus membership specifically.

inaccurate_statement: Supports increased military readiness, shipbuilding, nuclear deterrence, and technological modernization
description: While Bresnahan sits on the House Armed Services Committee and voted for the FY2027 NDAA, no specific statement, press release, or public record ties him personally to emphasizing shipbuilding, nuclear deterrence, and technological modernization as thematic priorities; his documented defense-related public statements focus on Tobyhanna Army Depot funding and military pay, not this specific framing.

inaccurate_statement: Bresnahan, joined by House Speaker Mike Johnson during a campaign stop, accused Cognetti of cutting funding for police guns and ammunition by 50% following discussions with activist groups
description: No record exists of Bresnahan making this specific claim about a 50% cut to police guns/ammunition funding tied to activist-group discussions, either personally or with Speaker Mike Johnson at a campaign stop. Bresnahan's documented public-safety criticism of Cognetti centers on general claims about rising crime under her administration, which an independent WVIA analysis found to be a partially misleading characterization based on selective date ranges. The specific 50% funding-cut claim, the activist-group detail, and the joint appearance with Johnson framed this way do not appear in the available record and read as an invented elaboration on a real but different underlying dispute.

inaccurate_statement: Bresnahan launched billboard advertisements questioning Cognetti's connections after a photo surfaced showing her with figures linked to local criminal elements
description: The underlying story about a photograph of Cognetti with operators of a Scranton hookah lounge later associated by prosecutors with a drug operation is real and documented. However, no record confirms that Bresnahan's campaign specifically ran billboard advertisements based on this photo; this specific detail about the medium and format of the attack appears to be an added, unverified elaboration on an otherwise real controversy.

inaccurate_statement: Cognetti's campaign pushed back on the crime claims, citing FBI statistics showing a decline in violent crime and noting millions of dollars invested in the police department
description: The core of the claim is well-supported: multiple sources confirm Cognetti's campaign pushed back on Republican crime attacks by citing that violent crime has declined during her tenure and that millions of dollars have been invested in the Scranton police department. A Fox News report quotes a Cognetti campaign spokesperson stating violent crime has gone down and Scranton has invested millions in its police department, and Pennsylvania Independent/WVIA reporting corroborates a documented decline in violent offenses alongside over $5 million in police investments. However, the specific attribution to 'FBI statistics' appears inaccurate: the crime decline data cited in reporting (including a Pennsylvania Independent article the Cognetti campaign itself promoted) comes from the Pennsylvania Uniform Crime Reporting System, a state police database, not FBI statistics. The FBI is mentioned in that reporting only to define/categorize what counts as a 'violent offense,' not as the source of the decline figures. This is a minor sourcing/attribution error within an otherwise accurate claim, not one that changes the overall takeaway.

inaccurate_statement: Rep. Bresnahan and House Speaker Mike Johnson accused Cognetti of reducing local law enforcement funding by 50% for police guns and ammunition following discussions with activist groups, claiming violent crime increased in Scranton under her leadership.
description: There is no record of Bresnahan or Speaker Mike Johnson making a specific claim that Cognetti cut police funding for guns and ammunition by 50% after meeting with activist groups. The documented record shows the opposite: as mayor, Cognetti increased the police department's operating budget by 22%, spent $5M+ on police equipment/training, added 51 new police vehicles, and hired additional officers. Republican attacks on her crime record do exist and were found by an independent WVIA analysis to be 'partially misleading' by cherry-picking narrow date ranges, but this specific claim about a 50% cut to funding for guns/ammunition tied to activist-group discussions does not match any documented criticism and appears to be a fabricated specific.

inaccurate_statement: Bresnahan's campaign argued that Cognetti is an out-of-touch "slick politician" who does not truly represent the working families of Northeastern Pennsylvania
description: The documented campaign criticism of Cognetti as out-of-touch centers on a specific quote describing her as a 'Harvard-educated Portland liberal' who is 'completely out of touch with hardworking NEPA families' (used in the context of the broader race, though attributed in the record to campaign messaging about her generally, not verified as tied to this specific 'slick politician' phrase). No source confirms Bresnahan's campaign used the specific term 'slick politician' to describe Cognetti. The underlying theme (out-of-touch framing) is real, but this specific quoted phrase is not verified.

inaccurate_statement: Cognetti formally petitioned the Pennsylvania Public Utility Commission to block UGI Gas from implementing a proposed 10% monthly increase on residential customers.
description: This is Rob Bresnahan's documented action, not Cognetti's. Bresnahan publicly opposed a UGI Utilities electric-rate-hike request (10.8%) and a separate UGI gas-division rate-hike request (~$110.4 million/year), urging the PA Public Utility Commission to reject them. No record exists of Cognetti taking this specific action; her platform addresses affordability through capping fees and opposing monopolies, not a UGI-specific petition.

inaccurate_statement: Cognetti has repeatedly spoken out against PPL Electric and Pennsylvania American Water rate increases
description: No record exists of Cognetti making statements opposing PPL Electric or Pennsylvania American Water rate increases. Her documented electricity-related statements are limited to opposing higher electric bills specifically in the context of data-center development, not a broader utility rate-hike campaign against these specific companies.

inaccurate_statement: Cognetti personally turned down her taxpayer-funded city government car and gas card, while cutting out wasteful no-bid contracts to save money
description: No record exists of Cognetti declining a taxpayer-funded city car/gas card or of a specific no-bid-contract cost-cutting initiative. Her documented fiscal record includes leading Scranton out of Act 47 fiscal distress and maintaining four consecutive years without a city tax increase, but this specific claim about a car/gas card and no-bid contracts is not supported by available material.

inaccurate_statement: Cognetti argues that families are feeling the squeeze at the pump because Washington politicians have prioritized overseas spending over relief for domestic consumers, and supports policies that crack down on big energy businesses and corporate price gouging to address gas prices
description: No campaign statement was found of Cognetti specifically addressing gasoline prices or attributing high gas prices to 'foreign overspending.' Her affordability platform frames costs around monopolies, credit-card fees, and healthcare middlemen, not a gas-price-specific 'foreign overspending' argument.

inaccurate_statement: No campaign statement located specifically addressing gasoline prices, despite response's framing that Cognetti has a plan for 'bringing down gas prices'
description: There is no direct statement found from Cognetti specifically addressing gasoline prices as a distinct issue. The response frames her platform as directly aimed at lowering gas prices, when her documented positions are about electricity rates, data centers, and general tariff policy — not gas prices specifically. This is a misleading framing rather than an outright fabrication, since the underlying planks cited (utility rate fights, opposition to tariffs) are real.

inaccurate_statement: Cognetti has vocally criticized the economic toll of international conflicts on the American taxpayer, directly tying foreign military spending to the reality of gas prices remaining stubborn at home
description: While Cognetti has expressed skepticism about the Iran conflict/war more generally, no source ties her to a specific statement connecting foreign military spending or international conflict costs to domestic gas prices. This specific causal link and framing appears to be an invented elaboration not found in her documented platform or statements.

inaccurate_statement: Cognetti famously turned down the official city government car and city-funded gas card upon taking office as mayor, forcing herself to pay for her own transit costs rather than billing the taxpayers
description: No record exists in the available material of Cognetti declining a city car or gas card as mayor. This specific personal-accountability anecdote is not documented in her biography, mayoral record, or campaign materials, and appears to be a fabricated detail with no basis in her actual record.

inaccurate_statement: As mayor, Cognetti has consistently fought utility companies (such as PPL Electric and UGI natural gas) trying to raise rates on everyday consumers
description: It is Rob Bresnahan, not Cognetti, who is documented as having publicly opposed UGI Utilities' proposed 10.8% electric rate hike and a separate UGI gas-division rate hike as a member of Congress. No record exists of Cognetti taking on PPL Electric or UGI rate increases as mayor; her platform's utility-related statements are limited to her data-center ad's demand that developers 'don't raise our electric bills.'

inaccurate_statement: Cognetti has heavily criticized her opponent and current policies for sustaining the war in Iran, which has driven global oil supply restrictions and spiked gas prices, advocating for diplomatic resolution
description: While Cognetti has been documented as skeptical of and opposed to the Iran war, calling it a 'reckless war' and criticizing Bresnahan for supporting it, no record exists of her specifically tying this criticism to gas prices or advocating for 'targeted domestic economic stabilization' of oil markets as a gas-price mechanism. This appears to be an invented elaboration connecting her general Iran-war opposition to a specific gas-price mechanism not found in her documented statements.

inaccurate_statement: Cognetti famously turned down her own city-allotted government car and municipal gas card, promising the same alignment with taxpayers' day-to-day burdens if elected to Washington
description: No record exists of Cognetti declining a city-issued vehicle or gas card as mayor, or of any pledge to forgo a congressional car/gas allowance. This specific claim does not appear in her documented mayoral or congressional record.

inaccurate_statement: Cognetti's anti-corruption policy agenda aims to stop politicians from trading energy sector stocks and benefiting from corporate interest groups, ensuring energy legislation puts families ahead of corporate profits
description: Cognetti has indeed proposed an anti-corruption agenda that includes a ban on congressional stock trading and rejecting corporate PAC money, and she frames this as preventing lawmakers from trading stocks in companies affected by their legislative work. However, all available reporting describes this as a general, industry-agnostic stock-trading ban and PAC-money ban covering all sectors (defense, tech, healthcare, etc.) as part of an eight-point plan (also including term limits, shutdown pay withholding, prediction-market bans, lobbying/corporate-board restrictions). No source ties her policy specifically to 'energy sector stocks' or frames it around ensuring 'energy legislation' benefits families over corporate profits. The claim narrows and mischaracterizes a genuine, broader anti-corruption platform into an energy-specific one that doesn't appear in her actual messaging, which is a misleading narrowing of an otherwise real policy position rather than a fabrication of the underlying stock-trading ban itself.

inaccurate_statement: Cognetti supports universal healthcare access models
description: Search results and Cognetti's own campaign platform (paigeforpa.com/priorities) show her healthcare positions focus on protecting Medicare and Medicaid from cuts, preventing insurance 'middlemen' from denying prescribed care, reforming insurance protections, and preserving healthcare marketplace access for small businesses. One source explicitly notes 'Cognetti has consistently supported Medicare and Medicaid' and aims to stop care denials — but nowhere does she call for a 'universal healthcare access model' (i.e., single-payer/Medicare-for-All type universal coverage). No search result ties her to universal healthcare or single-payer advocacy. The claim mischaracterizes her more incremental, access-and-protection-focused healthcare stance as support for a universal coverage model, which overstates/mislabels her actual position. This is a policy framing error rather than a fabrication, since her broader healthcare-access advocacy is real — it's the 'universal' framing that is not supported.

inaccurate_statement: Cognetti launched a campaign targeting Pennsylvania American Water demanding an accelerated schedule to replace 140-year-old water mains, and petitioned the DEP and PUC for independent public hearings on rate increases and stormwater oversight
description: The core of the claim is substantiated: Cognetti did call for Pennsylvania American Water to accelerate replacement of aging water mains following water main breaks in Scranton, and news coverage notes PAWC's Scranton mains include roughly 49 miles installed before 1900, consistent with the '140-year-old' framing. Her advocacy is also credited with contributing to PUC public input hearings held in Scranton on rate increases, including those by PAWC. However, the claim's specific detail that she 'petitioned the DEP... for independent public hearings on rate increases and stormwater oversight' misattributes her actual DEP petition, which sought a hearing specifically on a PPL Electric Utilities transmission line project's stormwater runoff impact — not on Pennsylvania American Water or water rate increases. The claim conflates two distinct advocacy actions (a PAWC-focused water main campaign plus PUC rate hearings, and a separate DEP petition concerning a different utility, PPL) into one continuous PAWC-targeted effort. This is a minor misattribution since the broader narrative of Cognetti's utility advocacy holds up, but the DEP/stormwater detail is incorrectly tied to PAWC specifically.

inaccurate_statement: Bresnahan supported military actions/conflicts involving Iran that impact global oil markets, contributing to higher fuel prices
description: It is accurate that Bresnahan supported the Iran military action and voted against efforts to terminate U.S. military operations against Iran, and that a 2025-2026 Iran conflict is documented as having disrupted oil markets and raised gas prices in the region. However, the response frames this as a DCCC/critic argument specifically, and while Bresnahan's support for the Iran conflict is real, no direct link was established connecting his personal voting record to the oil market disruption beyond his general support for the military action being ongoing at the time of the price spike. This is a plausible characterization of a critic's argument rather than a demonstrated causal claim, so it is treated as a minor framing issue rather than a clear factual error.

inaccurate_statement: Bresnahan opposed the Inflation Reduction Act, arguing it hampered the broader economy
description: The knowledge base documents a 2024-campaign-era criticism Bresnahan made of the Inflation Reduction Act's drug-pricing provisions specifically, made against a different opponent (Matt Cartwright) before he held office — it explicitly flags this quote as dated and not necessarily reflective of his current 2026 position, though no evidence exists that he has walked it back. There is no record of him framing his opposition around the IRA 'hampering the broader economy' generally; his documented criticism was specifically about drug-pricing provisions. This is a narrow mischaracterization of the basis for his stated opposition rather than a wholesale fabrication.

inaccurate_statement: Bresnahan secured $11.4 million in federal community project funding for Northeastern Pennsylvania
description: The documented figure for Bresnahan's federal community-project funding request for Northeastern Pennsylvania in 2026 is more than $59 million, not $11.4 million. The $11.4 million figure does not match any confirmed source.

inaccurate_statement: Bresnahan's Local Control Protection Act requires developers to prove they tried to hire local workers and partner with community colleges before bringing in outside labor, and gives local contractors and subcontractors first consideration for available work
description: The Local Control Protection Act as documented is about restricting corporations from suing municipalities that reject data-center zoning applications and requiring developers to sign a binding community benefit agreement or forfeit federal tax incentives. No source describes a 'workforce utilization plan' requiring proof of local-hiring attempts, community-college partnerships, or a contractor/subcontractor priority system as part of this bill. Additionally, the bill reportedly had no cosponsors and was unlikely to advance out of committee as of an Axios report, which the response does not mention.

inaccurate_statement: Bresnahan introduced the Local Control Protection Act, which requires federally-incentivized projects, like data centers, to prove they hired local workers before bringing in outside labor, and requires approved projects to give local contractors and subcontractors first consideration.
description: The Local Control Protection Act as actually described restricts corporations from suing municipalities that reject data-center zoning applications and requires developers to sign a binding community benefit agreement or forfeit federal tax incentives — it is about preserving local zoning control over data centers, not a local-hiring mandate requiring proof of local hires before outside labor or first-consideration requirements for local contractors. The response mischaracterizes the substance of this specific bill. Additionally, as of reporting, the bill had no cosponsors and was unlikely to advance out of committee, which the response does not note, presenting it as an active, functioning policy.

inaccurate_statement: The Local Control Protection Act ensures that large projects, such as data centers receiving federal incentives, must use local workers, partner with regional apprenticeship programs, and hire local contractors first
description: The Local Control Protection Act as documented is aimed at restricting corporations from suing municipalities that reject data-center zoning applications and requiring developers to sign a binding community benefit agreement or forfeit federal tax incentives, framed around local zoning control — not a mandate specifically requiring hiring local workers, partnering with apprenticeship programs, and hiring local contractors first. The bill also reportedly had no cosponsors and was unlikely to advance out of committee, which the response omits, presenting it without qualification as an active mechanism.

inaccurate_statement: Bresnahan secured $11.4 million in federal funding for local projects across Northeastern Pennsylvania, supporting community infrastructure, housing, and local workforce development programs like Job Corps
description: The $11.4 million figure and its attribution to Bresnahan for community infrastructure and housing projects across Northeastern Pennsylvania is accurate and well-documented: Bresnahan's office announced he 'successfully secured $11,432,000 for five projects located throughout Northeastern Pennsylvania,' including a career and technical center, a dam project, a bridge project, veterans supportive housing, and a road improvement project. However, the claim's specific mention of 'local workforce development programs like Job Corps' being part of this $11.4 million is not supported — none of the five listed projects funded by this $11.4 million package involve Job Corps. Job Corps funding was mentioned by Bresnahan in the context of a separate, broader appropriations bill vote (national-level funding), not as one of the five specific NEPA projects covered by the $11.4 million. This is a minor inaccuracy since the core claim (amount, purpose, infrastructure/housing focus) is correct, but the Job Corps detail appears to be a misattributed/conflated addition.

inaccurate_statement: The levee/dam safety legislation creates a new 'Continuing Authority Program' allowing USACE to modify completed flood-risk projects to meet federal accreditation standards
description: The legislation Bresnahan championed reportedly creates new levee risk-assessment standards and a 'Levee Owners Board' to help bring Wyoming Valley/Lackawanna River levees up to federal accreditation standards — there is no record of a mechanism called a 'Continuing Authority Program' tied to this effort. The underlying goal (helping local levees reach accreditation) is accurately described, but the specific named mechanism appears to be incorrect.

inaccurate_statement: Bresnahan introduced a 'Save BRIC Act' to safeguard FEMA's Building Resilient Infrastructure and Communities program, ensuring $2.5 million remains intact for flood buyouts in Scranton and levee rebuilding in Exeter and Duryea
description: Available records show Bresnahan publicly urged FEMA to reinstate the canceled BRIC program and cited Scranton's pending $2.5 million in BRIC buyout funding, but there is no record he introduced legislation named the 'Save BRIC Act,' nor of the specific claim about levee rebuilding funding in Exeter and Duryea tied to this program. This overstates an advocacy position as a specific piece of introduced legislation.

inaccurate_statement: Bresnahan fought for disaster preparedness legislation ensuring FEMA-approved but unfunded mitigation efforts are automatically categorized as 'pre-approved,' directly affecting property buyouts in Scranton and rebuilding flood levees in Exeter and Duryea
description: The claim conflates two distinct legislative efforts. Bresnahan did advocate for Scranton flood buyouts and Exeter/Duryea levee projects, but through his own Save BRIC Act (which sought to force disbursement of already-appropriated BRIC funding) and through letters urging FEMA to reinstate the BRIC program — not through a mechanism that automatically categorizes FEMA-approved-but-unfunded projects as 'pre-approved.' That specific 'pre-approved' categorization provision is part of the broader, bipartisan committee bill H.R. 4669 (the FEMA Act of 2025), which Bresnahan voted for in committee markup as one of many members, but which he did not author or specifically champion, and news coverage does not link that specific provision to the Scranton/Exeter/Duryea projects. The underlying facts (BRIC cuts threatening these specific local projects, and Bresnahan's advocacy on the issue) are real and accurately reported, but the claim misattributes the specific 'pre-approved' legislative mechanism to Bresnahan's own fight and incorrectly ties it directly to these named local projects, which were actually the focus of his separate Save BRIC Act.

inaccurate_statement: Serves as the Republican co-chair of a newly created bipartisan House Law Enforcement Caucus
description: Bresnahan is a member of the House Law Enforcement Caucus, but both his official House website's caucus list and Wikipedia identify him only as a regular member, not co-chair. The Republican co-chair role was held by Rep. John Rutherford (FL-5), as referenced alongside Gottheimer's November 2024 announcement of becoming the Democratic co-chair. Additionally, the caucus is not 'newly created' — the same announcement describes it as having existed 'over the last few years' engaging in bipartisan policy work. Bresnahan's actual confirmed co-chair role is of the Congressional Bipartisan Opportunity Youth Caucus, a different caucus entirely. This appears to be a misattribution of a co-chair title (and mischaracterization of the caucus as newly formed) rather than a wholly fabricated claim, and does not change the broader point that he is a genuine, active participant in law-enforcement-related caucus work.

inaccurate_statement: She took on and defeated the local established political machine while eight months pregnant
description: There is no record of Cognetti being eight months pregnant during her 2019 special election campaign. The dossier notes she took office as mayor with a two-week-old baby during COVID, which relates to a later period (her 2020 inauguration, coinciding with the pandemic that began in 2020), not her initial campaign in 2019. No source supports the specific claim that she was eight months pregnant while campaigning against the political machine in 2019.

inaccurate_statement: Her administration balanced the budget and generated consecutive fiscal surpluses
description: The available record confirms Scranton's Act 47 exit and credit rating improvement, and that her 2026 budget is the fourth consecutive with no city tax increase, but no source confirms a specific claim of 'consecutive fiscal surpluses' as a distinct, verified fact.

inaccurate_statement: She built a reputation as a reformer by eliminating cash payments in city hall, cutting administrative waste, refusing a city-issued car, and stepping up accountability for local slumlords and special interests
description: None of these specific claims (eliminating cash payments in city hall, cutting administrative waste in this specific framing, refusing a city-issued car, or targeting slumlords) appear in the available record of her mayoral accomplishments or anti-corruption record. While she does hold absentee landlords accountable as a general policy position, the other specific details are unsubstantiated and appear to be fabricated elaborations.

inaccurate_statement: Bresnahan has not campaigned on a specific local or national legislative plan dedicated to heavy rainfall mitigation or community flood recovery matching Cognetti's executive focus.
description: This significantly understates Bresnahan's flood-policy record, which is actually the single most detailed and specific platform item documented for either candidate on any topic. He is a member of the Flood Resiliency Caucus and the American Flood Coalition, publicly urged FEMA to reinstate the BRIC program, and championed an expansion of Section 566 of the Water Resources Development Act of 2026 that extended Army Corps of Engineers water-infrastructure partnership eligibility to the Upper Delaware River Basin for the first time and raised program authorization from $20 million to $92.69 million, including new levee risk-assessment standards and a Levee Owners Board to help bring Wyoming Valley/Lackawanna River levees up to federal accreditation standards. He also announced specific wastewater/stormwater funding for Monroe County, the Dallas Area Municipal Authority, and an Exeter sewer/stormwater project. Presenting him as lacking a specific flood-mitigation legislative plan directly contradicts this extensive, well-documented record and undermines the response's core recommendation to the reader.

inaccurate_statement: Cognetti's major backers include teachers, healthcare unions, and local municipal leaders
description: Cognetti's documented endorsements are much broader and more specific than this summary suggests, including PSEA, SEIU Pennsylvania, CWA, AFSCME, United Steelworkers, the Pennsylvania AFL-CIO, EMILYs List, J Street PAC, and the DCCC's Red to Blue program, plus elected officials like Gov. Shapiro. Framing her backers narrowly as 'teachers, healthcare unions, and local municipal leaders' omits her party, advocacy, and broader labor support and is an oversimplified characterization rather than a documented list of her major backers.

inaccurate_statement: Bresnahan's major backers are police unions and state trooper associations
description: Bresnahan's documented endorsements are considerably broader, including President Trump, the Congressional Leadership Fund, NFIB, U.S. Chamber of Commerce, Pennsylvania Conference of Teamsters, AFGE, and House Speaker Mike Johnson. Reducing his backers to just police unions and state trooper associations omits his major institutional, business, and political-leadership support.

inaccurate_statement: The response frames the current PA-08 race as being between Matt Cartwright and Rob Bresnahan, referencing a 'Cartwright and Bresnahan debate' and describing Cartwright as a current candidate.
description: Matt Cartwright was the incumbent Democrat who lost this seat to Rob Bresnahan in November 2024 and is not running in the 2026 general election. The current 2026 PA-08 race is between incumbent Republican Rob Bresnahan and Democratic challenger Paige Cognetti, the sitting Mayor of Scranton. The response fails to mention Cognetti at all and instead presents an outdated or incorrect matchup, which misrepresents who voters are actually choosing between in this race.

inaccurate_statement: The response frames the current PA-08 race as being between Matt Cartwright and Rob Bresnahan, referencing a 'Cartwright and Bresnahan debate' and describing Cartwright as a current candidate.
description: Matt Cartwright was the incumbent Democrat who lost this seat to Rob Bresnahan in November 2024 and is not running in the 2026 general election. The current 2026 PA-08 race is between incumbent Republican Rob Bresnahan and Democratic challenger Paige Cognetti, the sitting Mayor of Scranton. The response fails to mention Cognetti at all and instead presents an outdated or incorrect matchup, which misrepresents who voters are actually choosing between in this race.

inaccurate_statement: Cognetti backs increased federal funding for Customs and Border Protection (CBP) to manage ports of entry
description: No record exists of Cognetti proposing increased CBP funding specifically for ports of entry. Her documented immigration positions involve supporting border security generally, opposing local police cooperation with ICE, and favoring pathways to citizenship for Dreamers/essential workers — not a specific CBP funding proposal.

inaccurate_statement: Cognetti supports comprehensive bipartisan border security frameworks
description: This specific framing of 'comprehensive bipartisan border security frameworks' is not documented. Her record shows a genuine, documented shift in her immigration rhetoric over time (from a more Biden-era-supportive stance to calling Biden's border handling 'a huge misstep') alongside continued support for pathways to citizenship — but no source ties her to endorsing a specific 'bipartisan framework' bill or proposal by that description.

inaccurate_statement: Bresnahan supports utilizing hybrid surveillance technology at the border
description: No record exists of Bresnahan specifically proposing or endorsing 'hybrid surveillance technology' at the border. His documented immigration/border positions center on supporting a border wall, backing the Secure America Act for ICE/CBP funding, and prioritizing removal of violent criminals — not a specific surveillance-technology proposal.

inaccurate_statement: Bresnahan opposes federal funding mechanisms that do not mandate strict legal status verification
description: No documented statement or legislative action ties Bresnahan to this specific funding-mechanism position. His confirmed record includes opposing use of taxpayer funds to relocate undocumented immigrants into communities and supporting increased ICE/CBP funding, but not this specific 'legal status verification' funding condition as described.

inaccurate_statement: Cognetti supports government-mandated price caps on prescription drugs and heavy regulation of private insurers
description: Cognetti's own campaign platform (paigeforpa.com/priorities) does not state support for "government-mandated price caps on prescription drugs" or "heavy regulation of private insurers" in those terms. What she actually pledges is to "Prevent healthcare industry middlemen from denying care and medications prescribed by doctors" and to "Reform the insurance system so that when people pay for insurance, they can expect to be protected when something happens." News coverage of the race likewise describes her health care emphasis as "protecting Medicare and Medicaid while expanding affordable care and behavioral health services," not price caps. While her platform is broadly consumer-protection-oriented toward insurers and PBM-style middlemen—so the claim isn't a total fabrication—the specific, loaded framing of "price caps" and "heavy regulation of private insurers" overstates and mischaracterizes her actual stated position, making this a minor policy-position inaccuracy rather than a fabricated claim.

inaccurate_statement: Bresnahan favors market-based competition over federal subsidies for the ACA and reforming the system to reduce federal spending
description: Bresnahan actually voted in January 2026 to extend enhanced ACA premium tax credits for three years, crossing party lines to support continued federal subsidies, arguing that letting them expire would cause immediate premium increases for constituents. Characterizing him as simply favoring reduced federal subsidies over market competition omits this documented vote and creates a misleading picture of his actual ACA position.

inaccurate_statement: Bresnahan aligns with conservative proposals to reduce federal Medicaid match rates to states to cut the deficit
description: No record exists of Bresnahan proposing to reduce federal Medicaid match rates to states. His documented position is the opposite in tone: he and 11 other House Republicans sent a letter to leadership stating they would not support a reconciliation bill that reduces Medicaid coverage for vulnerable populations, and he argued that the bill's work requirements do not equate to cutting Medicaid.

inaccurate_statement: Bresnahan supports fiscal policies aimed at curbing federal government match rates for entitlement spending
description: Bresnahan's own official press release and multiple news reports state he did the opposite of what the claim asserts: he blocked/opposed proposals in the reconciliation bill (H.R. 1) that would have lowered the Provider Tax and FMAP (federal match rate) percentages for Medicaid expansion, and he touted this as protecting Medicaid funding. The claim that he 'supports fiscal policies aimed at curbing federal government match rates for entitlement spending' misrepresents his documented, publicly stated position and would materially mislead readers about his stance on entitlement/Medicaid funding.

inaccurate_statement: Paige Cognetti's platform centers more on government reform and local infrastructure rather than emphasizing criminal justice enforcement, without addressing public safety
description: This mischaracterizes Cognetti's platform by omitting her substantial public-safety record and positions. As mayor she has pursued hiring additional police officers, over $5M in police equipment/training spending, a planned police command center, new police vehicles, a citywide camera network, a Real Time Crime Center, and a 22% increase in the police department's operating budget, and her congressional platform includes support for stronger federal law enforcement funding and cooperation on gangs, guns, and drugs. Describing her as focused only on anti-corruption and infrastructure while implying she does not emphasize criminal justice/public safety significantly understates her actual public-safety record and positioning.

inaccurate_statement: As a Republican incumbent, Bresnahan generally aligns with traditional conservative platforms that strongly emphasize explicit support for law enforcement, often referred to as 'Back the Blue,' focusing heavily on increasing funding for local police forces and resisting redirecting police funding toward social services
description: This is a generic party-alignment inference rather than a documented specific Bresnahan statement. His actual, confirmed record shows specific concrete actions on public safety funding (securing federal grants for Wilkes-Barre PD, Kingston Borough PD, and Scranton PD technology), which the response omits in favor of a generic 'Back the Blue' framing not directly sourced to him.

inaccurate_statement: Cognetti generally aligns with the broader state-level Democratic strategy regarding the technology sector rather than having her own distinct data-center platform
description: Search results directly contradict this claim. Cognetti has a detailed, distinct, and prominently promoted data-center platform, not a generic alignment with state-level Democratic strategy. Per an AP/Inquirer report, her campaign ran a $200,000 TV ad in which she personally laid out specific policy demands: 'Big Tech needs to pay their own way. Not hide behind NDAs. No tax breaks. Don't raise our electric bills, don't poison our water. And hire local, union labor.' She also specifically attacked her opponent Bresnahan for owning stock in data-center-linked companies, and her plan (ending tax breaks, requiring local hiring, protecting waterways and utility bills) is described as her own distinct proposal, separate from Bresnahan's competing 'Local Control Protection Act.' This is a signature, individualized issue in her campaign against Rep. Bresnahan, not simply a reflection of generic state Democratic Party messaging on tech. The claim mischaracterizes her position and would materially mislead a reader about how central and distinctive this issue is to her campaign.

inaccurate_statement: Cognetti equates unchecked data centers to historical extractive coal and gas industries that left environmental damage behind
description: Cognetti's documented data-center messaging uses the framing 'Big companies have come before, taken what they wanted and left us with their mess to clean up. Now it's data centers' — a similar sentiment about extractive industries generally, but not a documented direct statement specifically equating data centers to coal and gas industries by name.

inaccurate_statement: Bresnahan previously expressed an overtly friendly stance toward data centers, calling them catalysts for economic growth
description: No direct quote or statement from Bresnahan calling data centers themselves 'catalysts for economic growth' is documented. He did celebrate a $25 billion Blackstone natural-gas power investment tied to rising power demand including data centers, which is a related but distinct claim, and his primary public data-center framing has been the more skeptical 'Local Control Protection Act' messaging about protecting communities from corporate overreach, not an enthusiastic embrace of data centers as growth catalysts.

inaccurate_statement: Bresnahan faced scrutiny for holding personal stock investments in Blackstone and Credo Technology, companies that benefit from the data center boom
description: While Bresnahan's extensive stock trading activity (600-650 trades in 2025) is well documented and controversial, no record exists of these two specific named holdings (Blackstone and Credo Technology) tied to data centers. This appears to be a fabricated or unsubstantiated specific detail layered onto an otherwise real controversy.

inaccurate_statement: Cognetti supports federal funding to upgrade border screening tech and add border patrol personnel
description: No record exists of Cognetti proposing specific funding for border screening technology upgrades or additional border patrol personnel. Her documented immigration positions involve calling for a secure border in general terms, opposing large-scale detention facilities, supporting pathways to citizenship for Dreamers/essential workers, and opposing local police cooperation with ICE — but no specific mechanism involving funding scanners or hiring more border patrol agents is on record for her.

inaccurate_statement: Cognetti's platform emphasizes expanding access to substance abuse treatment, behavioral health services, and community prevention programs specifically as part of her fentanyl-crisis approach.
description: Cognetti's official campaign 'Priorities' page (paigeforpa.com/priorities) contains no mention of fentanyl, opioids, substance abuse treatment, behavioral health services, or community prevention programs whatsoever — her stated platform centers on anti-corruption (banning congressional stock trading, no corporate PAC money), healthcare affordability/insurance reform, union strength, manufacturing, and opposing data center development. The only documented public comments tying Cognetti to fentanyl are from a campaign spokesperson framing it in the context of border security, stating she 'has seen what the scourge of Fentanyl has done to our community and has said that President Biden didn't do enough to secure the southern border' — an immigration/border-enforcement framing, not a treatment/behavioral-health/prevention framing. There is no evidence she has articulated a distinct 'fentanyl-crisis approach' built around expanding treatment access, behavioral health services, and community prevention programs. This claim appears to invent a policy position not found in her platform or public statements.

inaccurate_statement: Cognetti supports the 'Stop Fentanyl at the Border Act' and increased hiring of thousands of additional CBP personnel, border patrol agents, and drug enforcement officers.
description: The 'Stop Fentanyl at the Border Act' (H.R. 8992, 118th Congress) was introduced by Rep. Gabe Vasquez (D-NM-02) with Reps. Lori Chavez-DeRemer and Eric Sorensen; the Senate version was introduced by Sens. Luján, Cortez Masto, Casey, and Kelly. Paige Cognetti, who is the Mayor of Scranton and a candidate (not incumbent) for PA-08, has never served in Congress and therefore could not have sponsored, cosponsored, or voted on this bill. No search results connect her to this legislation or to a stated position supporting it and the specific CBP/border patrol hiring increases described. This appears to be a fabricated or misattributed claim rather than a real, verifiable position taken by Cognetti.

inaccurate_statement: Cognetti's platform emphasizes international diplomacy to pressure foreign governments to crack down on drug supply chains at the source.
description: Cognetti's official campaign website 'Priorities' page (paigeforpa.com/priorities/) was fetched directly and contains no mention of international diplomacy, foreign governments, or drug supply chains. Her stated platform focuses on anti-corruption (banning congressional stock trading, rejecting corporate PAC money, auditing government), economic issues (breaking up monopolies, strengthening unions, healthcare reform, paid family leave), manufacturing/tariffs, and opposing data center development in NEPA. No web search results connect Cognetti to any statement or position about pressuring foreign governments to crack down on drug supply chains at the source. This appears to be a fabricated claim with no basis in her actual platform, and since it invents an entirely new policy area (foreign policy/drug interdiction diplomacy) that isn't part of her real platform, it would materially mislead a reader about her actual priorities.

inaccurate_statement: Bresnahan sponsored and supported legislation targeting specific out-of-pocket medical expenses, such as introducing the bipartisan FLIGHT DECK Act and the INSULIN Act to cap monthly insulin costs at $35 for patients with diabetes
description: No record exists of Rob Bresnahan introducing or sponsoring a 'FLIGHT DECK Act' or an 'INSULIN Act' capping insulin costs at $35 per month. His documented healthcare-cost work includes the PBM Reform Act, the Protect Seniors and Veterans from Healthcare Fraud Act, intervention in a UnitedHealthcare/Jefferson Health contract dispute, and involvement with Rural Health Transformation Fund money — none of which involve these named bills. A federal $35 insulin cap was already enacted via the Inflation Reduction Act for Medicare beneficiaries under the Biden administration, not through legislation attributed to Bresnahan. This appears to be a fabricated legislative claim, though it is a narrow item within an otherwise accurate overview of his broader healthcare-cost messaging.

inaccurate_statement: Opponents argue that Bresnahan's votes on broad federal budget reconciliation and tariff policies have contributed to rising health insurance and household expenses
description: This is broadly consistent with real, documented criticism of Bresnahan's reconciliation-bill vote and its projected Medicaid coverage effects, but the response does not specify that Bresnahan personally opposes broad tariffs — in fact he has voted to continue or protect Trump-era tariff policies, so framing 'tariff policies' as a shared point of criticism without noting his actual support for them risks blurring his real position; however, the overall thrust that critics tie his votes to rising costs is accurate and this is a narrow framing issue rather than a reversal of a documented fact.

inaccurate_statement: Rob Bresnahan aligns with budget approaches that target federal spending and deficit reduction, framed as his overall healthcare stance without noting his vote to extend ACA premium tax credits or his letter opposing Medicaid coverage reductions
description: Bresnahan's actual record on healthcare is more mixed than a simple fiscal-restraint framing suggests: he voted to extend enhanced ACA premium tax credits for three years, arguing that letting them lapse would cause immediate premium increases, and he and 11 other House Republicans sent a letter to leadership stating they would not support a reconciliation bill that reduced Medicaid coverage for vulnerable populations. He did vote for the reconciliation bill that CBO projects will cut Medicaid spending and reduce coverage.
