inaccurate_statement: Cognetti's platform centers on cutting administrative red tape for local permitting and speeding up infrastructure as her housing-cost approach
description: No federal congressional-campaign statement was found addressing housing costs specifically; her documented housing-related record exists primarily at the municipal level (a $125,000 affordable-housing grant, a touted goal of 1,000 new housing units, and the December 2025 Hilltop Heights affordable-housing groundbreaking), not as an articulated federal platform plank framed around cutting permitting red tape. The response substitutes a general infrastructure/anti-corruption framing for a housing-specific position that isn't clearly documented as her stated federal approach.

inaccurate_statement: Bresnahan's platform focuses on cutting government regulations and building costs for developers to encourage housing supply, framed as his primary approach to housing
description: Bresnahan's specific, documented housing-related actions are backing the 'Housing for the 21st Century Act' (aimed at reducing consumer costs and streamlining homebuilding) and the '21st Century ROAD to Housing Act' (restricting large institutional investors from buying additional single-family homes), plus permanent funding for the Low-Income Water Assistance Program. The response's generic 'cut red tape for developers' framing omits these specific, more targeted housing bills and instead presents a vaguer general deregulation narrative not clearly tied to his actual housing platform.

inaccurate_statement: Bresnahan's portfolio is managed entirely by financial advisors under standard, long-term retirement and wealth management strategies, with no direct personal involvement
description: This presents Bresnahan's defense as an unqualified fact rather than a disputed claim. Audio obtained by NOTUS shows Bresnahan himself describing active dialogue with his financial adviser about 'what different positions are coming up' in April 2025, directly contradicting his later claim of no such dialogue and his campaign's assertion that he never personally traded his own stocks. The response states his campaign's framing without noting this documented contradiction.

inaccurate_statement: Bresnahan's camp has maintained that his portfolio is managed by independent financial advisors through broad risk-tolerance strategies rather than individual day-to-day trades directed by him
description: Audio obtained by NOTUS shows Bresnahan describing active dialogue with his financial adviser about 'what different positions are coming up' in April 2025, directly contradicting his later claim in a June 2025 tele-town-hall that he does 'not have any dialogues with my financial advisers,' and his campaign has claimed he 'has never traded his own stocks' even as he made roughly 600-650 individual stock trades in 2025. The response's framing that his camp's account of hands-off, advisor-managed trading is an uncontested characterization omits this documented inconsistency and the extensive, well-corroborated controversy around his personal involvement in trading decisions.

inaccurate_statement: Changes to maternity leave provisions affected the police department's collective bargaining agreement in the same way as the clerical workers' agreement
description: The specific unpaid-FMLA-for-new-hires vs. 12-weeks-paid-for-pre-2021-hires provision was directly confirmed only for the Clerical Workers Local 2462 bargaining unit. Other city bargaining units, including the police department, may have separately negotiated terms that were not independently verified to contain the identical maternity-leave structure, so presenting the police department's contract as having the same specific change is not substantiated by the available record.

inaccurate_statement: Implicit framing that Cognetti's actual position amounts to supporting "open borders" or illegal immigration
description: No source found describes Cognetti as using "open borders" language or supporting illegal immigration generally; her documented record includes a real, acknowledged shift over time (from Biden-era-supportive statements in 2021/2023 to calling Biden's border handling "a huge misstep" in 2026), support for a pathway to citizenship for Dreamers/essential workers, and a statement that Scranton is not a sanctuary city and would not obstruct lawful ICE warrants. The response correctly attributes the "open borders" characterization to opponents/critics rather than stating it as fact, which is accurate framing, but does not mention the documented evolution in her position or her more security-oriented 2026 statements, giving an incomplete picture.

inaccurate_statement: Cognetti's financial disclosures revealed a net worth placing her well above the median household income of her district, leading opponents to label her a 'millionaire mayor'
description: No record exists of any financial disclosure showing Cognetti has a net worth substantially above the district median or of a 'millionaire mayor' label being applied to her. Her documented biography (English teacher, Treasury Department advisor, mayor) does not indicate substantial personal wealth, and no source describes her financial disclosures or a net-worth-based nickname of this kind. This appears to be an invented claim not grounded in any documented reporting on her finances.

inaccurate_statement: Bresnahan's legal counsel defended the helicopter omission, stating the aircraft was a business asset of his LLC and federal rules only require reporting the total value of the business interest rather than individual equipment
description: No record exists of Bresnahan's legal counsel offering this specific defense or rationale about LLC business-asset reporting rules. His office's actual documented response was that he 'has gone above and beyond to disclose all assets as required by law' — a general assertion of compliance, not this specific legal argument about business-interest valuation reporting. The complaint's existence and his office's general rebuttal are real, but this particular legal-counsel statement and rationale is not corroborated.

inaccurate_statement: Critics accused Bresnahan of attempting to obscure tracking data for the helicopter aircraft
description: No record supports a specific allegation that Bresnahan attempted to obscure or alter tracking data for the helicopter. The documented controversy centers on non-disclosure of the asset and questions about undisclosed campaign-related flights, not tampering with or obscuring aircraft tracking data.

inaccurate_statement: Watchdog groups accused Bresnahan of attempting to hide the helicopter's travel history on flight tracking sites
description: The documented helicopter controversy centers on non-disclosure of ownership and undisclosed flights (20+ documented flights), with his office responding that he has disclosed all required assets. No record exists of a specific accusation that he tried to hide or manipulate the helicopter's history on flight-tracking websites — this specific detail appears to be an embellishment not found in the underlying reporting.

inaccurate_statement: Watchdog groups questioned whether flights around his district and out-of-state constituted unreported in-kind campaign contributions
description: The documented controversy concerns non-disclosure of the helicopter as an asset, not a specific in-kind-campaign-contribution theory about individual flights. No source ties this specific in-kind-contribution framing to the helicopter complaint.

inaccurate_statement: Bresnahan's legal counsel dismissed the helicopter allegations as an "egregious lie"
description: The documented response from Bresnahan's office was that he "has gone above and beyond to disclose all assets as required by law" — a measured denial, not the specific quoted phrase "egregious lie," which does not appear in the available record of his office's response.

inaccurate_statement: Critics pointed out that Bresnahan's Medicaid-related votes coincided with financial moves such as selling off hospital development authority bonds
description: The well-documented financial-timing controversy involves Bresnahan selling stock in health insurers (Centene, Elevance Health, UnitedHealth, CVS Health) roughly a week before his vote for the Medicaid-cutting reconciliation bill, and a later shift into bonds/municipal securities in 2026 generally. There is no record of a specific claim about him selling "hospital development authority bonds" tied to the Medicaid vote timing — this appears to be a fabricated or garbled detail conflating the real stock-sale timing story with an invented bond transaction.

inaccurate_statement: The helicopter was valued between $1 million and $1.5 million
description: The knowledge base confirms the helicopter's reported value as 'up to $1.5 million' but does not establish a $1 million floor for this range; this is a minor imprecision rather than a substantive misstatement of the underlying allegation.

inaccurate_statement: Her administration earned fiscal management and municipal excellence awards
description: No record of specific named fiscal management or municipal excellence awards for Cognetti's administration appears in available material. Her documented fiscal accomplishments are the Act 47 exit and a bond-rating upgrade from junk to investment grade, but no specific awards are confirmed.

inaccurate_statement: Advocates for prohibiting members of Congress from serving on corporate boards, implementing term limits, and enforcing 'No Budget, No Pay' rules for Congress
description: Cognetti's documented anti-corruption platform includes banning congressional stock trading and increasing ethics/accountability measures, but no source ties her specifically to proposals banning corporate board service, congressional term limits, or a 'No Budget, No Pay' rule. These specific mechanisms are not found in her platform materials and appear to be invented elaborations beyond her actual documented anti-corruption planks.

inaccurate_statement: Promotes transparency, independent agency audits to eliminate waste and fraud, and merit-based hiring to combat nepotism and cronyism
description: Cognetti has called for a targeted federal audit to identify waste, fraud, and abuse, which is documented. However, no source supports a specific platform plank about 'merit-based hiring to combat nepotism and cronyism' — this appears to be an invented addition beyond her actual documented anti-corruption positions.

inaccurate_statement: Cognetti supports preserving and expanding access to affordable healthcare (implying an expansion beyond her documented ACA/Medicaid protections)
description: Cognetti's documented healthcare platform commits to protecting Medicaid and marketplace/ACA access and ending healthcare-middleman practices, but no source describes a broader specific 'expanding access' proposal beyond these planks. This is a mild overstatement/generalization of an otherwise accurate healthcare position rather than a contradiction of her record.

inaccurate_statement: Bresnahan advocates for reversing prior border policies to stop the flow of illegal drugs and unauthorized crossings
description: Bresnahan's border/immigration messaging that currently appears on his campaign materials includes stale 2024-cycle language referencing reversing 'Biden/Harris' era border policies; his more current and reliable record centers on votes like the Secure America Act and participation in immigration forums rather than a generic 'reversing prior policies' framing. This is a minor imprecision in framing rather than a substantive misrepresentation of his border-security stance.

inaccurate_statement: Bresnahan has co-sponsored legislation like the Fair Wage Act to raise the federal minimum wage scaled to the regional cost of living
description: There is no record of Bresnahan cosponsoring a bill called the 'Fair Wage Act' tied to regional cost-of-living minimum wage adjustments. The available record does confirm he has backed a minimum-wage increase in some general form, but this specific bill name and mechanism is not substantiated and appears to be an invented or misattributed detail.

inaccurate_statement: Cognetti called Bresnahan's pattern of behavior (regarding the financial-adviser contradiction) 'sickening' and dishonest
description: The word 'sickening' in the record refers to Bresnahan's own 2024 description of congressional stock trading in general (he called stock trading 'sickening' when pledging to ban it), not a quote from Cognetti characterizing his adviser-contact contradiction. No source shows Cognetti using the word 'sickening' to describe this specific inconsistency.

inaccurate_statement: Cognetti claimed Bresnahan profited off selling defense stocks right before voting on related legislation
description: The well-documented instance of Cognetti's criticism involves Bresnahan selling stock in healthcare/Medicaid-managed-care companies (Centene, Elevance Health, UnitedHealth, CVS Health) shortly before a vote cutting Medicaid funding. No record exists of a parallel claim about him selling defense stocks before a related vote — this appears to be an invented elaboration alongside the accurate Medicaid-stock claim.

inaccurate_statement: Cognetti attacked Bresnahan's votes regarding military funding and overseas conflicts, claiming he benefited personally by purchasing defense stocks prior to policy developments
description: No record exists of Cognetti making a specific claim that Bresnahan purchased defense stocks prior to military/foreign-policy developments to benefit personally. The documented stock-trading criticism from Cognetti centers on his overall high trade volume and specifically on healthcare-related stocks sold shortly before a Medicaid-cutting vote, not defense/foreign-policy-related trades. This appears to be an invented extension of the real stock-trading controversy rather than a documented criticism she made.

inaccurate_statement: Bresnahan's campaign has criticized Cognetti's background as a former Goldman Sachs banker
description: The available research on Cognetti's professional background does not describe her as a 'former Goldman Sachs banker' in the sense of a defining prior career element highlighted in this race — her career included fundraising for Democratic campaigns, a Treasury Department role, work with the PA Auditor General, and being a Scranton School Board member before becoming mayor. A separate accuracy sweep of this race did confirm she worked in wealth management at Goldman Sachs at some point, but no source in either candidate's record ties Bresnahan's campaign specifically to raising her Goldman Sachs background as a line of attack, or to a claim that she is hypocritical for attacking his business wealth while having her own affluent background — this specific attack line is not documented.

inaccurate_statement: Bresnahan's campaign pointed to reports regarding an unlisted second home near Elk Mountain on Cognetti's financial disclosures
description: No record exists in the available research of any claim involving an undisclosed second home near Elk Mountain on Cognetti's financial disclosures, nor of Bresnahan's campaign raising this specific allegation. This appears to be an invented detail not found in any documented reporting on the race.

inaccurate_statement: Bresnahan's team, partnering with national Republican campaign committees, has criticized Cognetti's mayoral record on public safety, alleging she minimized rising crime rates, limited police enforcement capabilities, and mishandled local administrative appointments
description: Republican attacks on Cognetti's crime record are real and documented, but an independent, neutral news analysis (WVIA) found these attacks to be 'partially misleading' — serious crime in Scranton is actually down 4.1% from 2021–2025 on the most reliable data window, with opposition messaging selectively choosing narrower date ranges/categories to suggest an increase. The response repeats the Republican attack framing without this important context. Additionally, no source found ties Bresnahan's campaign to a specific claim about Cognetti 'limiting police enforcement capabilities' or 'mishandling local administrative appointments' as phrased — the documented controversy involves a specific appointee (Michael Villa) to the Human Relations Commission and the city's delayed criminal-background-check policy for appointees, not a general 'mishandled administrative appointments' framing attributed to Bresnahan's campaign specifically.

inaccurate_statement: As Mayor of Scranton, Cognetti fought water, sewer, and gas utility rate hikes
description: No record exists of Cognetti, as Scranton mayor, fighting water, sewer, or gas utility rate hikes. Her documented utility-related advocacy is limited to opposing electric-bill increases specifically tied to data-center development, and her broader cost-of-living platform addresses credit-card fees, monopolies, and insurance reform rather than water, sewer, or gas utility rate hikes. This appears to be an invented elaboration rather than a documented position or action.

inaccurate_statement: A projected $5.7 million is specifically dedicated to stormwater management projects in Keyser Valley
description: The dossier documents a $6.4 million proposed Keyser Valley flood project, not a $5.7 million figure. This appears to be a numerical discrepancy from the confirmed figure.

inaccurate_statement: Regarding flood management systems specifically, public records from his office primarily emphasize structural transportation investments, roads, bridges, and rail/air safety, rather than standalone municipal flood control programs.
description: This significantly understates Bresnahan's documented flood-management record, which is actually the single most detailed and specific platform item found for him on any topic. He is a member of the Flood Resiliency Caucus and the American Flood Coalition, publicly urged FEMA to reinstate the canceled BRIC program, championed expansion of Section 566 of the Water Resources Development Act of 2026 to extend Army Corps of Engineers water-infrastructure partnership eligibility to the Upper Delaware River Basin and raise program authorization from $20M to $92.69M, and announced flood-adjacent wastewater/stormwater funding including $1.25M for Monroe County, $1M for the Dallas Area Municipal Authority, and $8M for an Exeter sewer/stormwater project. The response's framing that his office lacks standalone flood-control initiatives is contradicted by this substantial, specific record.

inaccurate_statement: As Mayor of Scranton, Cognetti joined other U.S. mayors in calling on federal leaders to pursue swift immigration reforms and executive actions to protect undocumented workers from deportation
description: No record exists of Cognetti joining a coalition of U.S. mayors calling for federal immigration reform or executive action to protect undocumented workers. Her documented immigration-related actions are specific to Scranton policy (declining local police involvement in ICE enforcement) and a general, evolving public stance on border security, not participation in a multi-mayor national advocacy effort. This is a narrow, unsubstantiated addition rather than a claim that changes the overall picture of her position.

inaccurate_statement: Cognetti's approach to immigration focuses primarily on comprehensive reform, labor needs, and legal pathways rather than traditional physical border enforcement measures, with her platform centering on managing immigration through systematic reform and workforce integration rather than border security enforcement mechanisms
description: This framing omits Cognetti's own documented statements supporting border security, including calling border security 'very, very important,' describing Biden's border handling as 'a huge misstep' and 'really terrible,' and stating that if ICE comes with lawful warrants in Lackawanna County they will be able to execute them. Her position is more accurately described as combining stated support for a secure border with legal pathways and reform, not a rejection of border enforcement as a priority.

inaccurate_statement: Cognetti's platform includes introducing term limits for public officials
description: No source describes Cognetti proposing or supporting term limits for public officials. Her documented anti-corruption platform centers on banning congressional stock trading, transparency measures, and rejecting corporate PAC money, but term limits for officials is not among her stated positions in the available material.

inaccurate_statement: As a former small business owner and entrepreneur
description: Bresnahan is not accurately described as a 'former' small business owner — he became CEO of Kuharchik Construction in 2013 and there is no indication he has divested from or left the company; he is generally described as a current business owner/CEO who continues to run the company while serving in Congress, not a past owner.

inaccurate_statement: She initially won a 2019 special election as an Independent after the previous mayor resigned due to corruption charges
description: The prior Scranton mayor pleaded guilty to federal corruption charges rather than simply resigning due to them; the pleading-guilty detail is the documented characterization, though the underlying connection between the scandal and her opportunity to run is accurate.

inaccurate_statement: She worked as an advisor to the Pennsylvania Auditor General on public school oversight
description: Cognetti's role under Pennsylvania Auditor General Eugene DePasquale was as Special Assistant focusing on government waste/fraud/nursing-home oversight, not specifically public school oversight. This is a narrow mischaracterization of the focus area of a real position she held.

inaccurate_statement: Kuharchik Construction is described as a 'third-generation' family company
description: Bresnahan became CFO of his grandfather Walt Kuharchik's electrical contracting business at age 19 and later became CEO — this makes him the second generation of family involvement (grandfather to grandson), not clearly a 'third-generation' company as the response states. No source confirms a third generation of ownership/leadership.

inaccurate_statement: Cognetti was appointed to the U.S. Trade Representative's Advisory Committee on Trade Policy by President Joe Biden, implying a 2009-2012 Treasury tenure timeframe attribution
description: The dossier confirms Cognetti served at Treasury during the Obama administration and was later appointed to the USTR advisory committee in 2024 under Biden; the response's specific parenthetical '(2009–2012)' for her Treasury tenure is a specific date range not confirmed in the available material, though her general Treasury service under Obama is accurate. This is a narrow, unconfirmed specific detail rather than a contradiction of her broader biography.

inaccurate_statement: Rob Bresnahan Jr.'s platform highlights his focus on protecting and strengthening safety-net programs like Medicaid and Social Security/Medicare
description: Bresnahan has publicly stated he opposes cuts to Medicare and Social Security and has taken some actions framed as protecting healthcare access, but this framing omits the significant tension with his vote for the reconciliation bill (OBBBA), which nonpartisan analysts (CBO, Center on Budget and Policy Priorities) project will cut Medicaid spending substantially and cause roughly 28,000 people in his district to lose coverage from new work requirements. Presenting his position as simply 'protecting and strengthening' Medicaid without any mention of this voting record creates a one-sided impression that doesn't reflect the documented conflict between his messaging and his actual vote.

inaccurate_statement: Rob Bresnahan's campaign focuses primarily on cutting red tape, unleashing the economy, and supporting small businesses and working families, without a primary platform centered on opposing data centers.
description: Bresnahan introduced the "Local Control Protection Act," a specific piece of legislation that would restrict corporations from suing municipalities that reject data-center zoning applications and require developers to sign community benefit agreements or forfeit federal tax incentives. He has made public statements framing this as a local-control response to data-center development ("We should never let billion-dollar corporations supersede the voices of those who live in the community"). This is a real, direct-statement platform item specifically on data centers, so the claim that he lacks any platform position on the issue is inaccurate.

inaccurate_statement: Cognetti's economic platform includes streamlining and lowering municipal permit fees as a federal campaign focus
description: Cognetti's federal campaign platform focuses on capping credit card fees, breaking up monopolies, ending healthcare middleman practices, and reducing red tape generally, but no source ties her congressional platform specifically to 'lowering municipal permit fees.' Her documented mayoral record does include cutting red tape that facilitated new housing and business permits in Scranton, but presenting 'lowering municipal permit fees' as a current congressional platform plank conflates her mayoral record with her federal campaign positions, which is a distinction her own materials draw carefully.

inaccurate_statement: Cognetti supports investments in domestic supply chains to stabilize prices as part of her affordability platform.
description: Cognetti's published platform addresses affordability through capping credit-card/junk fees, breaking up monopolies, opposing broad tariffs, and reforming insurance, but no source ties her to a specific proposal about investing in domestic supply chains to stabilize prices. This appears to be an invented elaboration rather than a documented part of her platform, though it doesn't contradict the broader thrust of her affordability messaging.

inaccurate_statement: Paige Cognetti is described as 'the former mayor of Scranton'
description: Paige Cognetti is the sitting, current Mayor of Scranton — she has not resigned or left office, and won decisive re-election in November 2025 while simultaneously running for Congress. Describing her only as a 'former mayor' misrepresents her current role and status.

inaccurate_statement: He advocates for expanding technical and trade apprenticeship programs
description: While Bresnahan has supported workforce-development initiatives generally (e.g., funding for a Career and Technical Center in Pike County), no specific documented platform plank about 'technical and trade apprenticeship programs' as a named priority was found in the available record; this is a narrow, unverified elaboration on his jobs platform.

inaccurate_statement: Referring to Paige Cognetti as 'Paige Gebhardt Cognetti' and describing her as a 'past or prospective challenger' alongside former Rep. Matt Cartwright, implying ambiguity about who the actual 2026 Democratic nominee is
description: Paige Cognetti is the confirmed 2026 Democratic nominee running against incumbent Rob Bresnahan in the current PA-08 general election, not a hypothetical or past challenger grouped loosely with former Rep. Matt Cartwright (who last represented the district before Bresnahan and is not on the 2026 ballot). This framing obscures who is actually running and understates that this is a direct, two-candidate contest.

inaccurate_statement: Bresnahan's efforts included 'coordinating the retention and reopening' of the Regional Hospital of Scranton, implying he was the primary broker
description: Bresnahan's own contemporaneous statement described the hospital deal as a 'positive step' where he would 'continue to work closely with' other local, state, and federal leaders — a more modest, supportive role than being the primary coordinator or broker. Neutral reporting credits the deal's momentum mainly to local community foundations and state/gubernatorial officials, with Bresnahan as one of several supportive stakeholders rather than the chief architect.

inaccurate_statement: Bresnahan co-sponsored bills extending ACA premium tax credits
description: Bresnahan voted for a three-year extension of enhanced ACA premium tax credits, but the record does not describe him as a co-sponsor of specific legislative packages doing so; he is documented as having voted for this policy, and separately voted for a December 2025 Republican healthcare bill that did not extend the credits, reflecting a more complicated voting history than simple co-sponsorship.

inaccurate_statement: Referring to Paige Cognetti as 'Paige Gebhardt Cognetti' and describing her as a 'past or prospective challenger' alongside former Rep. Matt Cartwright, implying ambiguity about who the actual 2026 Democratic nominee is
description: Paige Cognetti is the confirmed 2026 Democratic nominee running against incumbent Rob Bresnahan in the current PA-08 general election, not a hypothetical or past challenger grouped loosely with former Rep. Matt Cartwright (who last represented the district before Bresnahan and is not on the 2026 ballot). This framing obscures who is actually running and understates that this is a direct, two-candidate contest.

inaccurate_statement: Paige Cognetti is described as 'former Mayor of Scranton'
description: Paige Cognetti is the sitting, current Mayor of Scranton — she has not resigned or left office. She announced her congressional campaign in September 2025 while simultaneously running for and winning re-election as mayor in November 2025, and continues to serve as mayor while campaigning for Congress. Describing her as a 'former mayor' misrepresents her current role and status in the race.

inaccurate_statement: Bresnahan co-led safety measures like the Railway Safety Act
description: No record exists of Bresnahan co-leading or sponsoring the Railway Safety Act. His documented flood/infrastructure/transportation record includes the Flood Resiliency Caucus, American Flood Coalition membership, BRIC program advocacy, WRDA Section 566 expansion, the BASICS Act, and Wallenpaupack Creek Bridge funding — none of which involve a Railway Safety Act co-leadership role. This appears to be an unsupported addition rather than a documented part of his platform.

inaccurate_statement: Cognetti supports raising or indexing the minimum wage to match the cost of living.
description: No statement in Cognetti's documented platform or campaign materials addresses a minimum wage increase or indexing the minimum wage to cost of living. Her affordability platform is documented as centering on capping credit-card/junk fees, breaking up monopolies, paid family leave, affordable childcare, ending healthcare middleman practices, and opposing broad tariffs — not a minimum-wage proposal. This is a narrow, unsupported addition rather than a claim that upends the broader accurate characterization of her affordability focus.

inaccurate_statement: Paige Cognetti is described as 'the former mayor of Scranton'
description: Paige Cognetti is the sitting, current Mayor of Scranton — she has not resigned or left office. She is running for Congress while continuing to serve as mayor, having just won decisive re-election as mayor in November 2025. Describing her only as a 'former mayor' misrepresents her current status.

inaccurate_statement: Paige Cognetti's platform includes an emphasis on 'targeted border technology' at ports of entry
description: No evidence supports this claim. Cognetti's official campaign platform page (paigeforpa.com/priorities/) contains no mention of border security, immigration, or border technology at all — her platform focuses on anti-corruption, economic issues, and opposing data center development. Extensive news coverage of her immigration/border positions (e.g., Washington Examiner and Fox News pieces) documents her general comments about supporting 'a secure border,' concerns about fentanyl, and past support for a path to citizenship/amnesty — but none reference 'targeted border technology' at ports of entry as a platform element. This specific, distinctive policy detail appears nowhere in her campaign materials or press coverage, indicating it was fabricated rather than a paraphrase of a real position.

inaccurate_statement: Cognetti aligns with Democratic strategies focused on government intervention, including empowering Medicare to negotiate prescription drug prices directly, capping out-of-pocket costs for seniors, and penalizing manufacturers for excessive price increases
description: Cognetti's official campaign 'Priorities' page does not mention Medicare negotiating drug prices directly, capping out-of-pocket costs for seniors, or penalizing manufacturers for price increases (these are IRA provisions). Her actual documented healthcare priorities focus on different specifics: preventing PBM/insurance middlemen from denying prescribed care and medications, and broader insurance reform. A district-analysis news article explicitly attributes the 'prescription drug costs' emphasis to Bresnahan's campaign, while describing Cognetti's health focus as 'protecting Medicare and Medicaid while expanding affordable care and behavioral health services' rather than the specific negotiation/cap/penalty mechanisms cited in the claim. The claim's broad framing that she 'aligns with Democratic strategies' on government intervention in drug pricing is plausible in spirit, but attributing these specific, itemized policy mechanisms to her is not supported by her own platform and is a narrow misattribution rather than reflecting a wholesale fabrication, so it is best characterized as minor.

inaccurate_statement: The $5 million state grant to Fidelity Bank was intended for a police real-time crime center facility.
description: The $5 million state grant awarded to Fidelity Bank in November 2024 was for renovating the historic Electric Building that Fidelity purchased in 2022 for its new headquarters — it was not for a police real-time crime center. A separate, unrelated city budget item involved Scranton purchasing Fidelity's old headquarters building for police/City-Hall-annex use, and a real-time crime center is a separate initiative referenced elsewhere; neither is documented as the purpose of the $5 million grant.

inaccurate_statement: Cognetti's campaign fundraising relies on support from labor unions representing workers including USW, AFA, AFSCME, and SMART.
description: USW, AFA, AFSCME, and SMART-TD are documented as endorsers of Cognetti's campaign, but the endorsement record does not establish that union support constitutes a significant direct source of her campaign's fundraising dollars. Her FEC financial breakdown shows individual contributions make up about 84% of her total receipts, with PAC/other-committee contributions (which would include any union PAC money) at only about 9%. Describing union support as a primary source of her fundraising overstates and conflates endorsement support with the actual composition of her campaign finance receipts.

inaccurate_statement: Applications for mail-in or absentee ballots must be received by your county election board by October 27, 2026
description: Pennsylvania's statutory deadline for mail-in/absentee ballot applications to be received by the county election board is the Tuesday before the election, which in 2026 falls on October 27 only if that is indeed the correct Tuesday — however, Pennsylvania law generally sets this deadline as 5:00 PM on the Tuesday prior to Election Day, not simply 'received by October 27' without a time specified; the response omits the specific cutoff time, which is a material detail for voters attempting to meet this deadline.

inaccurate_statement: Applications for mail-in or absentee ballots must be received by your county election board by October 27, 2026

inaccurate_statement: Earned a Bachelor of Arts in Business Administration from the University of Scranton in 2012
description: His degree is documented as a Bachelor of Science in Business Administration, not a Bachelor of Arts.

inaccurate_statement: Under his leadership, the firm expanded its workforce and operations across multiple states
description: Available records describe Kuharchik Construction as growing to 150+ employees and doing work including post-disaster power restoration, but there is no documented basis for a claim that its operations expanded across multiple states; the company is described as based in Exeter, Pennsylvania, serving the regional Northeastern Pennsylvania market.

inaccurate_statement: Stelson spent 30 years as a local news anchor before entering politics
description: Stelson's broadcast journalism career spanned nearly 40 years, with 26 years specifically as an anchor at WGAL-TV Lancaster (1997–2023); she also worked at other stations before that. The figure of exactly '30 years as a local news anchor' does not match either the well-documented 26-year WGAL tenure or the nearly-40-year overall career total.

inaccurate_statement: Stelson worked for 30 years as a television news anchor before entering politics
description: Stelson had a nearly 40-year broadcast journalism career overall, most prominently 26 years as an anchor at WGAL-TV in Lancaster, plus earlier stints at other stations; "30 years as a television news anchor" does not match either the ~40-year overall career figure or the specific 26-year anchor tenure documented.

inaccurate_statement: Stelson was a television news anchor for 30 years at WGAL.
description: Stelson anchored at WGAL-TV Lancaster for 26 years (1997–2023), not 30. Her overall broadcast journalism career spanned nearly 40 years across multiple stations, but her specific tenure at WGAL was 26 years.

inaccurate_statement: Stelson registered as a Democrat ahead of her initial 2023 run for Congress.
description: Stelson switched her registration from Republican to Democratic in February 2023, but she did not run for office in 2023 — her first candidacy was in the 2024 election cycle.

inaccurate_statement: Scott Perry holds a pro-life position and believes individual states should decide on abortion access
description: Perry's actual record on abortion is conflicting, not a clean states'-rights position. His campaign site states he supports exceptions for rape, incest, and life of the mother, and he supports IVF access (co-introducing the IVF Protection Act). However, he is also a current cosponsor of the federal Life at Conception Act, which would establish a national, federal definition of personhood from the moment of fertilization with no exceptions — the opposite of leaving the matter to individual states. Presenting his position as simply 'states should decide' omits this federal cosponsorship and the exceptions he has stated, giving an incomplete and partially inaccurate picture.

inaccurate_statement: Scott Perry opposes limits on presidential war powers
description: No record in Perry's documented platform or voting history directly states a position opposing limits on presidential war powers specifically; the dossier notes he voted against a House resolution requiring removal of U.S. forces from hostilities with Iran, which is consistent with this framing but is a narrower, different claim than a general opposition to war-powers limits.

inaccurate_statement: Perry voted against caps on insulin and prescription drug prices
description: Perry actually backed 2019-2020 Republican legislation (H.R. 19, the Lower Costs, More Cures Act) that capped seniors' out-of-pocket insulin costs at $50/month and created a Part D out-of-pocket cap. His more recent, current position is cosponsoring a 2025 bill to repeal Inflation Reduction Act drug-pricing provisions (including the $2,000 out-of-pocket cap on Part D drugs) and having previously voted against the Lower Drug Costs Now Act. Characterizing him as generally having voted against caps on drug/insulin prices oversimplifies a mixed record and is not fully accurate, though it does not fundamentally reverse the overall picture of his opposition to Democratic-led drug pricing measures.

inaccurate_statement: Unsealed records revealed that Perry embraced and tried to 'sell' a plan to have then-Vice President Mike Pence admit alternative testimony or block electoral votes prior to the counting on January 6, 2021
description: There is no record of this specific claim about Perry pressuring or trying to 'sell' a plan involving Pence's role in blocking electoral votes. The documented record centers on Perry's role in the Jeffrey Clark scheme and his contacts with Trump allies and the DOJ leadership dispute, not a Pence-pressure plot attributed to him specifically. This appears to be an embellishment not supported by the available record.

inaccurate_statement: In late 2025, Perry claimed during a radio appearance that Democratic lawmakers only join the military to 'get the credential' to run for office and that 'all their votes say they don't support America,' drawing bipartisan backlash
description: No record of this specific 2025 radio controversy involving Perry making these remarks about Democratic veterans in Congress exists in the available material. This is a specific, checkable claim with no corroboration, and does not match any documented controversy for Perry.

inaccurate_statement: In 2002, while running Hydrotech Mechanical Services, Perry was charged by Pennsylvania with forwarding altered reports at a sewage plant regarding chlorine and acidity levels, entered a rehabilitative program, paid a fine, and had the record expunged
description: No record of any such environmental charges, altered sewage-plant reports, or rehabilitative program involving Perry's mechanical contracting business exists in the available material, which does document his co-founding of a mechanical contracting business as part of his civilian career. This is a serious, specific criminal-adjacent allegation with no support, and if untrue would be a significant fabrication materially affecting the reader's impression of Perry's background.

inaccurate_statement: A federal court ruled in late 2023 that Perry's informal communications were not part of official duties, ordering him to hand over 1,659 texts and emails to federal prosecutors
description: The court ruling on the scope of Speech or Debate Clause protection and the resulting release of 1,659 messages occurred via a D.C. Circuit ruling reported as of December 2023, which is broadly consistent with this description, though the characterization as strictly 'ordering him to hand over' rather than allowing investigators access is a simplification. This is a close-enough match to the documented record to not be flagged as a substantive error beyond minor framing.

inaccurate_statement: Perry remains the only sitting member of Congress to have his phone seized in connection to this probe
description: No source in the available record confirms Perry is uniquely the only sitting member of Congress to have had a phone seized in the broader 'Arctic Frost' or January 6-related investigations; this specific superlative claim is not substantiated and could not be verified against the available documentation, which discusses Perry's seizure as notable but does not establish exclusivity.

inaccurate_statement: Unsealed court filings showed Perry actively messaged Meadows, RNC Chair Ronna McDaniel, and Pennsylvania state legislators to strategize delaying the electoral count, pushing audits, and proposing that Vice President Mike Pence alter the certification process
description: While Perry's general involvement in efforts to delay certification and his contacts with Meadows and other officials around the Jeffrey Clark scheme are well documented, no record exists confirming this specific characterization of messages to Ronna McDaniel or a Pence-certification-alteration proposal attributed to Perry specifically; this level of detail goes beyond what is documented and could not be verified.

inaccurate_statement: Pennsylvania watchdog groups and constituents filed additional formal ethics complaints regarding Perry's conduct
description: No record of separate, additional formal ethics complaints filed by Pennsylvania watchdog groups or constituents against Perry (beyond the January 6th Committee's own referral) could be confirmed; this appears to be an unsupported addition.

inaccurate_statement: In text messages and memos to executive officials, Perry aggressively advanced a theory that an Italian defense contractor used military satellites to secretly flip votes from Trump to Biden, and suggested 'the Brits' and the CIA were conspiring to manipulate voting machines
description: No record substantiates this specific 'Italygate'/satellite vote-flipping claim or the claim about 'the Brits' and CIA conspiring on voting machines being attributed to Perry; this could not be verified and appears to be an unsupported or fabricated addition to his documented record.

inaccurate_statement: Perry publicly invoked the racist 'Great Replacement' theory during a closed-door committee hearing and falsely asserted the Ku Klux Klan serves as the 'military wing of the Democratic Party'
description: No record substantiates these specific claims about Perry invoking 'Great Replacement' theory in a closed-door hearing or making a KKK/Democratic Party statement; these are unverified and not part of his documented controversy record.

inaccurate_statement: Perry has cast doubt on hurricane data in Puerto Rico, baselessly suggested ISIS was behind the 2017 Las Vegas mass shooting, and promoted fringe narratives surrounding the death of DNC staffer Seth Rich
description: None of these specific claims (Puerto Rico hurricane data skepticism, Las Vegas shooting/ISIS theory, Seth Rich narratives) are documented; they could not be verified and appear to be unsupported additions not found in the available record.

inaccurate_statement: Perry suggested Democratic lawmakers only enlist in the military to 'get the credential' to run for office and don't actually support America based on their voting records
description: This specific radio-show quote and controversy involving veterans could not be verified against the documented record and appears to be an unsupported addition.

inaccurate_statement: In 2002, the state of Pennsylvania criminally charged Perry with forwarding altered water reports at a sewage plant masking excessive chlorine and acidity levels, and he entered an Accelerated Rehabilitative Disposition program that allowed the record to be expunged
description: No record of this criminal charge, sewage-plant incident, or ARD diversion program exists in Perry's documented biography or controversies; his confirmed record includes a mechanical contracting business but nothing about environmental contracting or a 2002 criminal case. This is a serious, specific fabricated criminal-history claim that would significantly mislead readers about Perry's background if untrue.

inaccurate_statement: Served as chairman of the conservative House Freedom Caucus from 2021 to 2023
description: Scott Perry chaired the House Freedom Caucus from 2022 to 2024, not from 2021 to 2023. This is a minor dating error about a role he did in fact hold.

inaccurate_statement: Perry supports leaving abortion regulations to individual state legislatures and opposes a federal abortion ban
description: This omits and contradicts documented facts about Perry's abortion record: he is a current cosponsor of the federal Life at Conception Act (H.R. 722), which would establish a federal constitutional right to life from the moment of fertilization with no exceptions for rape, incest, or life of the mother — a national personhood measure, not a 'leave it to the states' position. Presenting his position as simply deferring to states and opposing any federal abortion ban, without noting this federal cosponsorship, misrepresents a genuinely conflicting record and would materially mislead a reader about where he actually stands.

inaccurate_statement: Perry opposes a federal abortion ban
description: Perry is a documented current cosponsor of the Life at Conception Act, a federal bill establishing a nationwide definition of personhood from fertilization with no exceptions — this is itself a form of federal abortion restriction, directly in tension with a claim that he 'opposes a federal abortion ban.' His record on this point is conflicting, not settled in the direction the response states.

inaccurate_statement: He opposes a nationwide, federal abortion ban.
description: This presents only one side of a genuinely conflicting record. While Perry's campaign materials state he supports leaving abortion law to the states and has spoken about exceptions for rape, incest, and life of the mother, he is a current cosponsor of the Life at Conception Act (H.R. 722), which would establish a federal, nationwide definition of personhood from the moment of fertilization with no exceptions for rape, incest, or life of the mother — legislation multiple outlets have characterized as effectively a national abortion ban. Presenting only the 'opposes a federal ban' side without this cosponsorship is a one-sided and misleading characterization of his actual position.

inaccurate_statement: He supports the Supreme Court decision to let individual states set their own abortion laws.
description: This reflects his stated campaign-site position but omits the conflicting fact that he currently cosponsors the Life at Conception Act, a federal bill that would impose a nationwide personhood definition from fertilization, which is in tension with a pure states'-rights framing on abortion.

inaccurate_statement: Perry holds a personal pro-life stance and supports leaving abortion regulations to individual state governments rather than enacting a federal ban
description: This mischaracterizes Perry's record. His stated personal position includes exceptions for rape, incest, and life of the mother, and he supports IVF, but he is a current cosponsor of the federal Life at Conception Act (H.R. 722), which would establish a nationwide, exception-free personhood standard from the moment of fertilization -- the opposite of leaving abortion regulation to the states or avoiding a federal ban. Presenting only the states'-rights framing omits his documented cosponsorship of federal personhood legislation, which multiple outlets have characterized as amounting to support for a national abortion ban with no exceptions.

inaccurate_statement: Perry was the sole member of Pennsylvania's congressional delegation—from either party—to vote against the bipartisan housing affordability bill
description: The housing bill (21st Century ROAD to Housing Act) passed the House 396-13, with Perry among the 13 Republicans (nationally) who opposed it. There is no confirmation that he was uniquely the only Pennsylvania delegation member to vote no; this specific 'sole member of the delegation' framing is not supported by available records and appears to be an embellishment of the underlying, accurate fact that Perry voted against the bill.

inaccurate_statement: Perry was the sole member of the Pennsylvania congressional delegation—from either party—to vote against a bipartisan housing affordability bill
description: The housing bill (21st Century ROAD to Housing Act) passed the House 396-13 (or 358-32 per another cited figure), with Perry among a larger group of 13-32 opposing Republicans nationally, not as the sole Pennsylvania delegation dissenter with no other context. While other sources do describe Perry as the only Pennsylvania House member to vote no, the response's framing of this specific vote count and characterization should be treated cautiously; the core claim that Perry voted against a bipartisan housing bill Stelson criticized him for is accurate, but asserting sole delegation dissent status is not clearly supported as an established fact and the vote tallies vary across sources.

inaccurate_statement: Perry has a specific flood management plan or platform statement addressing flood management systems in the district
description: No direct statement on flood management was found for Perry after repeated dedicated searches of his House.gov issues pages, campaign site, and local news coverage; this remains a confirmed gap, not a documented position. The response presents a detailed, specific flood-management strategy (leveraging WRDA authorizations, Army Corps grant programs) as his stated approach without any sourced basis for this specificity.

inaccurate_statement: Perry actively worked with the U.S. Department of Transportation and Federal Highway Administration to secure and release nearly $1.3 billion in federal funding for the I-83 South Bridge replacement
description: Perry co-signed a 2024 letter with the Pennsylvania congressional delegation urging federal discretionary funding for the I-83 South Bridge replacement, projected to cost $1.1-1.3 billion; there is no confirmation he personally secured or caused release of that exact dollar amount, and the project's funding status as of the available information was still in a pre-bid/planning phase rather than a completed secure-and-release action.

inaccurate_statement: Perry pushes to strip away green energy mandates, climate regulations, and DEI requirements embedded in federal transportation funding as part of his roads/flood strategy
description: No sourced statement ties Perry's roads or flood-management approach specifically to stripping DEI requirements or climate regulations from transportation funding; this appears to be an invented specific mechanism not found in his platform materials on infrastructure.

inaccurate_statement: Perry introduced legislation like the One Federal Decision framework (H.R. 7130), consolidating reviews under a single lead federal agency
description: No record exists of Perry introducing or sponsoring a bill called the 'One Federal Decision' framework or H.R. 7130 on this topic. The knowledge base documents his actual infrastructure/roads record (the I-83 South Bridge delegation letter, opposition to the 2021 infrastructure law) and specifically flags flood management as a confirmed gap with no direct statement found, with no mention of any One Federal Decision bill. This appears to be a fabricated legislative claim.

inaccurate_statement: Perry consistently refuses to submit Community Project Funding requests (earmarks) to bankroll specific hometown infrastructure or flood control projects, viewing them as wasteful government spending
description: No documentation of Perry's earmark policy or a stated refusal to request Community Project Funding appears anywhere in his record. This specific claim about his earmark practices is not supported and appears fabricated, though it is a narrow supporting detail rather than the central claim of the response.

inaccurate_statement: Perry advocates for tighter auditing of FEMA and argues it should focus strictly on core disaster readiness rather than 'non-traditional' missions
description: The record shows Perry has been skeptical about FEMA's mitigation spending effectiveness and cost, and has made FEMA/disaster mitigation part of his congressional work, but no source documents this specific framing about FEMA focusing on 'core disaster readiness' versus 'non-traditional missions' as a direct Perry position.

inaccurate_statement: Perry has partnered with the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers Baltimore District to study and map out MS4 stormwater infrastructure issues in areas like Harrisburg
description: No record of any such partnership or study exists. The record explicitly and repeatedly states that flood management is a confirmed gap for Perry with no direct statement found after dedicated searches of his House.gov issues pages, campaign site, and local news — this specific claim about an Army Corps Baltimore District MS4 stormwater study appears to be a fabrication that directly contradicts the documented absence of any flood-management statement or initiative from him.

inaccurate_statement: Perry firmly believes states and municipalities must take a larger fiscal role in budgeting for their own long-term flood resilience, culvert cleanups, and local drainage networks
description: This specific policy framing on flood resilience and local drainage funding is not documented anywhere in Perry's record, which explicitly notes no flood-management statement has been found for him despite repeated dedicated searches.

inaccurate_statement: As Chairman of the Subcommittee on Economic Development, Public Buildings, and Emergency Management, Perry has direct oversight over federal flood damage reduction and clean water management
description: The Economic Development, Public Buildings and Emergency Management subcommittee's jurisdiction covers disaster preparedness, mitigation, response, and recovery under the Stafford Act and FEMA/DHS emergency management matters — not flood-damage reduction or Army Corps of Engineers civil works, which fall under the separate Water Resources and Environment subcommittee. This conflates the two subcommittees' jurisdictions.

inaccurate_statement: Perry recently collaborated directly with the U.S. Department of Transportation to navigate the review process and advance the timeline for the I-83 South Bridge replacement project
description: Perry's documented I-83 South Bridge advocacy consists of a 2024 joint congressional delegation letter to then-Secretary Buttigieg urging discretionary funding; no record exists of a more recent direct collaboration specifically advancing DOT's review timeline as described here.

inaccurate_statement: Perry advocates for strict law enforcement responses to violent protests, asserting that individuals who block traffic or assault police officers should face immediate arrest and prosecution, and has noted the Insurrection Act should remain an option if local leaders refuse to protect communities.
description: No record of this specific statement or position exists in Perry's documented platform, voting record, or public statements. His House.gov and campaign site issues pages have no public-safety/crime section, and no comparable statement about the Insurrection Act was found.

inaccurate_statement: Perry signed the Heritage Action Police Pledge, formally committing to oppose any federal legislative efforts aimed at defunding the police.
description: No record of Perry signing a 'Heritage Action Police Pledge' appears in his documented record, which lists no dedicated public-safety plank at all.

inaccurate_statement: He co-sponsored the JUSTICE Act, which sought to increase police transparency, accountability, and training while ensuring departments retain full resources.
description: No record of Perry cosponsoring a bill called the JUSTICE Act was found in his documented legislative record.

inaccurate_statement: Perry introduced a bipartisan amendment to block federal highway funding from states or municipalities that use automated license plate readers for any purpose other than automated toll collection.
description: No record of this specific amendment concerning license plate readers exists in Perry's documented legislative record.

inaccurate_statement: He advanced legislation through the House Oversight Committee to ban D.C.'s speed and red-light cameras, calling them unfair financial 'money grabs.'
description: No record of this legislation or characterization appears in Perry's documented record.

inaccurate_statement: Perry authored the No Kill Switches in Cars Act to repeal federal mandates requiring anti-impaired-driving technology in new vehicles, arguing such systems violate the Fourth Amendment.
description: No record of Perry authoring a bill by this name or taking this position was found in his documented legislative record.

inaccurate_statement: Perry voted in favor of the STOP School Violence Act, which redirected $75 million in Department of Justice grant funds to state and local governments for security hardware, threat assessment teams, and crisis communication infrastructure.
description: No record of this specific vote or funding figure appears in Perry's documented voting record.

inaccurate_statement: He directly hosts educational forums in Pennsylvania pairing regional school administrators and educators with the U.S. Secret Service National Threat Assessment Center (NTAC).
description: No record of Perry hosting these specific forums was found in his documented record.

inaccurate_statement: Perry introduced the Freedom from Union Violence Act to close loopholes in the 1946 Hobbs Anti-Extortion Act, ensuring union officials can be prosecuted for violence or extortion during labor disputes.
description: No record of Perry introducing this specific bill was found in his documented legislative record.

inaccurate_statement: He consistently links public safety to national security, advocating for tighter southern border controls to curb illegal immigration and drug trafficking.
description: Perry does have a well-documented immigration/border-security platform, but this specific framing tying it explicitly to 'public safety' as a category is not directly supported; his documented public-safety plank is confirmed to not exist as a dedicated platform item.

inaccurate_statement: Perry supports H.R. 2 (the Secure America's Borders Act) as a primary legislative solution
description: H.R. 2 in the 118th Congress, which Perry voted for, was titled the Secure the Border Act of 2023, not the "Secure America's Borders Act." There is a similarly named 2025-cycle bill ("Secure America's Borders Act" or related "Permanent Trump Secure Border Act") in Perry's record, but the specific naming here conflates or garbles the bill title; his confirmed vote was for the Secure the Border Act (H.R. 2, 2023).

inaccurate_statement: Perry opposes sending U.S. taxpayer funds to other countries for foreign aid or border security abroad until the domestic border crisis is resolved
description: No record supports a blanket policy of halting all foreign aid until the border is secured; available material shows Perry's border stance centers on enforcement metrics, barriers, and staffing, not a specific foreign-aid-conditionality demand framed this way. This appears to be an unsupported extrapolation rather than a documented position.

inaccurate_statement: Stelson advocates for making child tax credits permanent
description: No record exists of Stelson making a specific pledge to make the child tax credit permanent. Her documented platform focuses on affordability generally (tariffs, gas, housing, prescription drugs), middle-class tax relief, and other specific proposals, but a specific child-tax-credit permanence pledge is not among her confirmed, sourced positions.

inaccurate_statement: Perry prioritizes traditional conservative family values
description: There is no documented statement from Perry framing his platform explicitly around 'traditional conservative family values' as a stated plank; his confirmed platform centers on deregulation, reduced spending, border security, and an all-of-the-above energy strategy. This is an unsupported characterization not tied to any specific sourced statement.

inaccurate_statement: Stelson focuses heavily on curbing gun violence through targeted legislative measures, such as mandating the reporting of lost or stolen firearms
description: No documentation of Stelson specifically proposing a mandatory lost-or-stolen-firearm reporting requirement was found. Her documented gun-safety platform (via GIFFORDS) covers expanding background checks, red flag laws, safe storage incentives, addressing ghost guns, and community violence intervention funding, but a specific 'reporting lost or stolen firearms' mandate is not among the confirmed planks and appears to be an invented specific detail layered onto an otherwise accurate general position.

inaccurate_statement: Perry promotes the Stop Insider Trading Act at the federal level
description: No record exists of Scott Perry sponsoring or promoting a 'Stop Insider Trading Act.' Perry's actual congressional stock-trading-related legislative activity documented is that he has sponsored legislation to prohibit members of Congress from trading individual stocks — a different, though related, measure. Attributing a specifically named 'Stop Insider Trading Act' to him is not supported and appears fabricated. This is a narrow supporting detail that doesn't change the response's overall characterization of Perry's crime platform.

inaccurate_statement: Stelson's position 'isn't simply more gun restrictions'; framed instead around accountability/prevention with mandatory uniforms/badges rather than her documented gun-restriction platform
description: Stelson's documented public-safety-adjacent platform centers on expanding gun-violence-prevention measures (expanded background checks, red flag laws, safe storage incentives, targeting ghost guns, domestic-abuser firearm restrictions) per her GIFFORDS endorsement profile, not a generic 'accountability plus prevention' framing that omits this. The response's description of her public-safety approach omits her actual documented gun-policy platform, giving an incomplete picture, though it doesn't invert her overall stance.

inaccurate_statement: Perry supports increasing federal mandatory minimum sentencing guidelines as a deterrent against repeat and violent offenders
description: No direct statement or documented platform item was found showing Perry has taken a specific position advocating stricter federal mandatory sentencing guidelines. His documented public-safety-adjacent record centers on opposing new gun restrictions and supporting law-enforcement-related legislation, with no dedicated current sentencing-policy plank identified.

inaccurate_statement: Perry frequently advocates for federal measures targeting drug trafficking—particularly fentanyl—and supports more rigid sentencing laws for violent crimes.
description: No record exists of a specific, current fentanyl-trafficking or violent-crime-sentencing platform plank for Perry. His documented public-safety-adjacent positions are limited to immigration enforcement, Second Amendment views, and general law-enforcement support language; no dedicated fentanyl or sentencing-law statement was found despite repeated dedicated searches for a public-safety plank.

inaccurate_statement: Perry has consistently opposed several federal police reform proposals that he argues limit qualified immunity or overly restrict law enforcement procedures.
description: No documented voting record or statement ties Perry specifically to opposing qualified-immunity reform bills. His public-safety record as documented consists of votes on immigration enforcement and general pro-law-enforcement statements; no specific qualified-immunity-related legislative opposition was found.

inaccurate_statement: Janelle Stelson publicly opposes local ICE raids that disrupt community safety and cause fear
description: Stelson's actual platform does not state opposition to ICE raids themselves. Her campaign site says she opposes open borders and supports deportation of violent criminals, while calling for accountability measures such as independent investigations of ICE incidents/killings, ICE agents wearing uniforms/badges instead of masks, and due process protections. This is a reform/accountability position, not a blanket opposition to 'local ICE raids that disrupt community safety and cause fear.' The claim overstates and mischaracterizes her stance as anti-enforcement, when analysts describe her as supporting stronger border security and tougher enforcement with due-process caveats. This is a narrower framing issue rather than a fabricated fact, so it's misleading but not a wholesale invention.

inaccurate_statement: Janelle Stelson advocates for reforming labor laws to support the district's agricultural workforce
description: Stelson has published a detailed rural/agriculture policy platform (Farm Bill renewal, right-to-repair equipment, poultry/Big Ag consolidation, tariffs, avian flu response, rural broadband, rural healthcare) and a separate labor platform (raising the minimum wage, strengthening union organizing rights, vocational training), but neither her campaign site's priorities page, her rural policy PDF, nor other sourcing found any statement specifically advocating for 'reforming labor laws to support the district's agricultural workforce' (e.g., farmworker wage/labor protections, H-2A visa reform, or farm labor organizing). Her labor positions are framed generally for all workers, and her agriculture positions focus on farm economics/equipment rather than farm labor law. The claim appears to conflate her general labor stance with her separate farm-economy platform, and this specific combined claim is not substantiated by available sources. This is a narrow, specific policy claim that doesn't undermine the broader accurate point that she supports both farmers and labor generally, so it is best characterized as a minor fabrication rather than one that would change the overall takeaway.

inaccurate_statement: Stelson supports expanding Medicaid and community health centers
description: No record exists of Stelson making a specific platform statement about expanding community health centers; her documented healthcare platform focuses on affordable care access, ending surprise billing, extending ACA subsidies, and expanding Medicare drug-price negotiation, along with opposing Medicaid cuts, but a specific 'community health centers' expansion pledge is not found in her documented positions.

inaccurate_statement: Perry voted against the Affordable Care Act
description: Scott Perry was first elected to Congress in 2012 and took office in January 2013; the Affordable Care Act was passed and signed into law in March 2010, before he was in Congress, so he could not have cast a vote on it. His documented record includes opposing and voting to repeal/undermine the ACA in various ways since taking office, but he never voted against its original passage.

inaccurate_statement: Janelle Stelson seeks a permanent child tax credit and a higher minimum wage
description: No record exists of Stelson proposing a permanent child tax credit or a higher federal minimum wage as part of her platform. Her documented affordability platform focuses on tariffs, healthcare costs, small-business support, and middle-class tax relief, without a specific child tax credit or minimum wage proposal on record.

inaccurate_statement: Scott Perry favors reducing federal spending on the Affordable Care Act to limit government debt as his 'free-market healthcare' approach
description: Perry's documented healthcare position centers on market-oriented alternatives like small-business insurance pooling and opposition to expanded federal subsidies, along with support for the 2025 reconciliation bill's Medicaid work requirements, rather than a stated goal of cutting ACA spending specifically to reduce the debt.

inaccurate_statement: Stelson supports robust alliances, international coalitions, and strategic foreign assistance to counter global threats, and is supportive of working with international allies to curb hostile actions abroad.
description: Available reporting indicates Stelson has taken more hawkish positions than this characterization suggests — she has said she supports Israel's right to 'root out Hamas and decimate the terrorist organization' and has called for continued aid to Ukraine, with some commentary describing her Ukraine stance as notably hawkish. The response's framing of her as favoring measured multilateral stability-building is a plausible but incomplete gloss that doesn't fully capture the more assertive tenor of her actual public statements on Israel and Ukraine.

inaccurate_statement: Stelson opposes the hardline tactics of the previous Trump administration on the border, citing humanitarian concerns.
description: Stelson's documented immigration statements emphasize opposing 'open borders,' focusing deportations on violent criminals, requiring ICE to be identifiable and follow due process, and increasing border technology and staffing — a specific, detailed platform. No direct statement was found explicitly framing her position as rejecting 'hardline tactics... citing humanitarian concerns' in those terms; this is a plausible but unverified gloss on her platform rather than a documented quote or position.

inaccurate_statement: Perry served nearly 40 years in the Pennsylvania Army National Guard
description: Perry's National Guard service ran from 1980 to 2019, which is approximately 39 years — this is essentially accurate and close enough to 'nearly 40 years' to not be a meaningful error; however, noting for completeness that the figure is a rounding of the documented 1980–2019 span.

inaccurate_statement: Perry leans heavily toward non-interventionism and opposes open-ended foreign aid or military engagements without distinct, immediate U.S. security outcomes.
description: The available record shows Perry supported the Trump administration's 2026 military action against Iran and voted against a House resolution that would have required removing U.S. forces from hostilities with Iran — actions inconsistent with a strongly non-interventionist characterization. While Freedom Caucus members are often skeptical of unconditional foreign aid, presenting Perry as leaning heavily non-interventionist without noting his support for the Iran strikes gives an incomplete and somewhat misleading picture of his actual foreign-policy record.

inaccurate_statement: Stelson is running with the endorsement of the Pennsylvania AFL-CIO
description: There is no record of a Pennsylvania AFL-CIO endorsement of Stelson in the available material. Her documented labor endorsements include AFGE Local 2004, United Brotherhood of Carpenters and Joiners, PA Professional Fire Fighters Association, United Mine Workers of America, IBEW Local 229, PA Building & Construction Trades Council, National Education Association, United Steelworkers District 10, and PA Conference of Teamsters, but not a specific Pennsylvania AFL-CIO endorsement. A specific research pass on Stelson's endorsements found several fabricated union-endorsement claims for unrelated unions, suggesting this may be another instance of an invented labor endorsement rather than one simply missed by that research.

inaccurate_statement: Stelson has an endorsement from the PA AFL-CIO
description: No record of a PA AFL-CIO endorsement of Stelson appears in her documented endorsement list, which includes a large slate of specific unions (AFGE Local 2004, United Brotherhood of Carpenters, PA Professional Fire Fighters, United Mine Workers, IBEW Local 229, PA Building & Construction Trades Council, NEA, United Steelworkers District 10, PA Conference of Teamsters, and others) but does not include the PA AFL-CIO by name. Given the documented pattern of fabricated or misattributed union endorsements for this candidate in other checks, this specific claim cannot be confirmed and is treated as unsupported. This is a narrow endorsement detail that does not undermine the broader accurate point that she has extensive labor support.

inaccurate_statement: Stelson is endorsed by the PA AFL-CIO and champions union protections, fair pay, and worker-centric policies
description: No record of a specific 'PA AFL-CIO' endorsement of Stelson was found; her documented labor endorsements include AFGE Local 2004, United Brotherhood of Carpenters and Joiners, PA Professional Fire Fighters Association, United Mine Workers of America, IBEW Local 229, PA Building & Construction Trades Council, National Education Association, United Steelworkers District 10, and PA Conference of Teamsters, but not a specifically named PA AFL-CIO endorsement. Her general support for union protections and fair pay is well documented and accurate, so only the specific named endorser is unverified/unsupported.

inaccurate_statement: Scott Perry argues manufacturing jobs are best protected via deregulation and tax cuts to keep factories competitive (implying this is his full stated approach)
description: While generally consistent with Perry's deregulation/tax-cut framing, his platform and record also include specific, targeted manufacturing interventions the response omits, such as his direct July 2025 letter urging Cleveland-Cliffs to reopen the Steelton steel mill and his push for tariff exemptions on cocoa imports to protect Pennsylvania chocolate manufacturers, meaning his manufacturing approach isn't purely hands-off free-market as implied.

inaccurate_statement: Stelson has prioritized infrastructure readiness, framing flash flooding from torrential storms as a critical issue threatening 25% of local infrastructure.
description: No statement from Stelson framing flash flooding as threatening '25% of local infrastructure' exists in her documented platform; her flood-management position is a confirmed research gap with no direct statement found on this topic at all, making this specific statistic and framing unsupported.

inaccurate_statement: Stelson's platform centers on using federal funding to update aging infrastructure—such as flood walls, levees, and stream restoration—to handle shifting weather patterns.
description: Stelson has made general statements supporting infrastructure investment in roads, bridges, public transit and the electric grid, but no specific statement mentioning flood walls, levees, or stream restoration has been found; flood management is a confirmed gap in her documented platform.

inaccurate_statement: Perry voted against certain federal flood insurance reform measures to minimize federal spending.
description: Available voting records point the other way on the specific flood insurance votes identifiable. Club for Growth's scorecard shows that on SB1182, which extended the National Flood Insurance Program, Perry's actual vote was 'Y' (yes/for), even though the fiscally conservative group wanted a 'no' vote, faulting the extension as 'fiscally irresponsible.' Separately, in a 2014 statement, Perry expressed support for H.R. 3370, which rolled back some Biggert-Waters NFIP reforms to protect homeowners' property values, while noting he would have preferred deeper structural/fiscal reforms but voted for the bill anyway. No identifiable instance was found of Perry voting against an NFIP/flood insurance reform bill specifically citing federal spending minimization as the reason. The claim's core framing (Perry as an opponent of flood insurance measures on fiscal grounds) is not well supported by the specific votes found; it may be a generic inference from his general fiscal-conservative reputation rather than a documented fact tied to actual flood insurance votes, so it's rated a minor inaccuracy rather than a fully fabricated one given the lack of exhaustive certainty.
