description: While Stelson has emphasized public safety and has real, documented ties to Shapiro's endorsement, no specific platform statement from Stelson tying her own position to a specific Shapiro initiative on state police cadet classes or municipal police recruitment/retention grants was found in the available record. The general framing of her as supportive of community-safety investment is consistent with her documented positions, but the specific policy details attributed to her are unverified and may overstate specificity she has not actually stated.

inaccurate_statement: Perry signed the Heritage Action Police Pledge, which explicitly vows to oppose any legislation or motion to defund law enforcement agencies.
description: No record of a 'Heritage Action Police Pledge' signed by Scott Perry exists in the available material on his record. His documented public-safety positions come from his House.gov and campaign-site content and social-media statements about supporting law enforcement broadly, with no dedicated public-safety plank found, and no mention of any such pledge by name. inaccurate_statement: Perry co-sponsored a bipartisan amendment aimed at restricting law enforcement's use of automated license plate readers (ALPRs) out of privacy concerns.
description: There is no record of Scott Perry co-sponsoring legislation restricting police use of automated license plate readers. inaccurate_statement: Janelle Stelson has criticized the pace of data center construction and supported state-level efforts to curb unchecked growth
description: Stelson's documented position on data centers is that local governments should be able to say no to projects until residents' concerns about water, grid capacity, and noise are addressed, and that data centers are 'nudging right up against' family homes and farms. There is no record of her pushing for 'state-level efforts to curb unchecked growth' specifically, or opposing rapid data center expansion outright — her documented position focuses on giving local municipalities more say, not a state-level curbing campaign.

inaccurate_statement: Janelle Stelson pushed back against federal tax incentives and legislative breaks for large tech and data center infrastructure
description: No record exists of Stelson taking a position on federal tax incentives or legislative breaks specifically for data center infrastructure. inaccurate_statement: Scott Perry defended the construction and promotion of data facilities, arguing the U.S. is in a critical global race for AI leadership against competitors like China, and stated that slowing down infrastructure development could harm technological and national security advantages
description: Perry has made a general statement along these lines nationally regarding not wanting to slow AI/data-center build-out due to competition with China, but his specific, documented position on data centers in his own district (per CNBC, April 2026) is notably more hands-off and localized: he says data-center zoning and siting decisions are 'local issues for local municipalities' and that as 'a federal guy,' he doesn't get into local zoning matters. Presenting him as actively 'defending the construction and promotion of data facilities' in the district, rather than deferring to local control, oversimplifies and somewhat mischaracterizes his actual stated position on this specific local controversy.

inaccurate_statement: Perry stated that Pennsylvania 'can't afford to slow down' on building data centers
description: Perry's documented quote was that the U.S. (nationally) 'can't afford to slow down the build-out' of data centers in the context of competition with China — the statement was about national competitiveness, not specifically about Pennsylvania. Attributing the quote to Pennsylvania specifically misstates its scope.

inaccurate_statement: Neither candidate has centered their federal campaign heavily on local data center zoning, framing both positions as purely inferred from party alignment rather than citing either candidate's own direct statements on data centers
description: Both candidates have made specific, confirmed, on-the-record statements about data centers to CNBC in April 2026: Stelson said data centers are 'nudging right up against the family home' and supports a federal role letting local governments say no to projects until resident concerns are addressed, while Perry said data-center zoning is a local-municipality matter outside his purview as 'a federal guy.' Presenting the comparison as pure inference from generic party alignment, without acknowledging these direct statements exist, omits material, directly responsive information for a voter asking specifically about this issue.

description: Both candidates have made specific, confirmed, on-the-record statements about data centers to CNBC in April 2026: Stelson said data centers are 'nudging right up against the family home' and supports a federal role letting local governments say no to projects until resident concerns are addressed, while Perry said data-center zoning is a local-municipality matter outside his purview as 'a federal guy.' Presenting the comparison as pure inference from generic party alignment, without acknowledging these direct statements exist, omits material, directly responsive information for a voter asking specifically about this issue.

inaccurate_statement: The bipartisan Senate border bill Perry opposed was endorsed by the National Border Patrol Council
description: The claim states that the National Border Patrol Council (NBPC), the union representing Border Patrol agents, endorsed the bipartisan Senate border bill (the Lankford-Murphy-Sinema deal from early 2024) that Scott Perry opposed. This is the opposite of what actually happened: the NBPC and its president, Brandon Judd, publicly criticized and opposed that bill, stating it would not solve the border crisis and declining to endorse it. Since the underlying premise of the claim is factually backwards regarding the union's actual position, this claim would materially mislead a reader into thinking law enforcement officials backed a bill that Perry opposed, when in fact the border agents' union shared Perry's opposition. This inverts the substance of the claim rather than being a minor misattribution, so it is rated critical.

inaccurate_statement: Scott Perry 'routinely votes against Democratic immigration packages, arguing they fail to stop crossings'
description: While Perry has a hardline, enforcement-focused voting record on immigration and has supported bills like the Secure the Border Act and the Permanent Trump Secure Border Act, no specific record of him repeatedly voting against 'Democratic immigration packages' with that specific rationale is documented. This is a generic characterization not directly tied to any confirmed vote, though broadly consistent with his documented hardline immigration stance.

inaccurate_statement: Stelson's platform includes specific plans to combat corporate price gouging and lower the cost of childcare
description: No record exists of Stelson's platform specifically addressing corporate price gouging or childcare costs as distinct planks; her documented affordability platform centers on tariffs, gas, housing, prescription drugs, and food costs rather than price-gouging enforcement or childcare specifically. This is a narrow, unverified addition to an otherwise accurate general characterization of her affordability platform.

inaccurate_statement: Stelson has introduced an affordable housing plan and opposes tariffs on building materials like lumber and drywall, arguing they directly elevate the price of new home construction

This specific mechanism appears to be an invented elaboration not found in her documented platform.

description: No record exists of Stelson specifically proposing to close corporate tax loopholes; her documented tax platform centers on middle-class tax relief rather than a corporate-loophole-closing proposal.

description: No record exists of Stelson releasing a specifically structured 'six-step' affordable housing plan; her documented platform supports federal investment in affordable housing generally, without this specific framing or step count.

description: Stelson's documented platform supports expanding Medicare drug-price negotiation and ending surprise billing, but no record shows her specifically proposing anti-price-gouging legislation or a plan to cap utility and grocery expenses via federal oversight in this framing.

description: Perry did vote against the bipartisan 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act (396-13), so the vote itself is accurate, but describing his housing approach as 'slashing regulatory burdens on builders' is not supported by his documented platform, which centers on general deregulation and tax reduction rather than a specific, named housing/construction deregulation plank.

At an April 2026 press conference at a Harrisburg gas station, she specifically blamed tariffs and the Iran war and pledged to work toward repealing tariffs and pursuing more stable foreign policy, rather than emphasizing corporate price gouging or a energy transition as the fix.

inaccurate_statement: Scott Perry's focus is on fiscal responsibility, reducing fraud and waste in entitlement programs, and market-based solutions
description: This is a fair general characterization but omits Perry's documented cosponsorship of H.R.191, which would repeal Medicare drug-price negotiation authority and the $2,000 out-of-pocket cap on Part D drugs, and his co-signed op-ed opposing permanent extension of enhanced ACA subsidies, both of which are more concrete and consequential than the vague 'fiscal responsibility' framing suggests.

inaccurate_statement: Supporters emphasize that Scott Perry has supported protections for pre-existing conditions in healthcare legislation

This vague, unsourced claim is not confirmed by his documented positions.

inaccurate_statement: Perry's platform calls for the House-passed 'Secure the Border Act' as a model
description: Perry's confirmed immigration platform references border security metrics, technology, agricultural worker visas, and reformed legal immigration processes on his official issues pages; while he has supported various border-security bills including the Secure the Border Act (H.R. 2) in 2023, presenting this specific bill as the central named model of his platform is not directly documented as his own campaign framing in available material, though it is broadly consistent with his hardline enforcement record.

inaccurate_statement: Scott Perry opposed caps on Medicare out-of-pocket costs
description: Perry actually backed 2019-era bipartisan-branded legislation (H.R. 19, the Lower Costs, More Cures Act) that would have capped Medicare Part D out-of-pocket costs and capped insulin costs at $50/month for seniors, along with drug-pricing transparency measures. This contradicts a blanket claim that he opposed such caps; his actual record shows support for a specific out-of-pocket cap proposal, even though he opposed the Democratic-backed alternative (H.R. 3) that included Medicare drug-price negotiation.

inaccurate_statement: Scott Perry voted against proposals to cap out-of-pocket costs for Medicare.
description: The available record shows the opposite: in 2020 Perry backed legislation (H.R. 19, the Lower Costs, More Cures Act) that included capping seniors' out-of-pocket insulin costs at $50/month and creating a first-ever Part D out-of-pocket cap, rather than voting against such caps. No record supports him voting against Medicare out-of-pocket cost caps.

inaccurate_statement: Scott Perry has previously voted for bills that reduce Medicaid enrollment scaling and cut funding, and voted against capping Medicare out-of-pocket expenses
description: The characterization of Perry voting for Medicaid cuts is generally supported (he voted for the 2025 reconciliation bill with Medicaid work requirements, which Pennsylvania officials estimated would cause thousands in PA-10 to lose coverage). However, the specific claim that he voted 'against capping Medicare out-of-pocket expenses' is not well supported — the available record shows Perry actually backed legislation (H.R. 19, the Lower Costs, More Cures Act) that included capping insulin costs and creating a Medicare Part D out-of-pocket cap, which runs counter to a blanket claim that he opposed capping Medicare out-of-pocket costs. This is a narrow point that doesn't change the broader picture of his healthcare record.

description: No source documents Stelson proposing a specific plan to prioritize congested commuter corridors or commuter-safety upgrades; her documented infrastructure statements are more general (investment in roads, bridges, transit, and the electric grid) and, more specifically, focused on the I-83 South Bridge project rather than commuter-corridor congestion relief.

inaccurate_statement: Perry advocates for identifying unspent federal funds and shifting them into core road and highway repairs, rather than raising taxes or issuing high-interest federal bonds, as his stated highway funding mechanism

His documented positions are opposition to large spending packages (like the 2021 infrastructure law) and support for deregulation/faster permitting, plus specific advocacy for the I-83 South Bridge project, but this particular funding-reallocation mechanism is not found in his platform materials.

This claim overstates the specificity and currency of a position that isn't documented as a clear, current direct statement.

inaccurate_statement: Stelson's platform includes capping corporate price-gouging
description: No record in Stelson's documented platform describes a specific policy of capping corporate price-gouging. inaccurate_statement: Stelson's platform includes increasing funding for affordable child care

description: Stelson's documented wage-related position is criticizing Pennsylvania's $7.25 minimum wage as "outrageous," but no broader platform plank calling for raising wages generally to match cost-of-living increases is documented.

inaccurate_statement: Stelson blames corporate profit margins and federal tax breaks for the wealthy, in addition to tariffs, for inflation
description: Search results strongly confirm two of the three components of this claim: Stelson repeatedly and explicitly blames tariffs for inflation/rising costs (e.g., she 'blamed Republicans in Washington, D.C., for the rising cost of gas, groceries and other everyday goods' and cited tariffs as a driver), and she criticizes federal tax breaks for the wealthy/corporations, arguing 'the cuts benefit corporations and wealthy earners instead of workers while increasing the national deficit.' Additionally, no source found has Stelson specifically invoking 'corporate profit margins' (e.g., corporate greed or price-gouging) as an inflation driver — this specific element of the claim could not be verified. Since two of three cited causes (tariffs, tax breaks for the wealthy) are well-supported as things she blames for economic strain/inflation, but the 'corporate profit margins' component lacks direct attribution in available sources, the claim is only partially accurate. This is a narrow factual gap rather than a wholesale fabrication, so severity is minor.

inaccurate_statement: Rep. Perry sits on the Aviation Subcommittee.

This appears to be a factual error regarding his committee assignments, though it is a narrow, checkable detail rather than a claim that would fundamentally alter the overall picture of his legislative role (which centers on Freedom Caucus leadership, Foreign Affairs, and Homeland Security work).

description: No record exists of Stelson proposing funding for regional drug-interdiction task forces; her documented immigration position focuses on border security technology, ICE accountability/uniform requirements, and a secure-but-humane enforcement approach, not this specific narcotics-task-force framing.

inaccurate_statement: Scott Perry's plan for public safety emphasizes robust funding for police departments and addressing crime through strong prosecution, as a defined platform plank
description: No dedicated, current public-safety or crime plank exists on Perry's House.gov issues page or his campaign site as of the most recent research pass; the closest documented material is a decades-old 2017 crime-victims-fund bill and an unverified social-media quote about supporting law enforcement. inaccurate_statement: As the daughter of a former State Trooper, Stelson heavily features her personal ties to the law enforcement community
description: No record exists of Stelson being the daughter of a former State Trooper or of her citing this specific family connection to law enforcement; her documented biography centers on a broadcast journalism career, and her public-safety-related credibility claims reference her journalism coverage of law enforcement and ride-alongs, not a family member's law-enforcement background.

description: No dedicated public safety plank or specific voting record on body cameras, qualified immunity, no-knock warrants, or racial profiling legislation was found for Perry. inaccurate_statement: Stelson has earned an endorsement from the Central Pennsylvania Building & Construction Trades Council specifically for her infrastructure investment emphasis
description: Stelson's documented endorsement list includes the PA Building & Construction Trades Council (statewide), but no record in the available material specifically names a 'Central Pennsylvania Building & Construction Trades Council' as a distinct endorsing entity tied specifically to her infrastructure platform.
