inaccurate_statement: Perry voted against a subsequent major surface transportation reauthorization package in committee
description: The documented record shows Perry opposed a 2026 House surface-transportation bill authorizing about $580 billion for highway and rail programs, and separately introduced the 'Highways First Act' to prevent highway funds being redirected to transit — but no record confirms this specific characterization of a committee-level vote against a 'surface transportation reauthorization package,' making this an imprecise characterization of his actual actions.

inaccurate_statement: Stelson strongly supports the continued implementation of the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law, emphasizing that these investments are vital for the state's 3,000+ structurally deficient bridges and thousands of miles of poor-condition highways
description: No documented statement from Stelson cites a specific figure of '3,000+ structurally deficient bridges' or a specific mileage figure for poor-condition highways. Her confirmed platform statements on infrastructure are more general, calling for investment in roads, bridges, public transportation and the electric grid as job creators, without these specific statistics attributed to her.

inaccurate_statement: Perry maintains that infrastructure is a core function of the federal government, and has previously called for bipartisan packages dedicated solely to traditional physical improvements, isolating it from larger social spending packages
description: No record exists of Perry proposing or calling for a standalone bipartisan infrastructure-only package separate from broader spending bills. His documented record shows he voted against the 2021 Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act while separately supporting the specific I-83 South Bridge project and co-signing a funding request letter for it, but no source describes him advocating for a distinct 'infrastructure-only' bill as an alternative strategy.

inaccurate_statement: Perry points to his regular opposition to federal mass-transit provisions that shift money away from direct surface transportation or burden taxpayers with funding out-of-state projects without adequate accountability
description: While Perry has opposed some transit-related measures (e.g., a 2026 amendment to remove WMATA funding, opposition to streetcar funding, the Highways First Act), no source documents him framing this specifically around 'out-of-state projects without adequate accountability' — this specific framing appears to be an invented elaboration not tied to any confirmed statement.

inaccurate_statement: Perry voted against the $1.2 trillion Bipartisan Infrastructure Law, arguing that too little of the package went to traditional roads and bridges and that massive federal spending spikes national debt
description: Perry did vote against the 2021 Bipartisan Infrastructure Law, and he has generally argued against large federal spending packages on debt grounds, but no record shows him giving this specific rationale (that too little of the package went to traditional roads and bridges) for his infrastructure-law vote. This specific justification is not documented and appears to be an invented elaboration on his real vote.

inaccurate_statement: Perry calls for completely banning sanctuary cities.
description: There is no record of Perry proposing or calling for a comprehensive ban on sanctuary cities specifically. His documented immigration platform emphasizes securing the border, enforcement metrics, and legal-immigration reform (agricultural worker visas, English-proficiency requirements, STEM visa changes), but no sanctuary-city ban plank or statement is on record. This is a narrow platform detail rather than a claim that changes the overall characterization of him as immigration-enforcement-focused.

inaccurate_statement: Perry has co-sponsored and introduced legislation aimed at cracking down on criminal offenses by individuals in the country illegally, including measures targeting domestic violence and sex offense convictions for mandatory deportation
description: No record exists of Perry cosponsoring or introducing legislation specifically targeting domestic violence or sex offense convictions for mandatory deportation of undocumented immigrants. His documented immigration record includes border-security bills like the Secure the Border Act, the Permanent Trump Secure Border Act, and legislation requiring deportation of undocumented people convicted of violent offenses generally, but no source ties him to a specific domestic-violence/sex-offense mandatory deportation bill. This is a narrow, specific legislative detail that doesn't change the broader accurate characterization of his hardline enforcement stance.

inaccurate_statement: Stelson's campaign attacked Perry directly, accusing him of previously voting to grant data center companies massive tax breaks
description: No record exists of Stelson's campaign making this specific attack about Perry voting to grant data center companies tax breaks. Perry's documented public position on data centers is that zoning and regulation of such projects are local municipal matters outside his purview as a federal legislator ("As a federal guy, you know, I don't get into local zoning and building"), not a description of a specific tax-break vote. This appears to be an invented specific claim not grounded in the documented record.

inaccurate_statement: Perry has called Governor Shapiro a "craven flip-flopper" for shifting from handing out corporate tax breaks to suddenly enacting restrictions
description: No record exists of Perry making this specific quote or criticism of Shapiro. Perry's documented position on data centers is that regulation of such projects is a local, not federal, matter, and he has separately said nationally that the U.S. can't afford to slow down the data-center buildout due to competition with China. No sourced statement calling Shapiro a "craven flip-flopper" was found.

inaccurate_statement: Perry's past support for fast-tracking AI infrastructure to compete globally has allowed opponents to frame him as a proponent of rapid data center expansion
description: While Perry has made a general statement that the U.S. can't afford to slow down data-center build-out due to competition with China, there is no documented record of him supporting specific legislation or action to "fast-track" AI infrastructure, nor of this specific framing being used by opponents. This appears to be an extrapolation beyond the documented record.

inaccurate_statement: Stelson stated that the state 'can't afford to slow down' on regulating these high-consumption facilities
description: This quote — 'can't afford to slow down' — is attributed in the knowledge base to Scott Perry in the context of AI/data-center competitiveness with China, not to Stelson regarding regulation. No record exists of Stelson using this specific phrase about regulatory urgency; her documented data-center statements focus on local impacts on neighborhoods and giving local governments power to say no, not this particular framing.

inaccurate_statement: Stelson's campaign has criticized Perry for voting to give data center companies massive tax breaks
description: No record exists of Stelson criticizing Perry specifically for voting to give data center companies tax breaks, nor of Perry casting such a vote. Her documented data-center criticism of Perry centers on his stated view that zoning/regulation of data centers is a local matter outside federal purview, not on a tax-break vote.

inaccurate_statement: Perry voted for tax incentives for data center companies
description: No documented vote or record shows Perry voting for data center tax incentives. His confirmed position, per CNBC reporting, is that data center zoning and regulation are local/municipal matters outside his purview as a federal representative, with no mention of a tax-incentive vote.

inaccurate_statement: Perry argues that pausing development risks falling behind foreign adversaries like China
description: While Perry has made general statements about not wanting to slow down data center/AI buildout due to China competition, the knowledge base documents his primary stated position as viewing data center siting/zoning as a local, not federal, matter — his own quote emphasizes deference to local municipalities rather than a national urgency argument against pausing development.

inaccurate_statement: The $45,000 podcast payment to Stelson came from a 'dark money' progressive group
description: The $45,000 came from a nonprofit called Voting for America, founded by DNC/DCCC alumni and a political lawyer; while it is fairly characterized as 'dark money' due to lack of donor disclosure, describing it simply as a 'progressive group' paying for a podcast omits that this was personal income paid to Stelson individually (disclosed on her federal financial disclosure), not a campaign contribution — the response's brief description is not sharply wrong but blurs this distinction that the sourcing treats as important.

inaccurate_statement: Perry publicly dismissed the legitimacy of the House January 6th Committee's subpoena
description: The knowledge base documents that Perry declined the committee's request and a subsequent subpoena, leading to a referral to the House Ethics Committee, but does not document him publicly dismissing the committee's legitimacy as the specific stated reason for defiance; this specific framing/detail is not corroborated in the available material.

inaccurate_statement: Perry was the only member of Pennsylvania's congressional delegation to vote against awarding Congressional Gold Medals to the police officers who protected the Capitol during the insurrection
description: No record of this specific vote or claim exists in the available material on Perry. This is a specific, checkable claim not corroborated by the source documentation on his record.

inaccurate_statement: In early 2024, a lawsuit was filed seeking to disqualify Perry from the primary ballot under Section 3 of the 14th Amendment due to his involvement in fake elector schemes, later withdrawn following a U.S. Supreme Court ruling
description: No such 14th Amendment disqualification lawsuit against Perry is documented in the available material, which covers his January 6-related controversies (phone seizure, Jeffrey Clark scheme, Ethics Committee referral) in detail but contains no mention of any ballot-disqualification suit or 'fake elector' scheme involvement specific to him.

inaccurate_statement: Perry drew heavy criticism from community groups for using Nazi analogies during a speech at the Pennsylvania Leadership Conference
description: No record of this specific incident (Nazi analogies at the Pennsylvania Leadership Conference) appears in the available material on Perry's controversies, which otherwise catalogs his January 6-related record in detail.

inaccurate_statement: Perry's campaign faced backlash for posting and subsequently deleting an antisemitic meme on its Facebook page
description: No record of this specific incident appears in the available material documenting Perry's controversies.

inaccurate_statement: Stelson's campaign actively promotes outreach to independent and center-right voters under the slogan "Republicans for Janelle"
description: "Republicans for Janelle" is a real group — a coalition of five former Republican House members (Barbara Comstock, Adam Kinzinger, Denver Riggleman, Dave Trott, and Joe Walsh) who signed a joint letter backing Stelson during the 2024 cycle — but it is not her own campaign's slogan or outreach program; it is an independent third-party endorsement effort by former officials, not something her campaign runs or promotes as a slogan for reaching center-right voters generally.

inaccurate_statement: Available campaign-finance trackers classify Janelle Stelson as having $0 in corporate PAC contributions (contradicted by response's claim she receives corporate PAC money)
description: The knowledge base notes Stelson is explicitly listed by End Citizens United as a 'No Corporate PAC' candidate, and that her PAC/other-committee contributions (~8% of receipts) are a small share dominated by individual giving; there is no confirmed record she takes corporate PAC money or that Exelon/Norfolk Southern PACs specifically donated to her campaign. This is a specific, checkable financial claim not supported by (and in tension with) the documented record.

inaccurate_statement: Janelle Stelson faced criticism from her primary opponent, Justin Douglas, for accepting D.C. insider support and corporate PAC contributions.
description: The documented criticism from Justin Douglas of Stelson during the primary concerned her declining to debate him, not her accepting corporate PAC contributions or D.C. insider support. No record supports this specific characterization of his criticism.

inaccurate_statement: Studies and state officials say his votes could cause over 300,000 people in Pennsylvania to lose Medicaid
description: The documented Pennsylvania DHS/Shapiro administration estimate tied to Perry's district and this legislation is 18,720 PA-10 residents projected to lose Medicaid coverage (with a broader central-PA regional figure around 42,000 across multiple counties/districts cited in some reporting). A statewide figure of 'over 300,000' is not supported by the sourced figures in the available material, though the broader claim that his votes could cause significant Medicaid coverage loss is directionally accurate.

inaccurate_statement: The response presents Justin Douglas as a current major candidate running to represent PA-10 alongside Janelle Stelson, describing the race as being between Stelson and Douglas.
description: Justin Douglas was Stelson's opponent in the May 19, 2026 Democratic primary, which Stelson won decisively (67.4%–32.6%). He is not on the November 2026 general-election ballot. The actual PA-10 general-election matchup is between Janelle Stelson (Democrat) and Scott Perry (Republican, incumbent), with Isabelle Harman (Independent) also on the ballot. The response fails to mention Scott Perry at all and instead frames a defeated primary candidate as a current rival, which fundamentally misrepresents who is actually running in this race.

inaccurate_statement: The response presents Justin Douglas as a current major candidate running to represent PA-10 alongside Janelle Stelson, describing the race as being between Stelson and Douglas.
description: Justin Douglas was Stelson's opponent in the May 19, 2026 Democratic primary, which Stelson won decisively (67.4%–32.6%). He is not on the November 2026 general-election ballot. The actual PA-10 general-election matchup is between Janelle Stelson (Democrat) and Scott Perry (Republican, incumbent), with Isabelle Harman (Independent) also on the ballot. The response fails to mention Scott Perry at all and instead frames a defeated primary candidate as a current rival, which fundamentally misrepresents who is actually running in this race.

inaccurate_statement: Perry has pushed back against federal spending bills that restrict enforcement resources for agencies like ICE and Customs and Border Protection (CBP).
description: No record exists in the available material of Perry taking a specific position pushing back against spending bills that restrict ICE/CBP enforcement resources. This is a specific, unverified claim not supported by his documented immigration platform, which focuses on border wall construction, ending catch-and-release, and enforcement metrics rather than a spending-bill funding fight.

inaccurate_statement: Stelson attributes high mortgage rates and inflation partly to federal deficit spending
description: Stelson's documented affordability messaging blames tariffs and Republican-driven policies (including Perry's votes) for inflation and cost-of-living pressures, not federal deficit spending as a cause of high mortgage rates. No record exists of her attributing inflation to deficit spending; this appears to be a mischaracterization of her actual framing, which centers on tariffs and corporate/utility cost increases.

inaccurate_statement: Perry's votes opposing certain bipartisan housing and infrastructure frameworks cited concerns over provisions like central bank digital currency restrictions
description: No record exists of Perry citing central bank digital currency concerns as a reason for opposing housing or infrastructure legislation. His documented opposition to the 2021 infrastructure law and the 2026 housing bill (21st Century ROAD to Housing Act, which he was one of only 13 House members to oppose) is tied to general spending/regulatory concerns, not CBDC provisions. This specific rationale appears fabricated.

inaccurate_statement: Janelle Stelson blames high costs on international tariff disputes affecting energy/gas prices
description: Stelson's April 2026 gas-price press conference blamed Trump tariffs and the Iran war for high gas prices; this is broadly consistent with the response's framing, though her platform's tariff-blame is more centrally about general cost-of-living items (food, housing, prescription drugs) rather than a distinct claim that tariffs specifically drive gas/energy prices. This is a narrow framing point that does not fundamentally distort her position, which does genuinely include tariffs as a blamed factor for gas prices.

inaccurate_statement: Stelson supports repealing tariffs on lumber and drywall
description: No record exists of Stelson taking a specific position on repealing tariffs on lumber and drywall. Her documented platform opposes broad tariffs generally and blames tariffs for raising costs, but no specific statement about lumber and drywall tariffs was found, and this specific, narrow policy detail does not appear in her documented platform materials.

inaccurate_statement: Stelson criticizes Perry for voting against key housing and prescription drug measures
description: Stelson's actual criticism regarding housing concerns Perry's vote against a bipartisan housing-affordability bill (the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act), which is accurate, but the characterization of a specific 'prescription drug measures' vote is unclear from the available record beyond his cosponsorship of legislation to repeal Inflation Reduction Act drug-pricing provisions; this framing is vague enough to be only loosely supported rather than a clean factual match, though it doesn't fundamentally distort the overall comparison.

inaccurate_statement: Stelson supports utilizing war powers resolutions to limit executive military action
description: While Stelson has opposed U.S. involvement in the 2026 Iran war and argued domestic priorities should come first, no record confirms she specifically called for using war powers resolutions to limit executive military action; this is a more specific mechanism than what is documented as her stated position.

inaccurate_statement: Perry voted against allowing Medicare to negotiate certain prescription drug prices
description: There is no record of a specific vote by Perry against Medicare drug-price negotiation authority itself; what is documented is his cosponsorship of H.R. 191, a bill that would repeal the 2022 Inflation Reduction Act (which created that negotiation authority), plus reporting that he previously voted against the Lower Drug Costs Now Act. Framing this as a direct vote 'against allowing Medicare to negotiate' conflates cosponsorship of a repeal bill with an actual floor vote, though the underlying policy opposition is accurately characterized.

inaccurate_statement: Perry maintains that individual states should decide abortion access
description: Perry's documented position is a personal stance supporting exceptions for rape, incest, and life of the mother, combined with cosponsorship of the Life at Conception Act (a federal personhood measure with no such exceptions) — a genuinely conflicting record, not a 'leave it to the states' position. No record shows him framing abortion as a states'-rights issue; his cosponsored federal bill would impose a national personhood standard, the opposite of leaving it to states.

inaccurate_statement: According to campaign finance data tracked by Capitol Trail, individual donors make up roughly 86% of Perry's direct campaign contributions
description: The claim attributes campaign finance statistics to "Capitol Trail," which is not a recognized or identifiable campaign finance tracking organization or database (unlike legitimate sources such as OpenSecrets, the FEC, or Ballotpedia). No evidence exists that such a source exists or that it tracks Scott Perry's donor composition. The specific 86% individual donor figure attributed to this named source cannot be corroborated, and the citation of a seemingly non-existent tracking entity strongly suggests this is a fabricated claim rather than a real, verifiable statistic. Genuine campaign finance data for Perry is publicly available through the FEC and OpenSecrets, and any accurate claim should cite those established sources rather than an apparently invented one.

inaccurate_statement: Federal judges ruled that Perry's communications with Trump staffers and campaign lawyers did not constitute official legislative duties and rejected most of his privilege claims, ordering disclosure, with the investigation described as part of Special Counsel Jack Smith's probe
description: The available record describes the phone seizure and Speech-or-Debate litigation as part of the broader January 6 investigation (later reported to be part of the 'Arctic Frost' probe), with a D.C. Circuit ruling permitting access to 1,659 of the contested messages by December 2023 — it does not specifically confirm this was Special Counsel Jack Smith's investigation as the response asserts. This detail about the specific investigating authority is not corroborated and may overstate certainty about which federal probe was involved.

inaccurate_statement: Perry has been classified as a witness (not a subject or target) in the investigation
description: No source in the available record confirms Perry was formally 'classified as a witness' in the investigation. The documented record states only that no criminal charges have ever been filed against him, described as an absence of charges rather than an affirmative formal classification such as 'witness' status.

inaccurate_statement: Perry completed an Accelerated Rehabilitative Disposition (ARD) program following allegations related to altered sewage treatment plant reports at a mechanical business he ran, during his time in the Pennsylvania House of Representatives
description: The core fact — that Scott Perry completed an ARD (Accelerated Rehabilitative Disposition) program related to allegations of falsified sewage/wastewater treatment reports connected to a mechanical business he was involved with — appears to be substantively real and has been reported. However, this incident dates to the early-to-mid 1990s, which predates his time in the Pennsylvania House of Representatives (he was not elected to the PA House until 2007). The claim's assertion that this occurred 'during his time in the Pennsylvania House of Representatives' misstates the timing/context of the event. The underlying ARD/allegation fact is likely true, but the temporal attribution to his PA House tenure is incorrect, making this a minor factual error rather than a fabrication of the core claim. Note: I was unable to complete live web verification this turn due to tool call limits, so this assessment relies on prior knowledge and should ideally be corroborated with a fresh search focused on the exact year of the ARD program and Perry's PA House service dates (2007-2012).

inaccurate_statement: Served as chairman of the House Freedom Caucus from 2021 to 2023.
description: Scott Perry served as chair of the House Freedom Caucus from 2022 to 2024, not 2021 to 2023. This is a narrow dating error about his caucus leadership tenure that does not change the overall picture of his qualifications.

inaccurate_statement: He pushes for rules that ban members of Congress from trading stocks.
description: While Perry has sponsored legislation to prohibit members of Congress from trading individual stocks (confirmed in the knowledge base), this claim appears in a section framed around Perry's own priority messaging; this is accurate as a factual matter about Perry's legislative record, not an error — retaining as accurate rather than inaccurate.

inaccurate_statement: Perry opposes a federal abortion ban and believes individual states should decide the issue
description: This mischaracterizes Perry's actual record. Perry is a longtime cosponsor of the federal Life at Conception Act (H.R. 722, 119th Congress), a national constitutional personhood measure with no rape/incest/life exceptions — the opposite of a 'let states decide' federalism position. His documented position is genuinely conflicting: his campaign materials describe a personal pro-life stance with rape/incest/life-of-mother exceptions, while his legislative cosponsorship record supports a federal fetal-personhood law that multiple outlets say would effectively function as a national abortion ban and put IVF at risk. Presenting his position as simple opposition to any federal ban and support for state-level decision-making, without any mention of this cosponsorship, is a substantive misrepresentation of his real, documented record.

inaccurate_statement: Perry supports leaving abortion regulations to individual states rather than a federal ban
description: This presents only one side of a genuinely conflicting record. While Perry's campaign materials state a personal position with rape/incest/life exceptions and support for IVF, he is also a current cosponsor of the federal Life at Conception Act (H.R. 722), which would establish a nationwide fetal-personhood standard from the moment of fertilization with no exceptions — a federal measure, not a states'-rights approach. Presenting his position as simply deferring to states omits this documented, conflicting federal cosponsorship and IVF-risk implications, which materially changes the picture of his actual abortion stance.

inaccurate_statement: Perry's flood management approach centers on NFIP reform, calling it a 'federal boondoggle' financing repairs for second/third homes, FEMA accountability/local budgeting criticizing 'non-traditional disasters' like pandemic management, and advancing WRDA to streamline the Army Corps of Engineers
description: No record exists of Perry making any statement on flood management specifically — this was confirmed as a genuine, repeatedly re-checked gap. There is no documented position from Perry on NFIP reform, no quote calling it a 'federal boondoggle,' no statement on FEMA covering 'non-traditional disasters' like pandemics, and no documented advocacy for WRDA tied to flood prevention. This entire section presents specific, detailed policy mechanisms and quotes as Perry's stated positions with no supporting basis, which would seriously mislead a reader into believing Perry has a developed, on-record flood-management platform when no such record was found despite dedicated research.

inaccurate_statement: Perry voted against the INVEST Act, criticizing it as fiscally irresponsible and heavily laden with federal debt
description: No record was found of Perry voting on or specifically criticizing 'the INVEST Act' by name, nor of a quote characterizing it as fiscally irresponsible; his documented opposition is to the 2021 Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act, not a separately named 'INVEST Act' vote with this specific characterization.

inaccurate_statement: Perry has questioned whether the federal government should recoup disaster relief funds when taxpayer-funded infrastructure projects later levy user tolls
description: No documented statement from Perry raises this specific toll/disaster-relief-recoupment argument; it does not appear in his platform materials, voting record, or any sourced quote.

inaccurate_statement: Perry pushes back against federal overreach in building codes and infrastructure requirements that burden local business owners and drive up project costs
description: No specific statement from Perry on building codes and infrastructure requirements as a burden on local business owners was found; this appears to be an invented specific policy claim not grounded in any documented source.

inaccurate_statement: As Chairman of the House Subcommittee on Economic Development, Public Buildings, and Emergency Management, Perry has direct oversight over federal highway infrastructure and flood damage reduction programs.
description: Flood-damage reduction and Army Corps of Engineers civil works activities fall under the jurisdiction of the House Transportation & Infrastructure Committee's Water Resources and Environment subcommittee, not the Economic Development, Public Buildings & Emergency Management subcommittee that Perry chairs. This subcommittee's actual jurisdiction covers disaster preparedness/mitigation/response under the Stafford Act and FEMA/DHS emergency management matters, not flood-damage reduction specifically.

inaccurate_statement: Perry collaborated with state and local leaders to successfully secure a $500 million federal grant to replace the deteriorating John Harris Interstate 83 South Bridge
description: Available records show Perry co-signed an April 2024 letter with the Pennsylvania congressional delegation urging federal discretionary funding for the I-83 South Bridge replacement, a project projected to cost $1.1-1.3 billion, but there is no confirmation of a secured $500 million federal grant for this project.

inaccurate_statement: Perry supports shifting focus toward pre-disaster flood resilience, advocating for legislation encouraging communities to look upstream to slow water flows before damage reaches critical local roads and culverts
description: No direct statement on flood management exists in Perry's documented record. Dedicated research specifically found no statement from Perry on flood management despite searching his House.gov issues pages, campaign site, and local news coverage. Presenting a specific, detailed flood-mitigation policy mechanism as his stated position, without any hedging language, invents a position not found in any available source.

inaccurate_statement: Perry has expressed concerns that FEMA resources are overly diluted by 'non-traditional disasters' and pushes for stricter fiscal accountability urging states and municipalities to budget for localized flood/storm management rather than relying on federal bailouts
description: No record of this specific FEMA framing or quote exists in Perry's documented statements. While he has been involved in FEMA oversight generally, this specific characterization and language was not found and appears to be an invented specific policy framing.

inaccurate_statement: Perry actively collaborated with local and federal officials to secure a $500 million federal grant to replace the I-83 South Bridge
description: The documented record shows Perry co-signed a 2024 letter urging federal discretionary funding for the I-83 South Bridge replacement project, which is estimated to cost $1.1-1.3 billion total; no source confirms a specific $500 million grant was secured, and this specific dollar figure does not match any documented figure.

inaccurate_statement: Perry championed the 'One Federal Decision' framework, arguing for a single lead agency to compile a single environmental impact statement to speed up infrastructure approval
description: No record of Perry specifically championing the 'One Federal Decision' framework by name was found in his documented platform statements or legislative record; this specific policy mechanism attribution is unconfirmed.

inaccurate_statement: Perry heavily opposed initial proposals to place a toll on the I-83 bridge, arguing Pennsylvania taxpayers should not pay tolls on infrastructure they already funded via taxes
description: The documented record notes that PennDOT's tolling plan for the I-83 South Bridge project was struck down in court, but no direct statement or quote from Perry specifically opposing the toll on these grounds was found in his documented record.

inaccurate_statement: Perry fights against automated speed and red-light cameras and introduced legislation to stop federal funds for these systems, calling them 'budget traps'
description: No record exists of Scott Perry introducing or supporting legislation banning automated traffic/red-light cameras, or of him characterizing them as 'budget traps.' His documented public safety and transportation positions focus on border security, law enforcement funding, highway funding, and opposition to certain transit spending — there is no mention anywhere of a traffic-camera policy position. This appears to be an invented specific detail central to the response's answer about how he would improve public safety.

inaccurate_statement: Perry hosts training events with the U.S. Secret Service that teach educators how to spot troubled students and stop violence before it starts
description: There is no record of Scott Perry hosting or participating in Secret Service-run school-safety training forums for educators. His documented record shows no dedicated public-safety/crime platform plank at all, and this specific claim about school-safety training events does not appear in any available source about him.

inaccurate_statement: Perry opposes any efforts to defund the police
description: While Perry's general pro-law-enforcement orientation is consistent with his record, no specific statement opposing 'defund the police' efforts is documented; this is a plausible but unconfirmed characterization not directly tied to a specific quote or vote in the available record.

inaccurate_statement: Perry has introduced legislation to stop the Department of Transportation from using taxpayer money to promote or install automated traffic cameras.
description: Perry has genuinely introduced legislation targeting automated traffic cameras, but the substance is mischaracterized. His bills strip Washington D.C.'s own authority to operate its 546-547 automated traffic enforcement cameras (and separately roll back D.C.'s right-turn-on-red restrictions), framed as stopping D.C. from using camera fines to 'balance its budget' rather than for safety. This is distinct from the claim's framing that his legislation stops the federal 'Department of Transportation from using taxpayer money to promote or install' cameras — that specific mechanism (restricting DOT's own spending on promotion/installation) is not supported by search results. Notably, a separate, DOT-initiated proposal (under the Trump administration) to eliminate D.C.'s cameras exists in parallel, but that is a DOT action, not a restriction Perry's bill placed on DOT. The core fact that Perry is a leading opponent of automated traffic cameras and has introduced relevant legislation is accurate, but the specific description of what the legislation does is factually off, which is a minor error given the overall correct thrust of the claim (Perry opposing traffic cameras via legislation).

inaccurate_statement: Scott Perry retired from the U.S. Army National Guard after 40 years of service
description: Perry served in the Pennsylvania Army National Guard from 1980 to 2019, which is approximately 39 years, not 40 — a negligible discrepancy, though the response's rounded figure is close to accurate. More notably, the knowledge base does not specify an exact total years figure as a confirmed direct statement, but the 1980–2019 span is documented, making "40 years" a minor rounding overstatement.

inaccurate_statement: Perry retired after 40 years of service in the Army National Guard
description: Perry served in the Pennsylvania Army National Guard from 1980 to 2019, which is approximately 39 years, not 40.

inaccurate_statement: Abortion: Stelson strongly supports abortion rights / Perry strongly anti-abortion
description: Presenting Perry as simply 'strongly anti-abortion' omits that his stated personal position includes exceptions for rape, incest, and life of the mother, and that he supports IVF access and co-introduced the IVF Protection Act, even though he also currently cosponsors the Life at Conception Act, which contains no such exceptions and defines personhood from the moment of fertilization. His record on this issue is genuinely conflicting rather than a simple, one-sided 'strongly anti-abortion, no exceptions' position, and presenting only one side risks misleading readers about his actual documented stance.

inaccurate_statement: Perry supported Texas's lawsuit seeking to invalidate Biden's certified victories in Pennsylvania and other states
description: No record in the available material documents Perry personally supporting or joining the Texas v. Pennsylvania lawsuit (filed by Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton seeking to invalidate results in Pennsylvania, Georgia, Michigan, and Wisconsin). Perry's documented 2020-election-related actions center on the Jeffrey Clark scheme, phone seizure, and his January 6 certification vote, not this specific lawsuit. This appears to be an unsupported addition not found in the documented record.

inaccurate_statement: A 2024 Pennsylvania court filing stated that Perry was engaged with election deniers working to provide alternative elector slates and specifically described his involvement in efforts to present an alternative Pennsylvania slate
description: No record in the available material corroborates a 2024 Pennsylvania court filing describing Perry's involvement in a fake-elector scheme or an alternative Pennsylvania elector slate. The documented record instead centers on the Jeffrey Clark installation effort, the FBI phone seizure, and the January 6 vote; no fake-electors connection to Perry is documented in the available research.

inaccurate_statement: Perry supported a lawsuit brought by Texas seeking to invalidate Pennsylvania's and three other states' certified electoral votes
description: No record exists of Perry personally supporting or being involved in the Texas v. Pennsylvania lawsuit (Texas Attorney General's suit seeking to invalidate results in Pennsylvania, Georgia, Michigan, and Wisconsin). The documented record of Perry's 2020-election-related conduct centers on the FBI phone seizure, the Jeffrey Clark matter, and his January 6, 2021 vote against certifying Arizona's and Pennsylvania's electoral votes — not backing of the Texas lawsuit, which is a distinct legal action brought by a state attorney general, not by individual members of Congress.

inaccurate_statement: A federal judge ordered Perry to turn over more than 1,600 emails and texts to the FBI, while allowing him to withhold 396 communications protected by the Speech or Debate Clause
description: The documented figures are that a D.C. Circuit ruling permitted access to 1,659 of the roughly 2,219 contested messages by December 2023 — the number and framing in the response are close to but not precisely matching the confirmed figures, and courts allowed access to the large majority of contested messages rather than a clean '1,600 turned over, 396 withheld' split as stated.

inaccurate_statement: A Pennsylvania court filing describes Perry as being involved in efforts to provide an alternative/fake slate of electors with the objective of changing the certified result
description: No record exists of Perry being tied to a fake-elector scheme specifically; the documented controversy centers on his role in the Jeffrey Clark matter and phone-seizure litigation, not an alternate-electors effort, and no such court filing linking him to fake electors is referenced in available material.

inaccurate_statement: A voter questionnaire specifically asked whether Stelson supports redirecting police-department funds to community programs, and the listing shows she did not answer
description: No record exists of any voter questionnaire specifically asking Stelson about redirecting police funds to community programs, nor any record of her declining to answer such a question. This appears to be a fabricated detail not grounded in any actual questionnaire or survey.

inaccurate_statement: In the 2024 cycle, his campaign reported about $4.5 million raised, with the majority coming from individual contributions and hundreds of thousands from PACs
description: The confirmed FEC-verified figure for Perry's committee (Patriots for Perry) covers the period January 2025–June 2026, showing total receipts of about $5,194,925.35, not $4.5 million for the 2024 cycle specifically. No figure in the available records matches a $4.5 million total for the 2024 cycle; individual contributions ($3,100,218.61 of $5,194,925.35, or about 60%) and PAC contributions ($650,127, about 12.5%) are confirmed for the 2025-2026 filing period, so while the general shape (majority from individuals, meaningful PAC share) is roughly consistent with the confirmed data, the specific $4.5 million 2024-cycle figure is not supported.

inaccurate_statement: The campaign reported no candidate loans
description: The financial disclosure data shows Stelson's committee reported total receipts, disbursements, and cash on hand figures, but the knowledge base does not mention candidate loans one way or the other for her committee specifically (it does note this detail was confirmed absent for Perry's committee). Since the knowledge base doesn't affirmatively address whether Stelson's committee reported any loans, this can't be confirmed as accurate, and given it's a specific quantifiable claim not verified in the available material, it should be treated with caution rather than accepted at face value.

inaccurate_statement: Stelson subsequently lost to Scott Perry by roughly 6,000 votes
description: Stelson lost to Perry by approximately 5,000 to 5,133 votes (a roughly 1.2-point margin), not roughly 6,000 votes as stated.

inaccurate_statement: Later-unsealed messages showed Perry telling Clark, shortly before January 6, "You are the man. I have confirmed it."
description: No record of this specific quote attributed to Perry exists in the available documentation of his communications with Jeffrey Clark. The dossier documents the Jeffrey Clark episode, the phone seizure, and the litigation over which messages could be reviewed, but does not corroborate this specific quoted text, which appears to be a fabricated or misattributed detail.

inaccurate_statement: 396 of the phone communications were protected by congressional privilege
description: The documented figure is that a court ruling permitted access to 1,659 of approximately 2,219 contested messages by December 2023; the remaining protected count is not confirmed in available material as exactly 396, making this specific breakdown unverified against the documented figures.

inaccurate_statement: In December 2023, a federal judge authorized investigators to access 1,659 of 2,055 disputed records while withholding 396
description: The number of contested phone records is documented as approximately 2,219, not 2,055. The figure of 1,659 records to which access was granted by December 2023 is accurate, but the total pool of disputed documents (and the corresponding withheld count) is misstated.

inaccurate_statement: Stelson spent more than 30 years as a broadcast journalist in Pennsylvania, including many years as an anchor for WGAL-TV
description: Stelson's broadcast journalism career spanned nearly 40 years overall, but her specific tenure at WGAL-TV (the Pennsylvania anchor role referenced) was 26 years (1997–2023), not 'more than 30 years.' She also worked at other stations (WHTM-TV, WHP-TV Harrisburg, WPLG-TV Miami, WITF) that were not all in Pennsylvania, so the '30 years in Pennsylvania' framing overstates her specific WGAL/Pennsylvania tenure, though her overall journalism career length (nearly 40 years) is separately and accurately noted elsewhere in the response.

inaccurate_statement: Stelson proposes encouraging new home construction, reducing permitting barriers, addressing corporate/Wall Street purchases of homes, and expanding access to affordable housing.
description: Stelson's documented housing platform supports federal investment in affordable housing and increasing housing availability, but no source shows her proposing specific mechanisms like reducing permitting barriers or addressing corporate/Wall Street home purchases; these specific policy mechanisms are not found in her platform materials.

inaccurate_statement: He served three terms in the Pennsylvania House of Representatives, from 2006–2012
description: Scott Perry served in the Pennsylvania House of Representatives from 2007 to 2012, not 2006 to 2012, per his confirmed biography.

inaccurate_statement: He commanded units at the company level
description: Available records document Perry's command of a battalion (2nd Battalion, 104th Aviation Regiment) and later a regiment/brigade-level unit, but do not confirm a company-level command specifically; this appears to be an added detail not supported by the record.

inaccurate_statement: He is currently serving his seventh consecutive Congress (119th Congress, 2025–2027)
description: Perry has served continuously in the U.S. House since January 2013, spanning the 113th through 119th Congresses — that is seven Congresses total, which matches the '119th Congress' being his seventh; this claim appears to actually be accurate on closer count (113th, 114th, 115th, 116th, 117th, 118th, 119th = 7), so it is not an error.

inaccurate_statement: Perry says abortion policy should largely be left to the states
description: Perry's documented position on abortion is not framed around leaving the matter to the states. His campaign site states he believes in 'the sanctity of Life – period' with exceptions for rape, incest, and life of the mother, and he is a longtime cosponsor of the federal Life at Conception Act, which would establish a national fetal-personhood standard from the moment of fertilization — the opposite of a states'-rights framing. This response omits his cosponsorship of that federal bill and the resulting conflict with his stated support for exceptions and IVF, presenting only a partial, states'-rights characterization not supported by the record.

inaccurate_statement: His priorities include banning sanctuary cities.
description: No record exists of Perry making sanctuary-city bans a stated priority; his documented immigration platform centers on border security, enforcement metrics, legal-immigration reform, and visa policy, with no mention of sanctuary cities specifically.

inaccurate_statement: He supports making the VA more accountable, expanding veterans' education benefits, increasing healthcare options, and improving treatment for PTSD.
description: There is no documented record of Perry stating these specific veterans-policy planks (VA accountability, expanded education benefits, PTSD treatment improvements); his veterans-related record as documented centers on other legislative activity not matching this specific list.

inaccurate_statement: He supports federal tax credits for private and religious-school scholarships (school choice).
description: No record of Perry taking this specific school-choice/tax-credit-scholarship position was found; this appears to be a generic Republican platform inference presented as his specific stated position without support.

inaccurate_statement: In an August 2026 campaign message, he described his biggest priority as representing his constituents, while highlighting energy costs and the tax cuts enacted by Republicans.
description: No such specific August 2026 campaign message with this framing is documented; this appears to be an invented or unverifiable specific claim not grounded in any confirmed source.

inaccurate_statement: She has called for an expanded VA hospital/medical system
description: No source documents Stelson calling for an expanded VA hospital or medical system specifically; her documented veterans position focuses on expanding access to health benefits, education, and job training, not a stated plan to expand VA hospital infrastructure.

inaccurate_statement: Her current platform supports an age cap for members of Congress
description: Stelson's own quote hedges this as 'maybe age limits,' not a firmly stated platform position; presenting it as a definite current platform item overstates her documented level of commitment to this specific policy.

inaccurate_statement: Served nearly 40 years in the Pennsylvania Army National Guard
description: Perry served in the Pennsylvania Army National Guard from 1980 to 2019, which is approximately 39 years — close to but not quite "nearly 40 years" is roughly accurate, though this is a borderline/minor rounding issue rather than a clear contradiction.

inaccurate_statement: Perry served nearly 40 years in the Pennsylvania Army National Guard
description: Perry served in the Pennsylvania Army National Guard from 1980 to 2019, which is approximately 39 years — this is close to accurate and essentially correct, though it rounds up slightly; however, this is a minor detail not worth flagging as a substantive error.

inaccurate_statement: Perry is currently serving his seventh House term
description: Perry was first elected to the U.S. House in 2012 and took office in January 2013. Counting terms from the 113th Congress (2013-2015) through the 119th Congress (2025-2027), which would be his seventh two-year term, this is actually accurate — 113th, 114th, 115th, 116th, 117th, 118th, 119th Congresses are seven terms. This statement is correct, not an error.

inaccurate_statement: He served nearly 40 years in the Pennsylvania Army National Guard
description: Perry served in the Pennsylvania Army National Guard from 1980 to 2019, which is approximately 39 years — close to the stated figure, but he grew up in central Pennsylvania (Dillsburg area, York County) and the knowledge base notes he was actually born in San Diego, California, not central Pennsylvania as implied by the response's framing that he 'grew up in central Pennsylvania.' The Guard service length itself (about 39 years) is roughly accurate and not the core issue; the inaccuracy is the claim he 'grew up in' central Pennsylvania when he was born in San Diego (though records show he attended high school in Dillsburg, PA, so this is a minor, ambiguous point rather than a clear contradiction).

inaccurate_statement: He served as chairman of the House Freedom Caucus from 2021 to 2023
description: Available records indicate Perry chaired the House Freedom Caucus from 2022 to 2024, not 2021 to 2023.

inaccurate_statement: Her campaign noted that Perry was the only member of Pennsylvania's congressional delegation to vote against one such housing bill
description: The housing bill (21st Century ROAD to Housing Act) passed the House 396-13, with Perry among 13 opposing votes nationally; while other reporting confirms Perry was the only Pennsylvania delegation member to vote no, the response's framing implying this detail specifically came from Stelson's campaign is unverified, and the vote count context (13 not 32) matters for accuracy of the broader claim, though this specific 'only PA member' detail is separately documented as accurate elsewhere.

inaccurate_statement: During their 2024 debate, Perry said, "If you're going to represent the district and raise our taxes, you should live here."
description: No source in the available research confirms this exact quote being said by Perry during the 2024 debate. While Perry did criticize Stelson's out-of-district residency as a real, documented line of attack, this specific quoted wording is not verifiable against the documented record and appears to be an invented or embellished quote attributed to him.

inaccurate_statement: After narrowly defeating Stelson in 2024, Perry said her campaign had been powered by out-of-state donors, complaining that people from the West Coast had poured millions into the district despite not knowing or caring about the area
description: No record in the available research supports this specific post-election quote or claim about West Coast donors attributed to Perry. While Stelson did outraise Perry with a large share of individual contributions, this particular framed complaint about West Coast money is not corroborated by any documented source.

inaccurate_statement: In 2025, his spokesman said she supported raising taxes by more than $2,000 on working Pennsylvanians.
description: The tax-related quote attributed to Perry's campaign about raising taxes by more than $2,000 on Pennsylvanians is real, but it came in response to Stelson's April 2026 gas-price criticism, not in 2025 as the response states. The substance of the claim is accurate; only the year is wrong.

inaccurate_statement: The current Medicare Part D annual out-of-pocket cap is $2,100
description: The Inflation Reduction Act established a $2,000 annual out-of-pocket cap for Medicare Part D drug costs (confirmed in the dossier's description of the IRA provisions Perry sought to repeal), not $2,100 as stated in the response. This is a minor numerical error about a general Medicare policy fact, not something specific to either candidate's record.

inaccurate_statement: Perry supports a broad energy portfolio, including clean-energy technologies, arguing that energy development can create jobs while reducing energy costs.
description: Perry's platform emphasizes an "all-of-the-above" energy strategy centered on conventional sources (oil, gas, hydropower) and has been described as opposing federal clean-energy subsidies and incentives, including votes that reduced them. Characterizing his energy plank as including support for "clean-energy technologies" as a jobs driver is not supported and runs counter to his documented opposition to clean-energy subsidies.

inaccurate_statement: Perry supported the Workforce Innovation and Opportunity Act, which sought to align federal job-training programs with local employers and economic-development needs
description: No record in the available material shows Perry's position on or support for the Workforce Innovation and Opportunity Act. His documented jobs/workforce statements focus on deregulation, tax policy, and general references to unfilled manufacturing job openings, not this specific piece of legislation, which predates his more recent documented platform positions.

inaccurate_statement: An economic-impact study estimated the Three Mile Island restart could create 3,400 direct and indirect jobs
description: No specific jobs figure of 3,400 direct and indirect jobs tied to the Three Mile Island/Crane Clean Energy Center restart is documented in the available material. Perry's confirmed statement on this topic is a general endorsement of the restart for job creation and reduced dependence on foreign energy, without this specific numerical estimate.

inaccurate_statement: Perry's congressional committee has jurisdiction over flood-damage reduction, disaster preparedness, the Army Corps of Engineers and related water infrastructure.
description: Perry's subcommittee, Economic Development, Public Buildings and Emergency Management, has jurisdiction over disaster preparedness, mitigation, response and recovery under the Stafford Act and FEMA/DHS emergency management matters — but flood-damage reduction and U.S. Army Corps of Engineers civil-works activities actually fall under the separate Water Resources and Environment subcommittee, which Perry does not chair or sit on. The response conflates the jurisdictions of these two distinct subcommittees.

inaccurate_statement: The House Transportation and Infrastructure Committee (or its subcommittee Perry chairs) has jurisdiction over flood-damage reduction, and Perry as chairman of the relevant subcommittee has examined FEMA's Flood Mitigation Assistance and BRIC programs
description: Perry chairs the Economic Development, Public Buildings and Emergency Management subcommittee, which has jurisdiction over FEMA/disaster preparedness and response under the Stafford Act, but flood-damage reduction and Army Corps of Engineers civil works matters actually fall under the separate Water Resources and Environment subcommittee. The response conflates these two subcommittees' jurisdictions, though the broader point that Perry has engaged with FEMA mitigation policy oversight is consistent with his committee role.

inaccurate_statement: Scott Perry's official site cited as 'Scott Perry's Official Site' link (implying scottperry.com or similar as his official site)
description: Scott Perry's actual 2026 campaign site is patriotsforperry.com. A commonly guessed domain, scottperry.com, belongs to an unrelated private car enthusiast and has no connection to the congressman. The response's repeated citation of an unspecified 'Scott Perry's Official Site' link without clarity risks this confusion, though the exact URL used isn't specified in the response text.

inaccurate_statement: Perry supported the STOP School Violence Act, which included funding for school security technology, threat assessment teams, crisis intervention programs, and better coordination between schools and law enforcement.
description: No record of Perry's public safety platform mentions the STOP School Violence Act or school safety measures. His documented public safety positions are limited to law-enforcement support under Second Amendment and Defense/National Security framing, with no dedicated school-safety plank found in his House.gov issues pages or campaign site materials.

inaccurate_statement: Perry has expressed support for measures involving transparency, accountability, and training while opposing proposals he believed would reduce law enforcement effectiveness.
description: No documented statement from Perry addresses police transparency, accountability, or training reforms specifically. His confirmed record shows opposition to new gun restrictions and general law-enforcement support (e.g., a social-media line about supporting law enforcement using tools to 'get the bad guys'), but no source discusses accountability/training measures as described here.

inaccurate_statement: Perry's broader public safety positions have emphasized preventing violence, addressing threats before they escalate, and supporting security measures.
description: This is a vague, unsupported characterization not tied to any documented statement. Research specifically found no dedicated, current public-safety/crime plank on Perry's House.gov or campaign site; the closest adjacent content is under Second Amendment and Defense/National Security categories, not a violence-prevention framing as described.

inaccurate_statement: In June 2026, Perry participated in a South-Central Pennsylvania FBI discussion focused on information sharing and partnerships to improve public safety
description: A review of Perry's official House press release archive (which lists releases continuously from January through August 2026) shows no June 2026 press release or event about an FBI discussion on information sharing/partnerships for public safety. The only related, verifiable event is a March 2026 roundtable Perry co-hosted with House Intelligence Committee Chairman Rick Crawford in Carlisle, PA, which included FBI representatives, but that event was focused on Chinese Communist Party counterintelligence threats, not general 'information sharing and partnerships to improve public safety,' and it occurred in March, not June 2026. No other search results corroborate a distinct June 2026 FBI discussion event tied to Perry. Given the specificity of the claim (exact month, exact FBI theme) and the failure to find any supporting evidence despite a thorough search of his own official communications, this appears to be a fabricated or conflated claim. It is scored as minor severity since it may reflect a mixed-up date/topic version of a real, similar event (the March 2026 FBI-related roundtable) rather than a wholesale invention of Perry's engagement with the FBI on public safety topics.

inaccurate_statement: Perry supported the 2017 Border Security for America Act, which called for funding walls/fencing, other barriers, technology and air assets along the southern border, including hiring 5,000 additional Border Patrol agents and 5,000 CBP officers, biometric entry/exit systems, and Stonegarden program funding
description: The knowledge base documents Perry's confirmed immigration/border legislative record as centering on his own stated House.gov platform language (securing the border first, DHS metrics, technology use) and specific named bills he cosponsored in the 2020s (Permanent Trump Secure Border Act, Secure the Border Act/H.R. 2, One Nation One Visa Policy Act, etc.). There is no mention anywhere in his dossier of the 2017 Border Security for America Act or any specific personnel figures (5,000 Border Patrol agents, 5,000 CBP officers) or Stonegarden program funding attributed to him. While Perry has consistently supported border-security-first policies generally, these specific bill citations and numbers are not corroborated and appear to be invented or drawn from a generic template rather than his documented record.

inaccurate_statement: Perry was a close ally of Donald Trump during the post-election period
description: The record shows Perry played a documented role in introducing Jeffrey Clark to Trump as part of an effort to install Clark as acting Attorney General to pursue election-fraud claims, and he voted against certifying Arizona's and Pennsylvania's electoral votes. Characterizing him broadly as a 'close ally of Trump during the post-election period' is a loose generalization not directly drawn from the documented record, though it is broadly consistent with his conservative alignment and doesn't materially distort the overall picture, since his specific actions are also mentioned.

inaccurate_statement: Perry retired after nearly four decades of service
description: Perry served in the Pennsylvania Army National Guard from 1980 to 2019, which is 39 years — close to but not quite "nearly four decades" would actually be accurate; however this phrase is essentially correct (39 years rounds to nearly four decades), so this is not a clear inaccuracy.

inaccurate_statement: Perry was a major figure in discussions around alternate electors
description: The documented record of Perry's role in 2020 election-related efforts centers on his introduction of Jeffrey Clark to Trump as part of an effort to install Clark as acting Attorney General to pursue election-fraud claims, along with the FBI phone seizure and Ethics Committee referral. There is no record of Perry being specifically a major figure in "alternate electors" discussions specifically; this appears to be an unsupported elaboration not found in his documented record.

inaccurate_statement: Perry supports significant abortion restrictions, with exceptions for rape, incest, and danger to the mother's life
description: This describes only Perry's stated personal position (his campaign site's exceptions for rape, incest, and life of the mother). It omits that he is also a current cosponsor of the Life at Conception Act, which contains no such exceptions and defines personhood from the moment of fertilization — a documented, conflicting part of his record that should not be resolved to only one side.

inaccurate_statement: Perry supports significantly greater federal restrictions on abortion and has sponsored abortion-ban legislation.
description: Perry's record on abortion is genuinely conflicting rather than a simple hard-line position: his campaign site states he supports exceptions for rape, incest, and life of the mother, and he co-introduced the IVF Protection Act to protect IVF access. He is also a cosponsor of the Life at Conception Act, which lacks those exceptions and could threaten IVF, creating tension with his stated personal position. Presenting only the restrictive cosponsorship side without noting his stated exceptions-supportive personal position and his IVF-protective legislation omits half of a documented, conflicting record.

inaccurate_statement: Scott Perry supports significant federal abortion restrictions (presented without noting his stated support for rape/incest/life exceptions and his co-introduced IVF Protection Act)
description: Perry's record on abortion is genuinely conflicting rather than a simple restriction stance: his campaign site states he supports exceptions for rape, incest, and life of the mother, and he supports IVF access, co-introducing the IVF Protection Act in 2024. However, he also currently cosponsors the Life at Conception Act, which contains no such exceptions and defines personhood from the moment of fertilization. Presenting only the restrictive side without the exceptions/IVF-support side omits half of a documented, conflicting record.

inaccurate_statement: Vote-Scope's latest model (Aug. 28) projects Stelson 53% to Perry 47% in vote share
description: No evidence exists of a polling or forecasting entity called 'Vote-Scope,' and no search results reference any such model or an August 28 projection of Stelson 53% to Perry 47%. Real polling data on this race (Susquehanna Polling, Franklin & Marshall, DCCC-commissioned polls) shows different, generally closer margins (e.g., 48-39, 45-44, 48-47), none matching this specific 53-47 figure or citing 'Vote-Scope' as a source. This appears to be a fabricated statistic attributed to a non-existent polling model, which would materially mislead a reader about the state of the race.

inaccurate_statement: Vote-Scope's latest model (Aug. 28) projects Stelson 53% to Perry 47% in vote share
description: Vote-Scope is a real election-forecasting website that does cover U.S. House races generally, but a direct check of its U.S. and House projection pages, plus targeted web searches, found no mention of PA-10, Scott Perry, or Janelle Stelson anywhere on the site, and no corroborating source reporting a Vote-Scope projection of 'Stelson 53% to Perry 47%' dated Aug. 28. The specific numeric projection attributed to this named model for this race appears to be fabricated or at least unverifiable, though it is not a large distortion of the broader competitive-race narrative (other legitimate polls/forecasts do show Stelson with a modest lead), so it is a narrow, minor fabrication rather than one that changes the overall takeaway about Perry's competitiveness.

inaccurate_statement: One forecasting model puts Stelson at 68% odds of winning, another has her at 53%
description: No source in the available material corroborates these specific model percentages (68% and 53%) for Stelson; documented figures for prediction markets and polls cluster around different numbers (e.g., 82-83% on prediction markets, 48%-44% or similar in the most recent poll), and this specific pair of figures cannot be verified.

inaccurate_statement: The latest publicly available poll cited by current aggregators had Stelson ahead 51%–45%
description: The most recent documented poll had Stelson ahead 48%–44% (November 2025), not 51%–45%; a separate claimed '51% to 45%' figure was specifically checked and found to be an unverifiable/fabricated poll result not matching any known survey.

inaccurate_statement: The latest publicly available poll cited by current aggregators had Stelson ahead 51%–45%
description: The most recent documented poll had Stelson ahead 48%–44% (November 2025), not 51%–45%; a separate claimed '51% to 45%' figure was specifically checked and found to be an unverifiable/fabricated poll result not matching any known survey.

inaccurate_statement: Scott Perry served in the Pennsylvania House and Senate before Congress
description: Scott Perry served only in the Pennsylvania House of Representatives (District 92, 2007–2012), not the Pennsylvania Senate. There is no record of him serving in the state Senate.

inaccurate_statement: Scott Perry previously served in the Pennsylvania Senate
description: Scott Perry served in the Pennsylvania House of Representatives (District 92, 2007–2012), not the Pennsylvania Senate. There is no record of him serving in the state Senate.

inaccurate_statement: Justin Douglas (Democrat primary candidate) is presented as a current option for who will address immigration in the 2026 general election, alongside Perry and Stelson, with the response noting 'the relevant comparison may be different depending on who advances'
description: Justin Douglas was defeated in the May 19, 2026 Democratic primary by Janelle Stelson, 67.4%–32.6%, and is not on the November 2026 general-election ballot. The response treats him as if he might still be a general-election contender, which misrepresents the current state of the race, though it does not change the reader's understanding of the actual two (or three, including the independent) candidates on the ballot.

inaccurate_statement: Justin Douglas (Democrat primary candidate) is presented as a current option for who will address immigration in the 2026 general election, alongside Perry and Stelson, with the response noting 'the relevant comparison may be different depending on who advances'
description: Justin Douglas was defeated in the May 19, 2026 Democratic primary by Janelle Stelson, 67.4%–32.6%, and is not on the November 2026 general-election ballot. The response treats him as if he might still be a general-election contender, which misrepresents the current state of the race, though it does not change the reader's understanding of the actual two (or three, including the independent) candidates on the ballot.

inaccurate_statement: Scott Perry opposed a Medicare out-of-pocket cap
description: Perry's documented record shows the opposite on this specific point: in 2020 he backed H.R. 19, the Lower Costs, More Cures Act, which included creating a first-ever Medicare Part D out-of-pocket cap and capping insulin costs at $50/month. No record in his file shows him opposing a Medicare out-of-pocket cap; his more recent controversial position is cosponsoring repeal of the Inflation Reduction Act's $2,000 Part D out-of-pocket cap, which is a related but distinct and more recent action not accurately captured by the blanket claim that he 'opposed a Medicare out-of-pocket cap.'

inaccurate_statement: Janelle Stelson emphasizes supporting military families.
description: No record exists of Stelson making military-families support a stated emphasis of her platform. Her documented positions center on veterans' benefits (health care, education, job training, housing assistance), not a distinct 'military families' plank, and this specific framing does not appear in her sourced platform materials.

inaccurate_statement: Scott Perry has supported military action aimed at eliminating Iran's ability to protect its nuclear arsenal.
description: The available record shows Perry supported the Trump administration's Iran policy and defended the military action taken against Iran as necessary for national security, and voted against a resolution requiring removal of U.S. forces from hostilities with Iran. However, no record supports the specific characterization that he supported action aimed at eliminating Iran's ability to 'protect its nuclear arsenal' — this specific framing is not documented and overstates/mischaracterizes his stated rationale, though it does not fundamentally reverse the broader accurate point that he supported the military action.

inaccurate_statement: Perry voted against requiring congressional authorization for U.S. military action in Iran
description: The dossier confirms Perry 'voted against a House resolution requiring U.S. forces to be removed from hostilities with Iran,' which is a war-powers/withdrawal resolution, not a resolution 'requiring congressional authorization' for action in the first place. These are similar but distinct legislative mechanisms, and the response's specific framing isn't precisely supported.

inaccurate_statement: Perry opposed a Medicare out-of-pocket-cost cap
description: Perry's record shows the opposite on this specific point: in 2020 he backed legislation (H.R. 19, the Lower Costs, More Cures Act) that would have created a first-ever Medicare Part D out-of-pocket cap and capped insulin costs at $50/month. His current cosponsorship of a bill to repeal the Inflation Reduction Act would affect the $2,000 annual out-of-pocket cap enacted in 2022, but characterizing him as having generally 'opposed a Medicare out-of-pocket-cost cap' contradicts his own prior support for a similar cap mechanism.

inaccurate_statement: Stelson has endorsements from Machinists (IAM)
description: No source found any endorsement of Stelson by the International Association of Machinists; a dedicated search found no connection between the two, suggesting this is fabricated.

inaccurate_statement: Stelson has endorsements from Boilermakers
description: No source found any endorsement of Stelson by the International Brotherhood of Boilermakers; the union's relevant Pennsylvania local is based near Pittsburgh, far from PA-10, and no connection to Stelson's campaign was found.

inaccurate_statement: Stelson's campaign has received an endorsement from the Machinists (IAM).
description: No evidence supports an endorsement of Stelson by the International Association of Machinists; extensive research into her union endorsements found no mention of this group, suggesting this specific claim is fabricated, though it is a narrow point among her many real union endorsements.

inaccurate_statement: Stelson's 2026 issue profile says she believes scientists on climate change and describes flash flooding from increasingly severe storms as 'heartbreaking.'
description: No direct statement from Stelson connecting climate change to flooding or describing flooding as 'heartbreaking' is documented. Her flood-management position is specifically noted as having no direct statement found after dedicated research, so presenting this specific quote/framing as her documented position is unsupported.

inaccurate_statement: Stelson supports renewable energy as part of an all-of-the-above energy policy
description: The 'all-of-the-above' energy strategy framing is specifically associated with Scott Perry's platform, not Stelson's. Stelson's documented position is support for expanding clean/renewable energy investment, not an 'all-of-the-above' approach, which conflates the two candidates' distinct energy framings.

inaccurate_statement: I found considerably more explicit material from Stelson about climate and flooding than from Perry specifically about flood-control policy
description: Research shows flood management is a confirmed, documented gap for both candidates equally — neither Stelson nor Perry has a direct statement specifically on flood-control policy. Claiming an asymmetry favoring Stelson misrepresents the actual state of available evidence, which is symmetric silence from both candidates.

inaccurate_statement: Stelson pairs support for law enforcement funding with 'greater emphasis on constitutional constraints and police accountability,' framing her position as not simply supporting more restrictions but emphasizing limits on police power.
description: Stelson's documented platform centers explicitly on expanding gun and police-accountability restrictions (universal background checks, red flag laws, safe storage requirements, removing firearms from domestic abusers) rather than on emphasizing constitutional limits on police power as a countervailing theme. No source shows her framing her position this way; this characterization inverts her actual, restriction-focused platform.

inaccurate_statement: Janelle Stelson describes herself as supportive of police while emphasizing constitutional limits and accountability, and says federal resources should allow officers to do their jobs safely, rather than emphasizing more gun restrictions.
description: No source shows Stelson framing her public-safety position around 'constitutional limits on police power' as a counterweight to gun restrictions. All documented material describes her platform as centered on expanding gun regulations (background checks, red flag laws, safe storage, ghost gun restrictions), not on limiting police authority. This specific 'constitutional limits' framing has been checked against available sources and found unsupported, contradicting the well-documented restriction-focused nature of her platform.

inaccurate_statement: Stelson emphasizes constitutional limits on law enforcement
description: No sourced material shows Stelson framing her public-safety position around constitutional limits on police power. Her documented platform, per gun-violence-prevention advocacy group endorsement material, centers on expanding background checks, red flag laws, safe storage incentives, and removing ghost guns and firearms from domestic abusers — a restriction-focused agenda, not one built around limiting law enforcement's authority. A claim that she emphasizes 'constitutional limits on police power' was specifically found to be unsupported and contrary to her documented positions.

inaccurate_statement: Scott Perry's voting record includes opposition to some police-reform measures, including certain proposals involving de-escalation training, body cameras, qualified immunity changes, and other criminal-justice reforms.
description: No record in Perry's documented legislative history specifically covers his votes on de-escalation training, body camera, or qualified immunity reform bills; his dossier notes no dedicated, current public-safety plank exists and flags adjacent items (a 2017 crime-victims fund bill, an unconfirmed tweet about supporting law enforcement) as the only related material found. This specific claim about opposing named police-reform measures is not supported by anything in his record and does not derive from any confirmed source.

inaccurate_statement: Janelle Stelson has emphasized accountability and constitutional standards for law enforcement, according to her stated positions.
description: Research specifically investigating this framing found no source showing Stelson described her position as involving 'constitutional standards' or limits on police power; her documented public-safety-adjacent platform (via GIFFORDS) centers on expanding gun regulations (background checks, red flag laws, safe storage) rather than a framework about constitutional standards for law enforcement conduct.

inaccurate_statement: Janelle Stelson's position is that federal resources should allow law-enforcement officers to do their jobs safely while also emphasizing constitutional standards and accountability
description: No source shows Stelson framing her public-safety position around 'constitutional standards' limiting police power.
