description: Club for Growth is indeed a top contributor to Perry's campaigns, but across every election cycle checked (2018, 2020, 2023-2024), OpenSecrets/FEC data show these contributions are attributed entirely to individuals bundled through Club for Growth's network, with $0 coming from the PAC itself (e.g., Club for Growth totals of $51,887, $115,171, and $96,817 in various cycles, all listed as '$0' under 'PACs'). Direct PAC-to-candidate contributions are also capped at $5,000 per election under FEC rules, making a $15,800 direct PAC contribution from a single PAC in one cycle implausible without conduit/bundling being involved (which is exactly what OpenSecrets classifies as individual money, not PAC money). Thus, the claim's core framing—that Club for Growth PAC directly gave ~$15,800 in itemized PAC contributions—misstates how this money is categorized. The broader point that Club for Growth is a major, closely-linked backer of Perry is accurate, but the specific 'direct PAC contribution' amount and classification appears to be a factual/technical error rather than reflecting the real funding mechanism (individual bundled contributions), so this is a minor inaccuracy rather than one that would change the overall takeaway about Perry's relationship with Club for Growth.

inaccurate_statement: Numerous machinists, steelworker, laborers, and Teamsters organizations have endorsed Stelson (specifically citing machinists/IAM and Teamsters unions among a broad slate)
description: Research specifically found no evidence of an International Association of Machinists (IAM) endorsement of Stelson, and while she does have Teamsters and steelworker union support (Pennsylvania Conference of Teamsters, United Steelworkers District 10), the specific claim of an IAM/Machinists endorsement was checked and not found to be supported, appearing to be a fabricated addition to an otherwise broadly accurate labor-endorsement picture.

inaccurate_statement: The York County Harley-Davidson plant is a major manufacturing employer in PA-10, and recent U.S.-Canada tariff tensions have directly affected the plant's outlook
description: Harley-Davidson's York plant is located in York County, but no material in the available research on this race identifies this specific facility as a citied talking point in either candidate's platform or in campaign coverage of PA-10 manufacturing; this appears to be an unsupported, specific factual insertion not grounded in either candidate's documented record on manufacturing in the district.

inaccurate_statement: The York County Harley-Davidson plant is a major manufacturing employer in PA-10, and recent U.S.-Canada tariff tensions have directly affected the plant's outlook
description: Harley-Davidson's York plant is located in York County, but no material in the available research on this race identifies this specific facility as a citied talking point in either candidate's platform or in campaign coverage of PA-10 manufacturing; this appears to be an unsupported, specific factual insertion not grounded in either candidate's documented record on manufacturing in the district.

inaccurate_statement: Perry previously chaired a Transportation & Infrastructure subcommittee covering economic development, public buildings and emergency management.
description: Scott Perry currently chairs the Subcommittee on Economic Development, Public Buildings and Emergency Management within the 119th Congress (2025-2026), not in the past — this is his current, ongoing committee role, not a former one.

inaccurate_statement: Independent candidate Isabelle Harman withdrew from the race
description: Isabelle Harman, an Independent candidate, is documented as being on the November 2026 PA-10 general-election ballot alongside Perry and Stelson, with no indication in available records that she withdrew from the race.

inaccurate_statement: Independent candidate Isabelle Harman withdrew from the race
description: Isabelle Harman, an Independent candidate, is documented as being on the November 2026 PA-10 general-election ballot alongside Perry and Stelson, with no indication in available records that she withdrew from the race.

inaccurate_statement: Isabelle Harman, who initially ran as an independent, has withdrawn, so she is not on the November ballot
description: Isabelle Harman is documented as an Independent candidate who is on the November 2026 PA-10 general-election ballot alongside Perry and Stelson, not someone who withdrew from the race.

inaccurate_statement: Isabelle Harman, who initially ran as an independent, has withdrawn, so she is not on the November ballot
description: Isabelle Harman is documented as an Independent candidate who is on the November 2026 PA-10 general-election ballot alongside Perry and Stelson, not someone who withdrew from the race.

inaccurate_statement: Perry favors replacing the ACA with a more market-oriented approach.
description: Perry's official health-issues page does use fairly standard market-oriented GOP messaging (interstate insurance sales, HSA expansion, tort reform) critical of the ACA, but this framing is characterized as dated 2010s-era material rather than a fresh 2026 platform statement, and it omits his more consequential and current record: he voted for the 2025 reconciliation bill's Medicaid work requirements (projected to cause PA-10 residents to lose coverage), cosponsored legislation to repeal the Inflation Reduction Act's Medicare drug-price negotiation authority, and called permanent extension of enhanced ACA subsidies 'a colossal mistake.' Presenting his position solely as generic pro-market ACA reform, without this more specific and current record, is an incomplete characterization, though not a fabrication.

inaccurate_statement: Perry emphasizes parental control and reducing the federal government's role in education.
description: No education-specific platform plank emphasizing 'parental control' or reducing the federal government's role in education is documented for Perry; his confirmed platform issues are Agriculture, Defense/National Security, Economy/Jobs, Education, Energy, Federal Spending, Health Care, Immigration, Right to Life, Second Amendment, Social Security/Medicare, Transportation, and Veterans, but no specific parental-rights-in-education statement or record was found to substantiate this characterization.

inaccurate_statement: Perry supports the Dobbs framework and greater state authority over abortion.
description: This presents only one side of Perry's genuinely conflicting abortion record. His campaign site states he supports exceptions for rape, incest, and life of the mother and that he supports IVF access (having co-introduced the IVF Protection Act), but he is also a current cosponsor of the Life at Conception Act, which contains no such exceptions and defines personhood from the moment of fertilization — a position in tension with both a simple 'state authority' framing and his own stated exceptions. Presenting his position as simply 'Dobbs framework, state authority' without noting this conflict omits material context.

inaccurate_statement: Independent Isabelle Harman has withdrawn from the race, according to a September race tracker
description: There is no evidence Isabelle Harman withdrew from the PA-10 race. Both candidates' documented records confirm she remains on the November 2026 general-election ballot as an Independent candidate alongside Perry and Stelson. Describing the field as having 'narrowed' due to her withdrawal is a fabricated development that misrepresents the current ballot composition.

inaccurate_statement: Independent Isabelle Harman has withdrawn from the race, according to a September race tracker
description: There is no evidence Isabelle Harman withdrew from the PA-10 race. Both candidates' documented records confirm she remains on the November 2026 general-election ballot as an Independent candidate alongside Perry and Stelson. Describing the field as having 'narrowed' due to her withdrawal is a fabricated development that misrepresents the current ballot composition.

inaccurate_statement: Stelson won the primary roughly 69%–31%
description: The actual primary result was 67.4%–32.6%, not 69%–31%. The margin is close but the specific figures are off.

inaccurate_statement: That eliminated the main uncertainty on the Democratic side and set up a 2024 rematch with Rep. Scott Perry.
description: This is a 2026 general-election rematch of the 2024 contest, not '2024 rematch' — the current race is happening in the November 2026 election cycle, not 2024.

inaccurate_statement: Perry won by only about four points [in 2024]
description: Perry defeated Stelson in November 2024 by approximately 1.2 percentage points (about 50.5%-49.3% or 50.6%-49.4%), not four points. This significantly overstates how comfortable his 2024 win was.

inaccurate_statement: prediction markets have put Stelson around 77% to win versus 25% for Perry
description: Prediction market trackers consistently show Stelson at about 82-83% and Perry at roughly 26-28%, not 77%/25% as stated. The overall direction (Stelson strongly favored) is correct, but the specific figures are off.

description: Prediction market trackers consistently show Stelson at about 82-83% and Perry at roughly 26-28%, not 77%/25% as stated. The overall direction (Stelson strongly favored) is correct, but the specific figures are off.

inaccurate_statement: A current Pennsylvania political-race tracker has Stelson at roughly 77% to win versus 25% for Perry
description: PA-10 between Janelle Stelson and incumbent Scott Perry was consistently rated by forecasters and trackers (e.g., Cook Political Report, Sabato's Crystal Ball, 538) as a highly competitive toss-up or lean-Republican race throughout the 2024 cycle, not a race where Stelson held a lopsided ~77% win probability versus 25% for Perry. Perry ultimately won re-election in November 2024, further contradicting the notion that any credible tracker gave Stelson such a dominant probability of victory. No evidence supports the existence of a 'current' tracker showing this specific 77%-25% split, and the figure is inconsistent with how this race was actually characterized by political forecasters.

inaccurate_statement: Ballotpedia's 2026 analysis calls Perry the most conservative of several vulnerable Republican incumbents
description: The underlying fact is real: PoliticsPA analyst Louis Jacobson ranked Perry as the most vulnerable House incumbent for 2026 and noted he has articulated the most conservative views of the four vulnerable Republicans on that list. However, this analysis was produced by PoliticsPA, not Ballotpedia. Ballotpedia's news page simply quoted/reported on PoliticsPA's ranking rather than conducting its own '2026 analysis' calling Perry the most conservative. The claim misattributes the source of the analysis, though the substantive point about Perry being ranked as the most conservative of vulnerable Republican incumbents is accurate. This is a narrow misattribution that doesn't undermine the broader point being made.

inaccurate_statement: Stelson leads Perry 51%–45% in the most recent publicly listed poll (Normington Petts, April 2026)
description: No poll matching these specific figures and this pollster attribution could be found. Actual PA-10 polls cited in research show different results: a House Majority PAC/Data for Progress poll had Stelson leading 46%-43%, an F&M College poll showed different margins (45%-44% or 51%-48% depending on report), and the most recent conventional poll found was 48%-44% (November 2025), not April 2026. No poll with the exact 'Stelson 51% to Perry 45%' figure, dated April 2026, or attributed to 'Normington Petts' was found, indicating this specific poll citation is fabricated. The broader narrative of a competitive, Stelson-favored race remains directionally accurate.

inaccurate_statement: Stelson leads Perry 51%–45% in the most recent publicly listed poll (Normington Petts, April 2026)

inaccurate_statement: Stelson had no Washington experience before her 2025 campaign.
description: Stelson's first campaign for this congressional seat was in 2024, not 2025 — she ran against and narrowly lost to Perry in the November 2024 general election, not in a 2025 campaign.

inaccurate_statement: Before Congress, Scott Perry served in the Pennsylvania House and Senate
description: Scott Perry served in the Pennsylvania House of Representatives (District 92) from 2007 to 2012, but there is no record of him serving in the Pennsylvania Senate. This appears to be an erroneous addition, though it does not change the overall accurate point that he has extensive prior political and military experience.

inaccurate_statement: Harrisburg's police report says its homicide clearance rate was 78.5%
description: No record of this specific homicide clearance rate figure exists in the available background material on Harrisburg crime statistics; it is not corroborated by any of the sourced Harrisburg crime data (homicides, assaults, staffing vacancies) that is confirmed elsewhere.

inaccurate_statement: Harrisburg's police report says its homicide clearance rate was 78.5%
description: No record of this specific homicide clearance rate figure exists in the available background material on Harrisburg crime statistics; it is not corroborated by any of the sourced Harrisburg crime data (homicides, assaults, staffing vacancies) that is confirmed elsewhere.

inaccurate_statement: Perry's record includes votes against federal requirements involving police body cameras, de-escalation techniques, and certain criminal-justice reforms
description: No documented voting record on federal police body-camera or de-escalation-technique mandates was found for Scott Perry; his confirmed law-enforcement-related record centers on immigration enforcement, opposition to background-check expansion, and support for officer-safety and immigration-related legislation, not votes specifically on body cameras or de-escalation training requirements.

inaccurate_statement: Perry has supported ACA repeal/replacement
description: The available record shows Perry's official health-issues page uses standard 2010s-era GOP messaging criticizing the ACA (interstate insurance sales, HSA expansion, tort reform) and he cosponsored repeal of the Inflation Reduction Act's drug pricing provisions, but there is no confirmed direct statement or vote specifically characterized as 'ACA repeal/replacement' legislation in the current record. This is a generic characterization not directly tied to a specific, confirmed vote or bill in the available material, though it is broadly consistent with his documented opposition to ACA subsidy extensions and general conservative healthcare positioning.

inaccurate_statement: Perry has substantial direct involvement in federal disaster policy because he chairs a Transportation & Infrastructure subcommittee covering emergency management, implying this gives him direct flood-policy jurisdiction
description: Perry does chair the Economic Development, Public Buildings and Emergency Management subcommittee, which covers disaster preparedness, mitigation, response, and recovery under the Stafford Act and FEMA/DHS matters. However, flood-damage reduction and Army Corps of Engineers civil works activities actually fall under the separate Water Resources and Environment subcommittee, not the one Perry chairs. Presenting his subcommittee role as giving him substantial flood-specific policy involvement overstates his jurisdiction on this particular issue.

inaccurate_statement: Perry has supported reforms to the National Flood Insurance Program (NFIP), emphasizing financial sustainability and greater private-market participation rather than simply putting more federal money into the program
description: No record of Perry taking a specific position on NFIP reform, financial sustainability, or private-market participation in flood insurance was found in available research on his platform or voting record. This appears to be an invented specific policy position not grounded in his documented statements.

inaccurate_statement: Perry's subcommittee on the House Transportation and Infrastructure Committee has jurisdiction that includes flood-damage reduction.
description: Perry chairs the Economic Development, Public Buildings and Emergency Management subcommittee, which covers disaster preparedness, mitigation, response and recovery under the Stafford Act and FEMA/DHS matters, but flood-damage reduction and Army Corps of Engineers civil-works activities actually fall under the separate Water Resources and Environment subcommittee, not the one Perry chairs.

inaccurate_statement: Scott Perry has advocated for tougher approaches to violent crime, including the death penalty
description: Extensive searches find no evidence that Scott Perry has specifically advocated for the death penalty. His campaign platform (patriotsforperry.com) and House website list issues like economy, immigration, healthcare, Second Amendment, and pro-life positions, but no distinct crime or death-penalty plank. His legislative record includes some crime-related bills (e.g., protecting the Crime Victims Fund, penalizing union-related violence), which support a general 'tough on crime' characterization, but no bill, vote, quote, or statement tying him to death penalty advocacy could be found. Search results connecting 'Perry' and 'death penalty' almost exclusively refer to Rick Perry (former Texas governor), suggesting possible conflation. Since the death penalty component of this claim is a specific, checkable detail that isn't corroborated anywhere, it appears to be an unsupported addition to an otherwise plausible general characterization, making it a minor inaccuracy rather than one that undermines the broader 'tough on crime' framing.

inaccurate_statement: Stelson supports dedicating money and resources to law-enforcement officers so they can do their jobs safely, while also emphasizing constitutional limits on policing.
description: No source shows Stelson framing her public-safety position around dedicating resources to police alongside 'constitutional limits on policing.' Her documented platform, corroborated by a gun-violence-prevention organization's endorsement statement, centers on expanding background checks, red-flag laws, safe-storage incentives, removing ghost guns, and funding community violence-intervention programs — a restriction- and prevention-focused agenda, not one emphasizing resourcing police while constraining their power. This fabricated framing is used as the deciding factor in the response's bottom-line recommendation, so it would meaningfully mislead a reader about her actual position.

inaccurate_statement: Stelson's position isn't simply more restrictions—she emphasizes constitutional limits and accountability alongside supporting police funding, contrasted with Perry's more traditional pro-law-enforcement stance
description: No source shows Stelson framing her position with an emphasis on 'constitutional limits' on police power as a countervailing theme to funding law enforcement. Her documented public-safety-adjacent platform (via GIFFORDS) centers on expanding background checks, red flag laws, safe storage incentives, and removing firearms from domestic abusers — a gun-safety framework, not a 'constitutional limits on police' framework. This specific characterization of her position appears to be an invented nuance not found in her actual record.

inaccurate_statement: Stelson's campaign has criticized Perry for supporting a large data-center tax break and saying Pennsylvania 'can't afford to slow down' data-center construction
description: No documented campaign statement from Stelson specifically framing an attack around a 'data-center tax break' was found. Her confirmed, direct statement on data centers instead focuses on the local impact on neighborhoods and family homes/farms and a proposed federal role letting local governments block projects until concerns are addressed, not on a tax-break attack line against Perry.

inaccurate_statement: Perry voted for legislation providing a significant data-center tax incentive
description: No record in the available material shows Perry voting for or sponsoring a specific data-center tax incentive bill. His documented position on data centers is that he views the issue as a local zoning matter outside federal purview, and separately he has said the U.S. can't afford to slow the data-center build-out, but no specific tax-incentive legislation tied to him was found.

inaccurate_statement: Stelson's campaign has criticized Perry for supporting a major data-center tax break and for saying Pennsylvania 'can't afford to slow down' data-center construction
description: While a statement that the U.S. 'can't afford to slow down' data-center build-out due to competition with China is attributed to Perry in national commentary, there is no confirmed record of a specific 'data-center tax break' Perry supported, nor documentation that Stelson's campaign specifically criticized him on a tax break. This appears to be an extension or fabrication beyond what is documented.

inaccurate_statement: Perry's campaign has criticized Stelson's data-center position or criticized Shapiro's executive order specifically on data centers
description: No record exists of Perry's campaign issuing criticism of Shapiro specifically for 'changing course' on data centers. Perry's documented position on data centers is that zoning and regulation of data centers is a local-municipality matter outside his purview as a federal official ("I don't get into local zoning and building"), which is a stance of federal non-involvement, not active advocacy for data-center development or a documented attack on Shapiro's order.

inaccurate_statement: Perry has supported continued AI/data-center development and voted for a data-center tax break
description: There is no record of Perry voting for or sponsoring a specific data-center tax break. His only documented, confirmed statement on data centers is that he views data-center zoning and siting as strictly a local-municipality matter outside federal purview, not an endorsement of data-center construction or a specific tax break. Separately, a statement that the U.S. 'can't afford to slow down' data-center build-out due to competition with China was made in a broader national context, not tied to a specific tax-break vote. Presenting Perry as having 'voted for a data-center tax break' asserts a specific legislative action not supported by the available record and materially mischaracterizes his actual position, which is one of deference to local control rather than affirmative support for development.

inaccurate_statement: Stelson's campaign has explicitly supported Pennsylvania Gov. Josh Shapiro's August 2026 data-center restrictions
description: Stelson's documented position is that she supports a federal role allowing local governments to say no to data-center projects until resident concerns are addressed. There is no record of her explicitly endorsing a specific Shapiro executive order or restriction package from August 2026; the dossier notes only that Shapiro issued a related executive order around that time, without linking it to an explicit Stelson endorsement.

inaccurate_statement: Perry supported a large data-center tax break
description: No record exists of Perry supporting a specific data-center tax break. His documented position is that data-center zoning and regulation are local-municipality matters outside his purview as a federal representative, which is a neutral/hands-off stance rather than active support for tax incentives.

inaccurate_statement: Perry's campaign criticized Shapiro's new restrictions
description: No record exists of Perry or his campaign criticizing Governor Shapiro's data-center-related executive order or restrictions. His documented position is that he views data-center zoning as a local matter outside federal jurisdiction, not that he has attacked state-level restrictions.

inaccurate_statement: Perry's record is substantially more favorable toward data-center expansion
description: Perry's actual documented statement on data centers is that he views zoning and regulation of them as a local-municipality issue outside his purview as "a federal guy," a neutral/hands-off position rather than an affirmatively pro-expansion stance. Characterizing his record as "substantially more favorable toward data-center expansion" overstates and mischaracterizes this documented neutrality.

inaccurate_statement: The 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act passed the House 358–32, with Perry voting against it in June
description: The bill actually passed the House 396-13 on May 20, 2026, not 358-32 in June 2026. The core fact that Perry voted against this bipartisan housing bill and was the only Pennsylvania representative to do so is accurate, but the specific vote count and month are wrong.

inaccurate_statement: Perry voted for the Keeping Violent Offenders Off Our Streets Act in May 2026.
description: The claim describes a vote occurring in May 2026, which is a future date relative to the current timeframe. A congressional vote cannot have already occurred in the future, so this specific claim describing a completed vote by Perry in May 2026 is fabricated or at minimum temporally impossible to have happened as stated. There is no legitimate way to verify a past-tense vote for an event that has not yet occurred, and the claim as framed (asserting a completed action) misrepresents the timeline.

inaccurate_statement: Stelson proposes increasing the minimum wage
description: Stelson has called Pennsylvania's $7.25 minimum wage 'outrageous' and noted it is lower than neighboring states, which implies support for raising it, but no confirmed direct statement in the available record shows her specifically proposing a minimum-wage increase as a named policy plank — her platform instead emphasizes vocational training and jobs that pay 'family-supporting wages.' This is a plausible but not directly confirmed characterization of her position.

inaccurate_statement: Perry voted against the bipartisan housing-affordability bill 'in June'
description: The House passed the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act (the bipartisan housing-affordability bill Perry voted against) on May 20, 2026, not in June. This is a minor date error that does not change the substance of the claim that Perry opposed the bill.

inaccurate_statement: Perry has previously supported federal abortion restrictions, including a national ban.
description: Perry's record on abortion is genuinely conflicted rather than a simple 'national ban' position: his campaign materials state he supports exceptions for rape, incest, and life of the mother, and he supports IVF (having co-introduced the IVF Protection Act). Separately, he is a current cosponsor of the Life at Conception Act, which lacks those exceptions and has led critics to characterize his position as supporting a ban with no exceptions. Presenting only the 'national ban' side without noting his stated exceptions-supportive position and IVF advocacy gives an incomplete picture of his actual record.

inaccurate_statement: Perry supports significant federal restrictions on abortion, while Stelson supports federal protections for abortion access
description: This presents only one side of Perry's abortion record. His stated personal position includes exceptions for rape, incest, and life of the mother, and he supports IVF access and co-introduced the IVF Protection Act. His cosponsorship of the Life at Conception Act (which lacks such exceptions) is a genuine, documented conflict with his stated personal position, not a straightforward 'supports significant federal restrictions' characterization. The response oversimplifies a record that has two conflicting, well-documented sides.

inaccurate_statement: Stelson supports adequately funding law enforcement, while emphasizing constitutional accountability
description: No source shows Stelson framing her public-safety position around emphasizing constitutional limits on police power or accountability in this way. Her documented platform centers explicitly on expanding gun restrictions (background checks, red flag laws, safe storage, ghost gun crackdowns, community violence intervention) rather than a 'constitutional accountability' counterbalance to law enforcement funding, so this specific framing appears invented rather than drawn from her actual record.

inaccurate_statement: I found considerably less detail from her campaign about how she would fund or prioritize roads and bridges
description: Stelson has a documented, specific transportation position calling for investment in roads, bridges, public transportation and the electric grid, has specifically highlighted the I-83 South Bridge project, and has directly attacked Perry for voting against the infrastructure law that funded it. Characterizing her position as lacking meaningful detail compared to Perry's contradicts this record and undermines the central premise of the response.

inaccurate_statement: Perry has the stronger demonstrated commitment and specific record on roads and bridges, and 'says he supports federal surface-transportation funding and coordination with state and local governments'
description: This framing omits that Perry voted against the 2021 bipartisan Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act, which is the very law that funded the I-83 South Bridge replacement he is credited with championing. Presenting his record as simply strong on roads/bridges without this well-documented vote gives an incomplete and misleadingly favorable picture of his legislative record on the topic.

inaccurate_statement: PA-10 has a National Low Income Housing Coalition-estimated shortage of 14,701 affordable rental units for extremely low-income renters, with a two-bedroom fair-market rent of about $1,377/month
description: The NLIHC's official PA-10 Congressional District Profile confirms the shortage figure of 14,701 affordable rental units for extremely low-income renters exactly as claimed. However, the two-bedroom Fair Market Rent figure in the same official NLIHC profile is listed as $1,466, not $1,377 as stated in the claim (a discrepancy of about $89/month, roughly 6%). This may reflect an earlier data vintage since NLIHC updates FMR figures annually, but based on current official data the FMR figure cited is incorrect. Since the core statistic (the 14,701 unit shortage) is accurate and only the secondary rent figure is off, this is a narrow, minor error rather than one that undermines the overall claim.

inaccurate_statement: Stelson advocates an 'all-of-the-above' energy policy, including wind and solar, to reduce energy costs over time.
description: The 'all-of-the-above' energy strategy label is specifically Scott Perry's stated platform branding, not Stelson's. Stelson's documented position emphasizes expanding clean energy and diversifying energy sources to reduce costs, but she has not been described as running on an 'all-of-the-above' approach — that phrase describes Perry's approach, which actually leans on continued oil/gas/hydropower development. The underlying idea that Stelson favors diversifying energy sources including renewables is roughly accurate, but attaching Perry's specific policy label to her is a mischaracterization.

inaccurate_statement: In an August 2026 town hall, Perry acknowledged the high gas prices but predicted they would 'rapidly drop.'
description: The claim references an August 2026 town hall, which is a future date that has not yet occurred. There can be no genuine record of Scott Perry making this statement at an event that hasn't happened. This appears to be a fabricated claim with an impossible timestamp, meaning the specific quote and event cannot be real or verifiable.

inaccurate_statement: Janelle Stelson favors an 'all-of-the-above' energy strategy including renewables
description: The specific 'all-of-the-above' energy-strategy framing is documented as Scott Perry's stated approach, not Stelson's. Stelson's documented energy positions emphasize expanding clean/renewable energy investment and opposing abandonment of Pennsylvania's energy sector, but no source attributes the specific 'all-of-the-above' phrase or framing to her; attributing Perry's specific policy label to Stelson misrepresents her actual stated approach.

inaccurate_statement: In 2020, Perry backed the bipartisan Lower Costs, More Cures Act.
description: The Lower Costs, More Cures Act (H.R. 19) did include provisions like a $50/month insulin cap and drug-pricing transparency measures that Perry supported, but characterizing it as 'bipartisan' is misleading. The bill attracted only Republican cosponsors and was frequently mislabeled 'bipartisan' in GOP press releases despite having no Democratic support and never receiving a standalone floor vote.

inaccurate_statement: There's evidence that federal investments associated with Perry have produced employment in the district's wood-products sector
description: No record exists of any federal investment tied to Perry producing employment in a wood-products sector in PA-10. This specific claim does not appear in Perry's documented record, which covers manufacturing (notably the Cleveland-Cliffs steel mill intervention), infrastructure (I-83 South Bridge), and general deregulation positions, but nothing about a wood-products sector. This is a narrow, peripheral detail that doesn't change the overall comparative picture presented.

inaccurate_statement: Perry's committee has direct jurisdiction over flood-damage reduction, disaster preparedness, water infrastructure and Army Corps of Engineers activities
description: Perry's Economic Development, Public Buildings & Emergency Management subcommittee has jurisdiction over disaster preparedness, mitigation, response and recovery and FEMA/DHS emergency-management matters, but flood-damage reduction and U.S. Army Corps of Engineers civil-works activities actually fall under the separate Water Resources and Environment subcommittee, not his subcommittee.

inaccurate_statement: He was endorsed by the NFIB in the 2024 election, which is meaningful evidence that at least one major small-business advocacy organization viewed him as the stronger small-business candidate at that time.
description: NFIB's logo appears on Perry's current campaign endorsements page as of a 2026 re-check, but there is no confirmation that this endorsement specifically dates to or was announced in the 2024 election cycle as the response claims; the timing attribution to '2024' is unsupported and could be inaccurate.

inaccurate_statement: Perry has supported data center tax incentives and backed a data center tax break
description: No record exists of Perry supporting or backing any specific data-center tax break or incentive. His documented position on data centers is that zoning and regulation of such projects are local/municipal matters outside his purview as "a federal guy," not an affirmative advocacy for tax incentives for the industry.

inaccurate_statement: Perry has generally taken a more pro-development position, arguing that Pennsylvania should compete in AI and data center growth, and supported continued data center development
description: Perry's documented statement on data centers describes zoning and siting decisions as local matters outside federal jurisdiction, not an affirmative pro-development advocacy position specific to Pennsylvania competing in AI growth. While a broader national comment attributed to him supports not slowing data-center build-out generally, characterizing his PA-10-specific position as actively pro-development conflates a hands-off/deferential stance with an advocacy stance.

inaccurate_statement: Perry has not held a town hall since 2019
description: Scott Perry has not held an in-person, open town hall since July 30, 2019, but he does hold regular telephone town halls on topics like tariffs, the reconciliation bill, and other issues, including ones scheduled in 2026. Stating flatly that he 'has not held a town hall since 2019' without specifying 'in-person' omits this distinction and could leave the impression he has held no town halls of any format, which is inaccurate — his documented pattern is specifically an avoidance of open, in-person formats rather than of constituent contact altogether.

inaccurate_statement: The DCCC currently lists PA-10 as a Democratic pickup opportunity and Stelson as its candidate
description: The DCCC's confirmed involvement is naming Stelson to its 'Red to Blue' program (Feb. 23, 2026), not a generic 'pickup opportunity' listing; this is a minor mischaracterization of the specific DCCC program rather than a substantive error about her candidacy or party backing.

inaccurate_statement: Janelle Stelson is 'the clearest answer' to which candidate takes corporate PAC money, implying Perry does not
description: This framing is misleading and reverses the more supported conclusion. Perry's PAC/other-committee contributions ($650,127, ~12.5% of his total receipts) are larger in both dollar amount and share of total fundraising than Stelson's ($488,706, ~8% of her total receipts). Perry's documented backers include institutional PACs such as Club for Growth PAC, and he has accepted over $935,000 in corporate PAC money over his career according to End Citizens United. Presenting Stelson as 'the clearest answer' while citing Perry's larger PAC figure in the same response, without noting Perry also takes substantial PAC/corporate money, creates a misleading overall conclusion that inverts which candidate is more reliant on such funding.

inaccurate_statement: Democratic Jewish Outreach Pennsylvania has endorsed Janelle Stelson
description: Democratic Jewish Outreach Pennsylvania (DJOP), a Pennsylvania-specific group, had not formally endorsed Stelson as of research; the organization that actually issued a public endorsement was the Jewish Democratic Council of America (JDCA), a separate national group. This appears to be a mix-up between two similarly named but distinct Jewish Democratic organizations.

inaccurate_statement: Barbara Comstock is a current Republican supporter/endorser of Janelle Stelson
description: Comstock's endorsement of Stelson dates to the 2024 election cycle, as part of a joint letter from several former House Republicans backing Stelson against Perry that year. Presenting it without noting this origin misleadingly implies it is a current 2026-cycle endorsement.

inaccurate_statement: UFCW Local 1776 has endorsed Janelle Stelson
description: This specific union appears to have been drawn from an endorsement roster that actually belongs to a different Pennsylvania candidate (Sharif Street, in the PA-3 race), not Stelson's PA-10 campaign. No independent confirmation of a UFCW Local 1776 endorsement of Stelson was found.

inaccurate_statement: Barbara Comstock is listed as a current endorser of Stelson without noting her endorsement dates back to the 2024 election cycle.
description: Barbara Comstock's endorsement of Stelson originated in October 2024, as part of a group of former House Republicans backing her against Perry in that cycle. Presenting it without noting this timing implies it is a fresh 2026 endorsement, which current endorsement trackers do not separately confirm.

inaccurate_statement: Barbara Comstock, Denver Riggleman, and Gabby Giffords are grouped and labeled as 'U.S. Reps.' endorsing Stelson.
description: None of these three currently serve in Congress. Comstock and Riggleman are former Republican U.S. Representatives (from Virginia), and Gabby Giffords is a former Democratic U.S. Representative from Arizona who resigned in 2012. Labeling them collectively as sitting 'U.S. Reps.' misrepresents their current status, though the underlying fact that some of them have voiced support for Stelson is not itself disputed.

inaccurate_statement: UFCW Local 1776 has endorsed Stelson.
description: This union appears to belong to another Pennsylvania candidate's (Sharif Street, PA-3) endorsement roster rather than Stelson's; no source confirms UFCW Local 1776 specifically endorsing Stelson in PA-10.

inaccurate_statement: Stelson's largest reported PAC donor so far is Democracy Engine, Inc. PAC, at about $18,700
description: No record of a PAC named 'Democracy Engine, Inc. PAC' giving $18,700 to Stelson's campaign exists in available fundraising documentation, and a direct contribution of that size from a multicandidate PAC to a single candidate committee would exceed federal contribution limits (a maximum of $5,000 per election, or $10,000 combined for a primary and general election cycle). This mirrors a previously identified pattern of a fabricated PAC contribution figure exceeding legal limits, and this specific claim is not verifiable in the available finance records.

inaccurate_statement: Perry's largest listed PAC donor is Club for Growth PAC, at about $50,900
description: Club for Growth PAC is a real, confirmed 2026-cycle backer of Perry, but a direct contribution of $50,900 from a multicandidate PAC to a single candidate's committee would exceed federal contribution limits (capped at $5,000 per election, or $10,000 for a full primary-and-general cycle). No documented figure in available finance records supports this specific dollar amount, and a strikingly similar fabricated Club for Growth contribution figure for Perry has been identified as inaccurate in past research for the same reason.

inaccurate_statement: Of Stelson's itemized individual contributions with an address available, about $1.30M came from Pennsylvania and $2.54M from elsewhere, roughly 34% in-state vs 66% out-of-state
description: No breakdown of Stelson's individual contributions by in-state versus out-of-state donors appears anywhere in the available financial records; her disclosed totals only break contributions down by source type (individuals, PACs, transfers, party committees), not by donor geography. This specific geographic split appears to be an invented statistic not grounded in any documented FEC data.

inaccurate_statement: Stelson's largest direct political-committee contributors include Democracy Engine PAC ($18,719), EMILY's List ($11,662), Zinc Collective PAC ($10,500), and several labor PACs at about $10,000 each
description: While EMILY's List is a confirmed real endorser/supporter of Stelson, no source documents these specific dollar figures for individual PAC contributions to her campaign, and entities like 'Democracy Engine PAC' and 'Zinc Collective PAC' with these exact amounts are not corroborated by any available record. This appears to be fabricated financial detail, though it is a narrow point that doesn't change the overall picture of her fundraising.

inaccurate_statement: Perry's largest reported PAC contributor is Club for Growth PAC, at about $50,900
description: Club for Growth PAC is confirmed as one of Perry's real institutional backers, but federal contribution limits cap what a multicandidate PAC can give directly to a single candidate's committee per cycle (generally $10,000 for primary plus general), making a $50,900 direct contribution implausible and unsupported by any documented FEC figure. This specific dollar amount appears to be fabricated, though it doesn't change the broader accurate picture that Club for Growth PAC backs Perry.

inaccurate_statement: Perry's other receipts were about $10.7K
description: The documented FEC breakdown for Perry's committee does not include an itemized 'other receipts' figure of $10.7K; the confirmed breakdown accounts for contributions, transfers, and party committee funds without this additional category being specified in available records.

inaccurate_statement: Stelson is more skeptical of using U.S. military power and spending abroad
description: Available reporting indicates the opposite: Stelson has taken hawkish positions, including supporting Israel's military campaign against Hamas and supporting continued U.S. aid to Ukraine against Russian aggression, with even critical commentary describing her Ukraine stance as 'reckless and hawkish.' Perry, by contrast, has been part of the more skeptical/isolationist wing of the GOP on unconditional foreign aid. This reverses the actual contrast between the two candidates on foreign policy.

inaccurate_statement: Perry has sponsored legislation to restrict/ban abortion nationally
description: Perry is a cosponsor, not the sponsor, of the Life at Conception Act (H.R. 722, 119th Congress); he did not personally sponsor this legislation. The response also omits that Perry's stated personal position includes rape/incest/life-of-mother exceptions and support for IVF, presenting only the more restrictive side of what is a documented, genuinely conflicting record.

inaccurate_statement: Perry voted for the Respect for Marriage Act.
description: Scott Perry voted against the Respect for Marriage Act. When the House passed H.R. 8404 in July 2022, only 47 House Republicans joined Democrats in voting yes; Perry, a member of the conservative Freedom Caucus representing PA-10, was not among them and voted no. The claim that he voted for the bill misstates his voting record on a specific, well-documented roll call vote, which is a significant error given how central this vote is to his record on LGBTQ-related legislation.

inaccurate_statement: Perry has sponsored a 20-week abortion ban and supported broader restrictions, although he has said abortion policy should largely be left to states
description: There is no record of Perry sponsoring a 20-week abortion ban or saying abortion policy should largely be left to states. His documented position is a stated personal stance supporting exceptions for rape, incest, and life of the mother, combined with IVF support and co-introduction of the IVF Protection Act, in direct tension with his confirmed current cosponsorship of the Life at Conception Act (H.R. 722), which contains no such exceptions and defines personhood from the moment of fertilization. Neither a 20-week ban sponsorship nor a states'-rights framing appears in his documented record, making this a fabricated characterization of a genuinely conflicting and more complex actual position.

inaccurate_statement: Stelson is described as a 'first-time candidate for Congress'
description: This is inaccurate given that the response itself acknowledges the race is a rematch — Stelson previously ran for this same House seat in 2024 and narrowly lost to Perry. She is a repeat candidate for this office, not a first-time candidate, even though she has never held elected office prior to running.

inaccurate_statement: A federal judge ordered him to turn over more than 1,600 texts and emails that weren't protected by congressional privileges
description: The documented figure is that a D.C. Circuit ruling permitted investigator access to 1,659 of Perry's contested phone messages by December 2023, out of roughly 2,219 documents originally seized and disputed under the Speech or Debate Clause. Describing this as a single federal judge's order covering 'more than 1,600 texts and emails' is a reasonably close approximation of the confirmed 1,659 figure, but simplifies an appellate court process and slightly mischaracterizes the procedural history; this is a narrow detail that doesn't change the overall picture of the investigation.

inaccurate_statement: She has supported legalization/amnesty for some undocumented immigrants, so her position is not simply "deport everyone"
description: There is no documented statement of Stelson supporting legalization or amnesty for undocumented immigrants. Her actual platform explicitly focuses on opposing "open borders," prioritizing deportation of those who have committed violent crimes, and securing the border with technology and funding. The available record shows no amnesty/legalization position, and this claim appears to be an unsupported addition to her documented stance, though it does not fundamentally overturn the accurate overall framing that she opposes open borders.

inaccurate_statement: Stelson was reportedly a registered Republican for many years before switching parties during the Trump era
description: Stelson was a registered Republican until February 2023, when she switched to the Democratic Party, citing the 2022 Dobbs decision — this switch occurred during Joe Biden's presidency, not during Donald Trump's time in office, and was tied to a specific Supreme Court ruling rather than a general Trump-era political shift.

inaccurate_statement: Stelson began reporting in Pennsylvania in the 1980s
description: The knowledge base states her broadcast journalism career spanned nearly 40 years, with 26 years (1997–2023) specifically at WGAL-TV. It does not confirm she began reporting in Pennsylvania specifically in the 1980s; her career included stops at WPLG-TV Miami and other outlets as well, and the WGAL tenure is dated 1997–2023, which would place her start there in the 1990s, not matching a claim that Pennsylvania reporting began in the 1980s.

inaccurate_statement: She says a new five-year Farm Bill would be a top priority
description: Stelson's platform calls for a new Farm Bill aimed at lowering farmers' input costs and providing greater certainty, but no source specifies a five-year term for this proposal. The specific 'five-year' detail appears to be an invented specific not found in her documented platform.

inaccurate_statement: She has argued that ICE should be held accountable for deaths of U.S. citizens
description: Stelson's documented position calls for independent and thorough investigations into every killing involving ICE agents generally, and that ICE agents should be identifiable (wear uniforms/badges, no masks), not specifically framed around deaths of U.S. citizens as the claim states.

inaccurate_statement: She supports an "all-of-the-above" energy approach that includes wind and solar, arguing renewable energy can help lower costs
description: Stelson's documented energy positions emphasize expanding clean-energy investment and renewable energy generally, along with an earlier (2024-cycle) statement supporting restarting Three Mile Island nuclear plant. "All-of-the-above" is actually the term used to describe opponent Scott Perry's energy platform (which explicitly includes continued oil/gas development alongside renewables); attributing this specific framing to Stelson without support is not confirmed by her documented platform, which does not use this term.

inaccurate_statement: Perry served nearly 40 years in the Pennsylvania Army National Guard
description: Perry served in the Pennsylvania Army National Guard from 1980 to 2019, which is 39 years — close to but not quite "nearly 40 years" in a way that could be seen as accurate rounding; however, the more precisely documented span is 1980–2019, which rounds to 39 years, not requiring correction, so this is essentially accurate. No error found upon review.

inaccurate_statement: Perry's platform includes supporting clean-energy technologies alongside expanded natural gas and nuclear production.
description: Perry's documented record shows opposition to clean-energy subsidies, including sponsoring legislation to eliminate subsidies for renewable energy, EVs, and ethanol, and eliminating the Renewable Fuel Standard. His energy platform is centered on conventional (oil, gas, hydropower, nuclear) production rather than active support for clean-energy technologies, making this characterization misleading.

inaccurate_statement: Perry wants to preserve and protect Social Security and Medicare for seniors rather than fundamentally restructuring them.
description: Perry has historically supported raising the Social Security retirement age and reducing benefits, and has argued spending cuts are needed to address long-term federal finances — positions that involve structural changes to the programs, not simply preservation without restructuring.

inaccurate_statement: Perry's platform on abortion is presented only as supporting exceptions for rape, incest, and life of the mother, without noting his cosponsorship of legislation with no such exceptions.
description: Perry's stated personal position includes exceptions for rape, incest, and life of the mother, and he supports IVF. However, he is also a current cosponsor of the Life at Conception Act, which contains no such exceptions and defines personhood from the moment of fertilization, a provision reported to put IVF at legal risk. Presenting only the exceptions-supportive framing omits this documented conflict in his record.

inaccurate_statement: Perry's abortion position is presented only as pro-life with rape/incest/life-of-mother exceptions, without noting his cosponsorship of the Life at Conception Act, which contains no such exceptions
description: Perry's campaign materials do state he supports exceptions for rape, incest, and life of the mother, and he has said he supports IVF and co-introduced the IVF Protection Act. However, he is also a current cosponsor of the Life at Conception Act (H.R. 722), which contains no such exceptions and defines personhood from the moment of fertilization, in direct tension with his stated personal position. Presenting only the exceptions-supportive framing as his complete position omits this documented conflict and gives an incomplete picture of his actual legislative record on abortion.

inaccurate_statement: Perry has opposed a federal abortion ban while saying abortion policy should largely be left to the states
description: This mischaracterizes Perry's actual, documented record. Perry is a current cosponsor of the federal Life at Conception Act (H.R. 722, 119th Congress), which would establish a constitutional right to life for every human being from 'the moment of fertilization' with no exceptions for rape, incest, or life of the mother — a national personhood framework that multiple outlets have described as effectively a national abortion ban, in direct tension with any claim that he opposes a federal ban or favors leaving abortion policy to the states. His own campaign materials state he supports exceptions for rape, incest, and danger to the mother's life, but nothing in his record supports a 'leave it to the states' federalism position, and his cosponsorship of a federal personhood bill is the opposite of opposing a federal ban.

inaccurate_statement: He voted for the Stop Insider Trading Act in 2026
description: The claim references a vote occurring in 2026, a future date for which no congressional voting record can yet exist. There is no 'Stop Insider Trading Act' vote from 2026 that Scott Perry could have participated in, as this timeframe has not occurred. This appears to be a fabricated or erroneously dated claim — either the bill/vote does not exist as described, or the date is incorrect and cannot be verified as stated. Without being able to confirm any real underlying vote (e.g., a similarly named bill in an earlier Congress) explicitly attributed to Perry, and given the claim explicitly cites a not-yet-occurred year, this should be treated as inaccurate/fabricated as presented.

inaccurate_statement: Perry is strongly pro-life and has supported federal restrictions on abortion, including a 20-week ban and restrictions on federal funding for abortion
description: This presents only one side of Perry's abortion record. While his campaign materials describe a pro-life position with exceptions for rape, incest, and life of the mother, he is also a current cosponsor of the Life at Conception Act, which defines personhood from the moment of fertilization and contains no such exceptions, in direct tension with his stated personal position. Presenting only the exceptions-based framing omits this documented conflict in his actual legislative record.

inaccurate_statement: Stelson criticized Perry for promoting the debunked claim that Italian satellites manipulated the 2020 election
description: No record exists of Stelson making this specific criticism, nor of Perry promoting an 'Italian satellites' conspiracy theory (sometimes called 'Italygate'), in either candidate's documented record. The extensive, well-sourced account of the January 6/2020 election controversy involving Perry covers the FBI phone seizure, the Jeffrey Clark matter, and the pardon dispute, but contains no mention of this satellite claim, suggesting this detail is fabricated or conflated from an unrelated source.

inaccurate_statement: Perry responded to the FBI phone-seizure allegation by saying he was 'not under investigation' and calling the claim a falsehood propagated by his political opponents and the media.
description: The claim conflates two distinct things. Perry did state, through himself and his attorney, that he was "not a target" of the FBI investigation (close in substance to "not under investigation") — e.g., his attorney said “the Justice Department had informed us that Representative Perry is not a target of its investigation." However, Perry never called the phone-seizure allegation itself a "falsehood" — he personally announced and confirmed the seizure occurred ("three FBI agents visited me and seized my cell phone"), and he framed the episode as politically motivated overreach by Garland's DOJ/FBI ("banana republic tactics"), not as a false claim propagated by "political opponents and the media." So the underlying fact (Perry disputing being a target) is real, but the claim misleadingly recasts what he denied and who he blamed, making it a minor mischaracterization rather than a fabrication of the entire episode.

inaccurate_statement: In 2025, Perry's campaign said Stelson supported raising taxes on 'hardworking south-central Pennsylvanians by more than $2,000.'
description: The documented version of this claim comes from Perry's comparison statement issued after Stelson won her May 2026 primary, not from 2025 — he said her preferred tax policy 'would have... raised [taxes] by more than $2,000 on Pennsylvanians.' The substance of the attack is accurate, but the date attributed to it is wrong.

inaccurate_statement: PennDOT is already planning major roadway work in Luzerne County, including the Kidder/Mundy Street project, while the Wyoming Valley Flood Protection Authority is addressing erosion threatening the levee
description: Luzerne County and the Wyoming Valley are not part of Pennsylvania's 10th Congressional District, which covers the Harrisburg-area counties of Dauphin, Cumberland, and York. This appears to be a mix-up with a different Pennsylvania district's infrastructure projects, making the specific example irrelevant to the district actually being discussed, though it doesn't change the core accurate conclusion that Stelson hasn't laid out a project-specific roads/flood plan.

inaccurate_statement: Perry's energy agenda includes repealing CAFE standards and opposing regulations he describes as increasing vehicle and energy costs
description: No record exists in the available material of Perry specifically advocating repeal of CAFE (Corporate Average Fuel Economy) standards as part of his energy platform. His documented energy positions focus on an 'all-of-the-above' strategy, repealing the Renewable Fuel Standard, and general deregulation rhetoric (the '$15,000/family' regulatory-cost figure), but no source ties him specifically to CAFE standards repeal. This is a narrow, specific policy claim not attributable to any documented statement.

inaccurate_statement: Perry recently said that gasoline prices would 'rapidly drop,' attributing much of the current spike to the Iran conflict
description: Perry's documented statement on this topic says he wants gas prices to come down and that resolution of the Iran conflict would help prices 'return to pre-war levels' -- there is no record of him using the specific phrase 'rapidly drop.' This is a narrow wording embellishment on an otherwise accurately-characterized position, not a substantive mischaracterization of his overall stance.

inaccurate_statement: Describing the Lower Costs, More Cures Act (H.R. 19) as 'bipartisan'
description: The Lower Costs, More Cures Act (H.R. 19) was a Republican-only bill with 145 cosponsors, all Republicans; Republican offices branded it 'bipartisan' in press releases, but it did not have cross-party cosponsorship or support and never received a standalone floor vote. The specific policy provisions cited (insulin cap, out-of-pocket cap, transparency measures) are accurate, but calling the bill itself bipartisan is a mischaracterization.

inaccurate_statement: Perry has specifically promoted a "One Federal Decision" approach so major transportation projects can move through federal agencies more quickly
description: No record exists of Scott Perry specifically promoting a "One Federal Decision" permitting approach. His documented position on speeding up infrastructure approvals is limited to general criticism of environmental-review delays and praise for the Trump administration's NEPA/permitting streamlining plan (which was not his own proposal), not a specific named "One Federal Decision" initiative attributed to him.

inaccurate_statement: As chairman of the House subcommittee dealing with emergency management, Perry has pushed for a more streamlined FEMA response, and his 2025 congressional testimony criticized overlapping federal requirements that can delay disaster assistance
description: Perry chairs the Transportation and Infrastructure Subcommittee on Economic Development, Public Buildings and Emergency Management, so the chairmanship claim itself is accurate, but no record exists of specific 2025 congressional testimony by Perry criticizing overlapping federal disaster-assistance requirements. This specific testimony claim is unverified and does not correspond to any documented statement.

inaccurate_statement: Perry's committee (Transportation and Infrastructure) jurisdiction includes flood-damage reduction and the Army Corps of Engineers
description: Perry chairs the Economic Development, Public Buildings and Emergency Management subcommittee, whose jurisdiction covers disaster preparedness, mitigation, response and recovery under the Stafford Act and FEMA-related matters — not flood-damage reduction or Army Corps of Engineers civil works, which fall under the separate Water Resources and Environment subcommittee. The response conflates these two subcommittees' jurisdictions.

inaccurate_statement: She came within roughly 5,200 votes of defeating incumbent Scott Perry, making the race one of the closest House contests in the country
description: The 2024 margin between Stelson and Perry was approximately 5,000–5,133 votes per available sourcing (Ballotpedia and Wikipedia), not 5,200 — a small numerical discrepancy that doesn't change the overall characterization of the race as extremely close.

inaccurate_statement: Perry has said abortion policy should largely be left to the states.
description: Perry's documented record on abortion is a genuine conflict, not a simple 'leave it to the states' position: he is a current cosponsor of the federal Life at Conception Act, which would establish a nationwide, constitutional definition of personhood beginning 'at the moment of fertilization,' with no rape/incest/life-of-the-mother exceptions. This federal personhood approach is in tension with a 'leave it to the states' framing, and the response presents only the more moderate side of his position (personal pro-life view with exceptions, support for IVF) without noting this conflicting federal cosponsorship record.

inaccurate_statement: Perry served nearly four decades in the Pennsylvania Army National Guard
description: Perry served in the Pennsylvania Army National Guard from 1980 to 2019, which is 39 years — close to but not quite "nearly four decades" is actually accurate as a round figure; however, the retirement year is confirmed as 2019, matching the response, so this statement is accurate rather than inaccurate.

inaccurate_statement: He served nearly 40 years in the Pennsylvania Army National Guard
description: Perry's National Guard service ran from 1980 to 2019, which is 39 years — close to but not quite "nearly 40 years" is roughly accurate; however, this is a very minor point and arguably within rounding tolerance.

inaccurate_statement: Perry served nearly 40 years in the Pennsylvania Army National Guard
description: Perry's National Guard service ran from 1980 to 2019, which is 39 years — 'nearly 40 years' is essentially accurate and within reasonable rounding, so this is not a substantive inaccuracy, but flagged for note since the dossier specifies 1980–2019 rather than an open-ended 'nearly 40 years' framing.

inaccurate_statement: Perry co-founded Hydrotech Mechanical Services, a mechanical contracting company
description: Available background confirms Perry co-founded a mechanical contracting business, but no record specifies the company name as 'Hydrotech Mechanical Services' — this specific name is not verifiable against the documented biography, which only describes the venture generically as a mechanical contracting business.

inaccurate_statement: Perry represented parts of Cumberland and York Counties in the Pennsylvania House of Representatives
description: Perry represented Pennsylvania House District 92, which was based in York County; no record confirms Cumberland County was part of that state house district specifically.

inaccurate_statement: Perry served nearly 40 years in the Pennsylvania Army National Guard
description: Perry served in the Pennsylvania Army National Guard from 1980 to 2019, which is approximately 39 years — close to but not quite "nearly 40 years" in a way that could be considered a rounding overstatement, though this is a very minor discrepancy and arguably within reasonable rounding.

inaccurate_statement: In 2020, Perry backed the bipartisan Lower Costs, More Cures Act, which proposed a Medicare annual out-of-pocket limit and an insulin cost ceiling
description: Perry did back this legislation (H.R. 19, the Lower Costs, More Cures Act, primarily associated with 2019) and it did include an insulin cost cap and an out-of-pocket limit, but describing it as 'bipartisan' is misleading. The bill attracted only Republican cosponsors, and while GOP offices branded it 'bipartisan' in press materials, it did not have genuine cross-party cosponsorship and never received a standalone floor vote. The core substantive point about Perry's support for these specific provisions is accurate, but the bipartisan characterization is not.

inaccurate_statement: His phone was seized by the FBI in 2022 as part of the federal investigation into efforts involving fake electors
description: The 2022 FBI phone seizure was part of the broader January 6 investigation focused on Perry's role introducing Jeffrey Clark to Trump in an effort to install Clark as acting Attorney General to pursue election-fraud claims, not specifically the fake-electors scheme. This is a narrow mischaracterization of which strand of the January 6 investigation his phone seizure related to, not a fabrication of the underlying seizure itself.

inaccurate_statement: Stelson advocates for investments in renewable energy sources like wind and solar to lower costs and supports tightening environmental regulations
description: No direct statement was found of Stelson specifically naming wind and solar or proposing to tighten environmental regulations; her documented position emphasizes general support for expanding clean-energy investment and diversifying energy sources to lower costs, without the specific 'tightening environmental regulations' framing or naming wind/solar specifically. This presents a more specific policy mechanism than what is actually confirmed on the record.

inaccurate_statement: Stelson advocates for an all-of-the-above energy strategy incorporating renewable sources like wind and solar to lower costs and address climate change
description: The 'all-of-the-above' energy strategy label is Scott Perry's stated platform framing (an all-of-the-above approach including hydropower and continued oil/gas development), not Stelson's. Stelson's platform emphasizes expanding clean-energy investment and lowering costs, but she is not documented as branding her approach 'all-of-the-above.'

inaccurate_statement: Scott Perry generally favors leaving abortion regulations up to individual states
description: Perry's documented record does not show him favoring a states'-rights approach to abortion. He is a current cosponsor of the federal Life at Conception Act, which would establish a nationwide constitutional right to life from the moment of fertilization — a federal personhood law, not a policy of deferring abortion regulation to individual states. His campaign site also states a personal position with rape/incest/life-of-mother exceptions, again a personal stance rather than a 'leave it to the states' framework. This characterization mischaracterizes his actual legislative position.

inaccurate_statement: Perry supports leaving abortion regulations primarily to state legislatures
description: Perry's record on abortion is a federal-level cosponsorship matter, not a states'-rights framing. He currently cosponsors the federal Life at Conception Act (H.R. 722), which would establish a federal constitutional right to life from the moment of fertilization with no exceptions for rape, incest, or life of the mother — a national personhood standard, not a position of deferring the issue to individual states. His campaign site separately states a personal position supportive of rape/incest/life exceptions and IVF access. Describing his position as 'leaving abortion regulations primarily to state legislatures' omits this documented federal cosponsorship record and presents only a partial, more moderate-sounding characterization of a genuinely conflicting record.

inaccurate_statement: Perry maintains a pro-life stance, emphasizing the protection of the unborn while supporting exceptions and leaving specific regulations largely up to individual states
description: This presents only one side of Perry's genuinely conflicting record on abortion. While his campaign site does state he supports exceptions for rape, incest, and life of the mother, he is also a current cosponsor of the Life at Conception Act, which contains no such exceptions and defines personhood from the moment of fertilization — a position that conflicts with 'leaving specific regulations largely up to individual states' framing and with his stated exceptions. Presenting only the exceptions-supportive framing without noting this contradiction is a one-sided characterization of a documented conflict, not a fabrication of either individual fact.

inaccurate_statement: Perry maintains a pro-life position, supporting state-level decision-making on abortion.
description: There is no documented statement from Perry framing his abortion position around leaving the issue to states. His actual legislative record shows he currently cosponsors the federal Life at Conception Act, which would establish a national, federal personhood standard from the moment of fertilization with no rape/incest/life-of-mother exceptions — the opposite of a 'leave it to the states' approach. His stated personal position (with rape/incest/life exceptions) also doesn't mention states' rights specifically. Describing his position as 'state-level decision-making' mischaracterizes his documented federal legislative record, though the broader characterization of him as pro-life is accurate.

inaccurate_statement: Perry maintains a personal pro-life stance, has previously supported restrictions, and favors leaving the issue primarily to the states.
description: Perry's actual record on this issue is more complicated than 'leaving it to the states' suggests: he is a current cosponsor of the federal Life at Conception Act, which would establish a constitutional right to life from the moment of fertilization nationwide, with no rape/incest/life-of-mother exceptions — a federal personhood measure, not a states'-rights position. His separate, stated personal position does include rape/incest/life exceptions and IVF support, but the response's characterization omits this federal cosponsorship and the conflict it creates, oversimplifying his actual position.

inaccurate_statement: Perry promoted alternative plans including the 'fake electors' scheme
description: The documented record centers on Perry's role in the Jeffrey Clark scheme, contacts with Mark Meadows, and his January 6 certification vote. No source in the available material ties Perry specifically to promoting a 'fake electors' scheme (a separate effort involving alternate slates of electors in swing states) as opposed to the Jeffrey Clark/DOJ pressure campaign. This conflates two distinct post-2020-election strategies and overstates what is documented about Perry's specific role.

inaccurate_statement: Federal investigators and the House January 6 committee concluded that Perry was a key figure in the multi-pronged effort to reverse the outcome
description: While the House January 6 Select Committee did seek to question Perry about his documented role in the Jeffrey Clark effort and he was referred to the House Ethics Committee, the framing that federal investigators and the committee reached a definitive 'concluded' finding overstates the record. Perry declined the committee's request and subpoena, and the ultimate disposition of the ethics referral was never confirmed. No criminal charges were ever filed against him.
